Source
Neutral status. The abc conjecture is not proved here. The project neither assumes that inter-universal Teichmüller theory is correct nor that it is wrong; a countermodel to a simplified abstraction is not a counterexample to the papers.

Statements

The statements of IUT I to IV: 369 statements in the mechanical index (numbered and lettered), 18 curated unnumbered items of a section, and 242 curated parts and proof steps. Each row is a statement of the mechanical index or a curated unnumbered item of a section; its curated parts, proof steps and fragments are listed in its record.

blocked by missing justification (BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_JUSTIFICATION): the text gives an assertion where a formalization needs a derivation; this is not a claim that the result is false.

The table is data/statements.json, the mechanical index merged with the curated records of data/curated/. Titles come from the mechanical extraction: subscripts and superscripts are often lost, and a few titles keep traces of symbols. Statement status not extracted means that the statement is not yet recorded to the standard of an extracted statement (content, hypotheses and conclusion from pages read); the record may already hold partial content. A Lean declaration is shown for a record only when the record names one; a fragment checks one step, and its parent is not counted as formalized through it.

IUT1.ThmATheorem AF± l -/Fl -Symmetries, Θ-Links, and Frobenius-/Étale-Pictures Associated to Θ±ell NF-Hodge Theaters
Record

Construction of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters from initial Θ-data, with an F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry on the additive side and an F_l^*-symmetry on the multiplicative side; the Θ-link from the Θ-pilot data of one theater to the q-pilot data of another, which induces a full poly-isomorphism of the unit portions; Frobenius-pictures and étale-pictures.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • A fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1).

Conclusion.

Summary statement of Corollaries 3.7 to 3.9, 4.12, 6.10, 6.12 and Definition 6.13 in introductory form.

Obligations.

  • Every term needs a definition: Frobenioids, D-prime-strips, Hodge theaters, poly-isomorphisms.

Ambiguities.

  • Introductory summary; the precise content is in the corollaries of §§3 to 6.

IUT1.ThmBTheorem BProfinite Conjugates of Tempered Decomposition and Inertia Groups
Record

Let k be a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field and X a hyperbolic curve over k, with tempered fundamental group Π^tp_X and étale fundamental group Π̂_X, so that Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X and Π̂_X is the profinite completion of Π^tp_X. (1) A decomposition group in Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp of X (respectively an inertia group in Π̂_X of a cusp) is contained in Π^tp_X if and only if it is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) A Π̂_X-conjugate of Π^tp_X contains a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if it is equal to Π^tp_X.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • k a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field (MLF)
  • X a hyperbolic curve over k
  • Π^tp_X the tempered fundamental group and Π̂_X the étale fundamental group of X, relative to suitable basepoints, with the natural inclusion Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X

Conclusion.

(1) For every decomposition group D ⊆ Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively inertia group I ⊆ Π̂_X of a cusp): D ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if D is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively I ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if I is an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) For every γ ∈ Π̂_X: γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} contains some decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively some inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} = Π^tp_X.

Obligations.

  • Tempered fundamental groups are not in Mathlib.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 16 says Theorem B is essentially Corollary 2.5 (with Remark 2.5.2), and that the stable reduction hypothesis of Corollary 2.5 is unnecessary by Proposition 2.4 (iii). This is a relation between the two statements, not part of Theorem B; Theorem B itself has no stable reduction hypothesis.

IUT1.Def1_1Definition 1.1
Record

Notation: Xu, Cu denote X, C with an underline in the paper; X→, C→ the arrow-decorated curves. Setting of page 37: l ≥ 5 an integer prime to 6; X a hyperbolic curve of type (1,1) over a field k of characteristic zero; Cu a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± over k whose k-core C also forms a k-core of X; Xu = Cu ×_C X, of type (1, l-tors); assumption (∗): G_k acts trivially on Δ_{Xu}^ab ⊗ Z/lZ. Pages 37 and 38 choose a nonzero cusp ε of Cu, use the decomposition group of the cusp 2ε to get a section σ : G_k → J_{Cu}, and obtain finite étale cyclic coverings X→ → Xu and C→ → Cu through cartesian diagrams, with Gal(C→/Cu) ≅ Z/lZ. Definition 1.1: a hyperbolic orbicurve over k isomorphic to the X→ (respectively C→) so constructed, for some choice of l and ε, is of type (1, l-tors→) (respectively (1, l-tors→)±).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • k a field of characteristic zero
  • l ≥ 5 an integer prime to 6 (page 37; l is not required to be prime here)
  • X a hyperbolic curve of type (1,1) over k; Cu a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± over k ([EtTh] Definition 2.1) whose k-core C is also a k-core of X; Xu = Cu ×_C X
  • assumption (∗): the natural action of G_k on Δ_{Xu}^ab ⊗ (Z/lZ) is trivial
  • ε a nonzero cusp of Cu

Conclusion.

Definition (no proof obligation): it names the types (1, l-tors→) and (1, l-tors→)± of the orbicurves X→ and C→ constructed on pages 37 and 38.

Obligations.

  • Orbicurves (stacks) are not in Mathlib.

Ambiguities.

  • The arrow decoration and the underlines were read from the rendered pages 37 to 39; Remark 1.1.1 (page 39) says the arrow denotes the archimedean ordered labels 1, 2, ... determined by the choice of ε.

IUT1.Cor1_2Corollary 1.2Characteristic Nature of Coverings
Record

Notation as in IUT1.Def1_1 (Xu, Cu underlined; X→, C→ arrow-decorated). Suppose k is an NF or an MLF. There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm that reconstructs Π_{Xu}, Π_{C→}, Π_{Cu} (respectively Π_{Cu}) together with the conjugacy classes of the decomposition groups determined by the sets of cusps {ε′, ε″}; {ε} (respectively {ε}) from Π_{X→} (respectively Π_{C→}); functoriality is with respect to isomorphisms of topological groups, and the groups are reconstructed as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X→}) (respectively Aut(Π_{C→})).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • k an NF or an MLF
  • the setting of Section 1, pages 37 and 38

Conclusion.

Existence of a functorial group-theoretic algorithm reconstructing Π_{Xu}, Π_{C→}, Π_{Cu} (respectively Π_{Cu}) and the stated conjugacy classes of decomposition groups of cusps from Π_{X→} (respectively Π_{C→}), as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X→}) (respectively Aut(Π_{C→})).

Obligations.

  • Étale fundamental groups of orbicurves; notion of group-theoretic algorithm.

Ambiguities.

  • "Algorithm" is informal; no formal model of computation is specified.

IUT1.Rem1_2_2Remark 1.2.2
Record

Corrections to the group-theoretic reconstruction of decomposition groups of cusps ([AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5, based on [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9), which contains minor inaccuracies. (i) The end of the second paragraph of the proof of [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9 is replaced: given finite étale coverings Z_i → V_i → X_i with Z_i cyclic of l-power degree over V_i, total ramification of Z_i → V_i (at some point) is group-theoretic, being equivalent to a factorization Z_i → W_i → V_i with W_i → V_i of degree l and r_{W_i} < l·r_{V_i}; this extends to pro-l cyclic coverings, so by [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.7 the inertia groups of cusps in the maximal pro-l quotient (Δ_{X_i})^(l) are the maximal subgroups corresponding to coverings satisfying the condition. (ii) The end of [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv) is replaced: the decomposition groups of cusps in H* are the maximal closed subgroups I ⊆ H* isomorphic to Z_l such that d_{χ^cyclo_G}((I^l·J)^ab ⊗ Q_l) + 1 < l·{d_{χ^cyclo_G}((I·J)^ab ⊗ Q_l) + 1} for every characteristic open subgroup J ⊆ H* with J ≠ I·J.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9 and [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5

Conclusion.

Corrected group-theoretic characterizations of cuspidal inertia groups ([AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9) and of decomposition groups of cusps ([AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv)).

Obligations.

  • The equivalence of total ramification with the factorization and the inequality r_W < l·r_V is called "easily verified" (page 40); the replacement text for [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv) is stated without proof.
  • Corollary 1.2 and Remark 3.1.2 (i) use this algorithm.

Ambiguities.

  • r_i, d_{χ^cyclo_G}, H* are notation of [AbsAnab] and [AbsTopI], not defined on page 40.

IUT1.Rem1_2_3Remark 1.2.3
Record

Related corrections to [CombGC]: (i) Galois finite étale coverings are understood to be connected. (ii) In [CombGC] Definition 1.4 (v), the cuspidal and nodal cases of purely totally ramified coverings are unnecessary, and the terminology of Definition 1.4 (vi) on descending coverings may be deleted. (iii) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.2: for G of pro-Σ PSC-type with Σ = {l} and G' → G Galois of degree a positive power of l, a cyclic G' → G is cuspidally totally ramified if and only if r(G'') < l·r(G), with G' → G'' → G the unique factorization with G'' → G of degree l; and a Π^unr_G-covering G' → G (n(G') = deg(G'/G)·n(G)) is verticially purely totally ramified if and only if i(G') = deg(G'/G)·(i(G) − 1) + 1, equivalently i(G') − n(G') = deg(G'/G)·(i(G) − n(G) − 1) + 1. (iv) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.3: cuspidal edge-like subgroups of Π_G are the maximal closed subgroups A ≅ Z_l such that for every characteristic open Π_{G'} ⊆ Π_G, with Π_{G''} = A·Π_{G'}, the cyclic covering G' → G'' is cuspidally totally ramified; for sturdy G, the set of vertices is characterized via the split injection ⊕_v M^unr_G[v] ↪ M^unr_G (image M^unr-vert) and elementary abelian quotients, as the set of nontrivial quotients M^unr-vert ↠ M^unr_G[v] ⊗ F_l. (v) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.4: for noncuspidal G, the nodal edge-like subgroups are characterized similarly with nodally totally ramified coverings, equivalent to module-wise nodal ones. (vi), (vii) Replacement texts for the second and final paragraphs of the proof of [CombGC] Theorem 1.6, deriving group-theoretic cuspidality and assertion (iii) from Remarks 1.4.3 and 1.4.2.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • G a semi-graph of anabelioids of pro-Σ PSC-type with Σ = {l} (as in [CombGC])

Conclusion.

Corrected characterizations of cuspidally and verticially purely totally ramified coverings, of cuspidal and nodal edge-like subgroups and of the set of vertices, and corrected proof steps of [CombGC] Theorem 1.6.

Obligations.

  • Each characterization is introduced with "one verifies immediately"; only the sufficiency in (iv) has a short argument (finiteness of the set of cusps gives a compatible system of cusps stabilized by A).

Ambiguities.

  • The symbols r, i, n (underlined in the paper) are the invariants of [CombGC] Remark 1.1.3; they are not defined on these pages.
  • Page 42 writes the vertex characterization for sturdy G only.

IUT1.Prop2_1Proposition 2.1Profinite Conjugates of Nontrivial Compact Subgroups
Record

In the notation of the preceding discussion, let Λ ⊆ Π^tp_G be a nontrivial compact subgroup and γ ∈ Π̂_G with γ·Λ·γ^{-1} ⊆ Π^tp_G (equivalently Λ ⊆ γ^{-1}·Π^tp_G·γ). Then γ ∈ Π^tp_G.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of the discussion preceding Proposition 2.1 (a semi-graph of anabelioids G with tempered group Π^tp_G ⊆ Π̂_G)
  • Λ ⊆ Π^tp_G a nontrivial compact subgroup
  • γ ∈ Π̂_G with γ·Λ·γ^{-1} ⊆ Π^tp_G

Conclusion.

γ ∈ Π^tp_G.

Obligations.

  • Semi-graphs of anabelioids and tempered groups are not in Mathlib. This library defines semi-graphs, connected anabelioids and semi-graphs of anabelioids (the fragments of this record and of IUT1.Prop2_2); morphisms of semi-graphs of anabelioids, the groups Pi_v, tempered groups in this setting and the statement itself are not formalized.

Ambiguities.

  • Read at the level of statements only; proofs not checked.

Parts, steps and fragments.

  • IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.anabelioid_morphism (fragment) IUT.Prerequisites.AnabelioidMorphism statement formalized not extracted
    Record

    Definitions: a morphism X to Y of connected anabelioids is an exact functor (Mathlib's ExactFunctor: preserving finite limits and finite colimits) from Y to X; it is an isomorphism when that functor is an equivalence; a basepoint is an exact functor to finite sets; the fundamental group of a basepoint is the automorphism group of its functor.

    Conclusion.

    Definitions.

    Covers.

    The Geometry of Anabelioids page 10, Definition 1.1.2 (i) and (ii).

    Not covered.

    The 2-categorical structure (Remark 1.1.2.1); recovery of G as Aut of a fundamental functor, uniqueness of fundamental functors up to isomorphism (page 9), independence of the fundamental group of the basepoint (Remark 1.1.2.2), Proposition 1.1.4.

    Pages read: IUT I pages 44 and 45 (rendered images); The Geometry of Anabelioids pages 9 to 11 (rendered images); Semi-graphs of Anabelioids pages 7, 8, 22 and 23 (rendered images); Comments on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids (text layer, all pages; pages 3 and 7 rendered)

  • IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.connected_anabelioid (fragment) IUT.Prerequisites.IsConnectedAnabelioid statement formalized not extracted
    Record

    Definition: a category is a connected anabelioid if it is equivalent to B(G) for some profinite group G (with fixed universe levels). Theorems: B(G) is a connected anabelioid; every Galois category in the sense of Mathlib is a connected anabelioid (via Mathlib's equivalence with finite continuous Aut F-sets of a fiber functor F). Definitions: a bundled connected anabelioid; the full subcategory of objects connected in the sense of Mathlib's Galois categories.

    Conclusion.

    Definitions with two theorems, proved.

    Covers.

    The Geometry of Anabelioids page 9: Definition 1.1.1 and one direction of Remark 1.1.1.1 (a Galois category is a connected anabelioid).

    Not covered.

    The converse of Remark 1.1.1.1 (a connected anabelioid is a Galois category; Mathlib has no transport of GaloisCategory along an equivalence); agreement of Mathlib's connected objects with the definition on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 7; anabelioids that are not connected; Example 1.1.3.

    Ambiguities.

    • Universes: the paper fixes one Grothendieck universe; here B(G) for G in universe u uses finite types in universe w and the predicate fixes both levels.
    • Connected objects use Mathlib's PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (not initial, no proper non-initial subobject), not the wording of Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 7 (not a coproduct of two nonempty objects).
    • The same declarations also serve IUT1.Prop2_2 (and, through the notation of IUT I Section 2, Corollary 2.5 and Theorem B, whose pages were not read for these records).

    Pages read: IUT I pages 44 and 45 (rendered images); The Geometry of Anabelioids pages 9 to 11 (rendered images); Semi-graphs of Anabelioids pages 7, 8, 22 and 23 (rendered images); Comments on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids (text layer, all pages; pages 3 and 7 rendered)

    Definition: B(G), for a profinite group G, is Mathlib's category of finite sets with the discrete topology and continuous G-action. Theorem: B(G) is a Galois category in the sense of Mathlib (proof by Mathlib).

IUT1.Prop2_2Proposition 2.2Commensurators of Decomposition Subgroups Associated to Sub-semi-graphs
Record

In the notation of the preceding discussion, Π̂_H (respectively Π^tp_H), the decomposition subgroup associated to a sub-semi-graph H, is commensurably terminal in Π̂_G (respectively in Π̂_G, hence also in Π^tp_G). In particular Π^tp_G is commensurably terminal in Π̂_G.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of the discussion preceding Proposition 2.1: a semi-graph of anabelioids G, a sub-semi-graph H, decomposition subgroups Π^tp_H ⊆ Π^tp_G and Π̂_H ⊆ Π̂_G

Conclusion.

Π̂_H is commensurably terminal in Π̂_G; Π^tp_H is commensurably terminal in Π̂_G and in Π^tp_G; Π^tp_G is commensurably terminal in Π̂_G.

Obligations.

  • Semi-graphs of anabelioids and tempered groups are not in Mathlib. This library defines semi-graphs, connected anabelioids and semi-graphs of anabelioids (the fragments of this record and of IUT1.Prop2_1); morphisms of semi-graphs of anabelioids, the groups Pi_v, tempered groups in this setting and the statement itself are not formalized.

Ambiguities.

  • Read at the level of statements only; proofs not checked.

  • IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.compactification (fragment) IUT.Prerequisites.SemiGraph.compactification statement formalized not extracted
    Record

    Definition: the compactification of a semi-graph, adding one new vertex for each branch abutting to no vertex, to which that branch then abuts; the morphism from a semi-graph to its compactification. Lemmas: in the compactification every branch abuts to a vertex; the compactification is a graph; a branch abuts to an old vertex v in the compactification exactly when it abuts to v in the original semi-graph.

    Conclusion.

    Definitions with lemmas, all proved.

    Covers.

    Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 13, the sentences defining the compactification and stating that a semi-graph forms a sub-semi-graph of its compactification.

    Not covered.

    The unique extension of morphisms to compactifications and the deformation retraction statement (page 13).

    Pages read: IUT I pages 44 and 45 (rendered images); Semi-graphs of Anabelioids pages 11 to 14 (rendered images); Comments on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids (text layer, all pages; pages 3 and 7 rendered)

  • IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph (fragment) IUT.Prerequisites.SemiGraph statement formalized not extracted
    Record

    Definition: a semi-graph is a type of vertices, a type of edges, a type of branches with a map to edges whose every fiber has exactly two elements, and a coincidence map sending each branch to the vertex it abuts to or to none. Further definitions: an edge abuts to a vertex; verticial cardinality; graphs; finite and countable semi-graphs; components; an edge joins two vertices; closed, open and isolated edges; coverticial edges; locally finite and untangled semi-graphs; the incidence graph and connectedness through it; joints. Lemmas: the branches of an edge form a finite type; verticial cardinality is at most two; in a graph every edge abuts to a vertex.

    Conclusion.

    Definitions with elementary lemmas, all proved.

    Covers.

    Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 11 (definition of a semi-graph, verticial portion and cardinality, graphs, branches, finite and countable, components, joins, abuts to), pages 12 and 13 (closed, open, isolated and coverticial edges; locally finite, untangled, joint). The semi-graph underlying the semi-graph of anabelioids of IUT I page 44.

    Not covered.

    The topological space of a semi-graph and the proof that connectedness of the incidence graph is its connectedness; trees; subjoints. Of Proposition 2.2: PSC-type, fundamental groups, decomposition subgroups, commensurable terminality.

    Ambiguities.

    • An edge of the page is a set of exactly two branches (not at most two); here the branches form one type with a map to edges whose fibers have exactly two elements, a reencoding of the same data.
    • The page defines connectedness through the associated topological space, which is not constructed; connectedness is taken as connectedness (with nonemptiness) of the incidence graph of vertices and edges.
    • The same declarations also serve IUT1.Prop2_1 (and, through the notation of IUT I Section 2, Corollary 2.5 and Theorem B, whose pages were not read for these records).

    Pages read: IUT I pages 44 and 45 (rendered images); Semi-graphs of Anabelioids pages 11 to 14 (rendered images); Comments on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids (text layer, all pages; pages 3 and 7 rendered)

IUT1.Cor2_3Corollary 2.3Subgroups of Tempered Fundamental Groups Associated to Sub-semi-graphs
Record

Setting (pages 46, 47): k an MLF with residue characteristic p, X a hyperbolic curve over k with stable reduction over O_k; Π^tp_X, Δ^tp_X the Σ̂-tempered quotients of the tempered fundamental groups; Δ̂_X the pro-Σ̂ fundamental group of X_k̄, Π̂_X the corresponding quotient; inclusions Π^tp_X ↪ Π̂_X, Δ^tp_X ↪ Δ̂_X. Assume p ∉ Σ, G is the pro-Σ semi-graph of anabelioids of the special fiber of the stable model 𝒳, and the sub-semi-graph H ⊆ G is stabilized by G_k; so Δ^tp_X ↠ Π^tp_G and Δ̂_X ↠ Π̂_G. Then: (i) Δ^tp_{X,H} = Δ^tp_X ×_{Π^tp_G} Π^tp_H ⊆ Δ^tp_X and Δ̂_{X,H} = Δ̂_X ×_{Π̂_G} Π̂_H ⊆ Δ̂_X are commensurably terminal, so the outer G_k-actions on Δ^tp_X, Δ̂_X induce outer actions on Δ^tp_{X,H}, Δ̂_{X,H}. (ii) The closure of Δ^tp_{X,H} in Δ̂_X is Δ̂_{X,H}. (iii) If (a) Σ̂ contains a prime l ∉ Σ ∪ {p}, or (b) Σ̂ = Primes, then Δ̂_{X,H} is slim, and there are exact sequences of center-free groups 1 → Δ^tp_{X,H} → Π^tp_{X,H} → G_k → 1 and 1 → Δ̂_{X,H} → Π̂_{X,H} → G_k → 1, with Π^tp_{X,H}, Π̂_{X,H} defined so as to make them exact. (iv) Under (iii)'s hypothesis, the images of Π^tp_{X,H} ↪ Π^tp_X and Π̂_{X,H} ↪ Π̂_X are commensurably terminal. (v) Δ̂_{X,H} ∩ Δ^tp_X = Δ^tp_{X,H} in Δ̂_X. (vi) For an inertia group I_x ⊆ Δ^tp_X (respectively Δ̂_X) of a cusp x of X, with ξ the cusp of 𝒳 corresponding to x: I_x lies in a Δ^tp_X- (respectively Δ̂_X-) conjugate of Δ^tp_{X,H} (respectively Δ̂_{X,H}) if and only if ξ meets an irreducible component of the special fiber contained in H.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • k an MLF of residue characteristic p; X a hyperbolic curve over k with stable reduction over O_k
  • Σ ⊆ Σ̂ nonempty sets of primes; G a semi-graph of anabelioids of pro-Σ PSC-type; H the semi-graph of anabelioids of a connected sub-semi-graph ℍ ⊆ 𝔾 (page 44)
  • Σ ⊆ Σ̂ sets of primes with p ∉ Σ (the notation of the discussion of Proposition 2.1 and of pages 46 and 47)
  • G the pro-Σ semi-graph of anabelioids of the special fiber of the stable model 𝒳; H ⊆ G a sub-semi-graph stabilized by G_k
  • (iii), (iv): Σ̂ contains a prime l ∉ Σ ∪ {p}, or Σ̂ = Primes

Conclusion.

(i) Δ^tp_{X,H} ⊆ Δ^tp_X and Δ̂_{X,H} ⊆ Δ̂_X are commensurably terminal, with induced outer G_k-actions. (ii) The closure of Δ^tp_{X,H} in Δ̂X is Δ̂{X,H}. (iii) Under (a) or (b), Δ̂{X,H} is slim and the two displayed sequences are exact sequences of center-free groups. (iv) Under the same hypothesis, Π^tp{X,H} and Π̂_{X,H} have commensurably terminal images in Π^tp_X, Π̂X. (v) Δ̂{X,H} ∩ Δ^tp_X = Δ^tp_{X,H}. (vi) I_x lies in a conjugate of Δ^tp_{X,H} (respectively Δ̂_{X,H}) if and only if ξ meets an irreducible component of the special fiber contained in H.

Obligations.

  • (i) follows from Proposition 2.2. (ii) from an elementary density observation about kernels of surjections of finitely generated free groups (proved on page 48 using a section of G ↠ F). (iii) has two proofs: an elementary one under (a), and one under (b) using [Tama2] Theorem 0.2 (v); both use [AbsTopII] Proposition 1.3 (iv) or [NodNon] Proposition 3.9 (i) and [Config] Proposition 1.4. (iv) from (i) and (iii). (v) reduces to F̂ ∩ G = F for finitely generated subgroups F of a free group G, via [SemiAnbd] Corollary 1.6 (ii). (vi) "by a similar argument" to [CombGC] Proposition 1.5 (i).
  • Tempered fundamental groups and semi-graphs of anabelioids are not in Mathlib; the density observation of (ii) and the claim F̂ ∩ G = F for a retract F of G are elementary profinite group theory.

Ambiguities.

  • Π^tp_{X,H}, Π̂_{X,H} in (iii) are defined only implicitly, as the groups that make the displayed sequences exact (page 47).
  • In the proof of (iii), the symbol F is used both for a quotient free group (page 48) and for a pro-Σ pro-cyclic subgroup (page 49).

Corollary 2.5 may be regarded as a very weak version of the Section Conjecture: certain sections of the tempered fundamental group (those arising from geometric sections of the profinite fundamental group) are geometric as sections of the tempered fundamental group (compare [SemiAnbd] Remark 6.9.1). The classification of maximal compact subgroups of tempered fundamental groups ([SemiAnbd] Theorem 3.7 (iv), Theorem 5.4 (ii); Remark 2.5.3 (ii), (E5), (E7)), or the elementary fact that any finite group acting on a tree without inversion fixes a vertex ([SemiAnbd] Lemma 1.8 (ii)), may be viewed as a combinatorial version of the Section Conjecture.

Conclusion.

Interpretation of Corollary 2.5; no new assertion beyond the cited fixed-point fact for finite groups acting on trees without inversion.

Ambiguities.

  • "A sort of version of the Section Conjecture" is an analogy, not a statement.

IUT1.Rem2_5_3Remark 2.5.3
Record

Corrections to [SemiAnbd]. (i) Terminology: (T1) a tempered group is Galois-countable if its topology has a countable basis, extended to (quasi-)temperoids; (T2) a semi-graph of anabelioids G is Galois-countable if countable with a countable collection of finite étale coverings G_i → G such that every finite étale covering becomes split over some G_i componentwise; (T3) G is strictly coherent if coherent ([SemiAnbd] Definition 2.3 (iii)) with component groups generated by N elements for a fixed N (finite coherent implies strictly coherent). (T4) Strictly coherent countable semi-graphs are Galois-countable. (T5), (T6) Under Galois-countability, the tempered fundamental groups of [SemiAnbd] Remark 3.2.1 and before Proposition 3.6 are well defined and Galois-countable; countability makes the nonabelian R^1 lim obstruction to compatible basepoints vanish. (ii) Effects (E1) to (E9): subquotients of absolute Galois groups of countable fields, and tame arithmetic fundamental groups over such fields ([AbsTopI] Proposition 2.2), are Galois-countable; no effect on [SemiAnbd] Examples 2.10, 3.10, 5.6, §§1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and the Appendix; Galois-countability must be assumed in [SemiAnbd] 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9 and throughout [QuCnf], [FrdII]; no effect elsewhere. (iii) The assertion in the second display of [SemiAnbd] Remark 2.4.2 is false as stated (Dehn twists of [SemiAnbd] Example 2.10 give a counterexample); it is replaced by: the isomorphism classes of the φ_v determine those of each φ_e and each φ_b up to composition with an automorphism of G_e → H_f → H_w arising from an automorphism of G_e → H_f; the subsequent discussion also needs every edge to abut to at least one vertex. (iv) In the proof of [SemiAnbd] Proposition 3.2, "is Galois" should read "is a countable coproduct of Galois objects". (v) Two wording corrections to [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.5 (ii). (vi) In [SemiAnbd] Definition 5.1 (i), conditions (c), (d) are strengthened to (c^new) (trivial action of H on G and continuity of H → Aut(G[c]) for the profinite topology from (O1), (O2)) and (d^new) (a finite set C* of components with compatible isomorphisms G[c] ⥲ G[c*]); by [NS] Theorem 1.1 (c) and (c^new) hold automatically since H is topologically finitely generated; the strengthening has no effect on the rest of [SemiAnbd].

Conclusion.

Corrections to [SemiAnbd] and [QuCnf], [FrdII]: Galois-countability hypotheses must be added in the listed places; one assertion of [SemiAnbd] Remark 2.4.2 is false and is replaced; Definition 5.1 (i) is strengthened. The text asserts that none of this affects IUT I.

Obligations.

  • (T4), (T5), (T6), (O1), (O2): "one verifies immediately"; no proofs given.
  • A formalization of tempered fundamental groups following [SemiAnbd] must include the Galois-countability hypothesis and the modified Definition 5.1 (i).
  • The claims of "no effect" on the remaining results are not argued beyond the listed reasons.

Ambiguities.

  • The remark records errors in a cited source; the corrected statements of [SemiAnbd] are what IUT I §2 relies on (Proposition 2.4 cites Remark 2.5.3 (ii), (E5), (E7)).

IUT1.Thm2_6Theorem 2.6Profinite Conjugates of Discrete Subgroups
Record

Let F be a group containing a finite index subgroup G that is a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable topological surface of genus ≥ 2, and H ⊆ F an infinite subgroup. Regard H, G ⊆ F ⊆ F̂ (F is residually finite), F̂ the profinite completion. Let γ ∈ F̂ with γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ F. Write H_G = H ∩ G. Then γ ∈ F·N_F̂(H_G), that is, γ·H_G·γ^{-1} = δ·H_G·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ F. If moreover H_G is nonabelian, then γ ∈ F.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • G ⊆ F of finite index, G free of finite rank or orientable surface group of genus ≥ 2
  • H ⊆ F infinite
  • γ ∈ F̂ with γHγ^{-1} ⊆ F

Implicit hypotheses.

  • F residually finite, cited from [Config] Proposition 7.1 (ii).

Conclusion.

γ ∈ F·N_F̂(H_G), the normalizer in F̂ of H_G itself (not of its closure); equivalently γ·H_G·γ^{-1} = δ·H_G·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ F. If H_G is nonabelian, γ ∈ F.

Obligations.

  • Statable in Lean: Mathlib has free groups and profinite completion of groups in some form; surface groups would need a definition. Not attempted.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 56 (rendered) shows N_F̂(H_G) with H_G undecorated; the closure Ĥ_G appears only in the proof on page 57, in N_Ĝ(H_G) = Ĥ_G.

IUT1.Lem2_7Lemma 2.7Well-known Properties of Free Groups and Orientable Surface Groups
Record

Let G be as in Theorem 2.6 (free of finite rank, or an orientable surface group of genus ≥ 2) and Ĝ its profinite completion. (i) Any subgroup of G generated by two elements is free. (ii) For x ∈ G, x ≠ 1, there is a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G with x ∈ G_1 and x of nontrivial image in G_1^ab. (iii) For noncommuting x, y ∈ G there are a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G and n ≥ 1 with x^n, y^n ∈ G_1 whose images in G_1^ab generate a free abelian subgroup of rank two. (iv) Every abelian subgroup of G is cyclic. (v) If T̂ ⊆ Ĝ is a closed subgroup and there is a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing an isomorphism T̂ ≅ Ẑ, then T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ. (vi) If G is nonabelian and N̂ = Ker(Ĝ ↠ Ĝ^ab), the centralizer Z_Ĝ(N̂) is trivial. (vii) In the notation of (vi), an automorphism of the profinite group Ĝ that preserves N̂ and restricts to the identity on N̂ is the identity.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • G a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable surface of genus ≥ 2 (as in Theorem 2.6)
  • Ĝ the profinite completion of G
  • (ii): x ∈ G, x ≠ 1
  • (iii): x, y ∈ G noncommuting
  • (v): T̂ ⊆ Ĝ closed, with a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing T̂ ≅ Ẑ
  • (vi), (vii): G nonabelian; (vii): α an automorphism of Ĝ preserving N̂ with α|_N̂ = id

Conclusion.

(i) two-generated subgroups are free; (ii) separation of x ≠ 1 in the abelianization of a finite index subgroup; (iii) x^n, y^n span a rank two free abelian subgroup of G_1^ab; (iv) abelian subgroups are cyclic; (v) T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ; (vi) Z_Ĝ(N̂) = {1}; (vii) α = id.

Obligations.

  • Several parts are classical facts whose Mathlib coverage was not checked; surface groups are not defined in Mathlib.

IUT1.Rem3_1_2Remark 3.1.2
Record

(i) The open subgroup Π_{X_K} ⊆ Π_{C_K} (arrow-decorated X_K, C_K) can be constructed group-theoretically from the topological group Π_{C_K}. (ii) Convention, the Θ-approach: the reconstruction algorithm of [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 is applied not to Π_{C_K} but to the open subgroup Π_{X_K}, reconstructing the function field of X_K with its natural action of Gal(X_K/C_K) ≅ Π_{C_K}/Π_{X_K}; similarly at v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non (respectively V^bad) to Π_{C_v} or, via Corollary 1.2, Π_{X_v}, Π_{C_v} with arrow decorations (respectively to Π^tp_{C_v} or, via [EtTh] Proposition 2.4, Π^tp of the double-underlined X_v). All uses of [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 and its consequences in the series are via the Θ-approach. (iii) From the tautological extension 1 → Δ_Θ → Δ^Θ_X → Δ^ell_X → 1 of [EtTh] §2, with Δ_Θ = [Δ_X, Δ_X]/[Δ_X, [Δ_X, Δ_X]], Δ^Θ_X = Δ_X/[Δ_X, [Δ_X, Δ_X]], Δ^ell_X = Δ^ab_X, its class in H^2(Δ^ell_X, Δ_Θ) gives a tautological isomorphism M_X ⥲ Δ_Θ (M_X ≅ Hom(H^2(Δ^ell_X, Ẑ), Ẑ) by [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 (b)), and hence M_{Xu} ⥲ (l·Δ_Θ) since [Δ_X : Δ_{Xu}] = l (Xu the underlined X). This isomorphism is a characteristic subquotient of Π_{C_{F_mod}}, with a natural conjugation action; the significance of the Θ-approach lies in this isomorphism, used in [IUTchII] at bad v, relating the cyclotome M_X to (l·Δ_Θ), central in the cyclotomic rigidity of [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (i). (iv) For large l, the role of the covering X in the Θ-approach recalls that of the universal covering of a complex elliptic curve by C in [AbsTopIII] §2.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in Definition 3.1, with the coverings X_K, C_K of Definition 3.1 (f)

Conclusion.

(i) Π_{X_K} ⊆ Π_{C_K} is group-theoretic in Π_{C_K}. (ii) Convention: the Θ-approach to [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9. (iii) The tautological isomorphisms M_X ⥲ Δ_Θ and M_{Xu} ⥲ (l·Δ_Θ). (iv) Heuristic analogy.

Obligations.

  • (i): the text says it "follows immediately" from the construction of the coverings at the beginning of [EtTh] §2 and from the "easily verified fact" that the image of each decomposition group of a nonzero cusp coincides with the image of Π_{X_K} in Π_{C_K}/Δ_X (underlined).
  • (iii): the identification of M_X with Hom(H^2(Δ^ell_X, Ẑ), Ẑ) is cited from [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 (b).

IUT1.Rem3_1_5Remark 3.1.5
Record

Since the 3-torsion points of E_F are rational over F and F is Galois over F_mod (Definition 3.1 (b)), K is Galois over F_mod (citing [IUTchIV] Proposition 1.8 (iv)). Define the algebraic stack S_mod = Spec(O_K)//Gal(K/F_mod) (stack-theoretic quotient). A finite extension L ⊆ F̄ of F_mod gives, by integral closure of S_mod in L, a stack S_{mod,L}; arithmetic line bundles on such stacks give, for any finite quotient Gal(F̄/F_mod) ↠ Q, a Frobenioid by the easily verified stack-theoretic version of [FrdI] Example 6.3, for which an analogue of [FrdI] Theorem 6.4 holds. After passing to the perfection or the realification these become naturally isomorphic to the non-stack-theoretic versions.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • initial Θ-data as in Definition 3.1

Conclusion.

(a) K/F_mod is Galois. (b) Definition of S_mod and S_{mod,L} and of stack-theoretic Frobenioids; an analogue of [FrdI] Theorem 6.4 holds for them. (c) Their perfections and realifications are naturally isomorphic to the non-stack-theoretic versions.

Obligations.

  • (a) rests on [IUTchIV] Proposition 1.8 (iv), which was not read for this record.
  • (b), (c): "one verifies immediately" that the analogue of [FrdI] Theorem 6.4 holds; no argument is given.

Ambiguities.

  • Depends on IUT IV Proposition 1.8 (iv), not read for this record.

IUT1.Rem3_1_7Remark 3.1.7
Record

Special rational functions on the model of C_F. (i) The model C_{F_mod} and κ-coric rational functions. (ii) ∞κ-coric and ∞κ×-coric functions and their pseudo-monoids. (iii) κ-solvable functions, the subgroup Gal(K/F(μ_l)) and a linear disjointness. (iv) κ-sol-automorphisms and the center-freeness of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • initial Θ-data as in Definition 3.1

Conclusion.

(i) C_{F_mod} exists uniquely and κ-coric functions are defined, with their elementary consequences. (ii) A κ-coric function of degree 4 exists; every element of L (respectively L^□) is a value of a κ-coric function at a non-critical point; ∞κ- and ∞κ×-coric functions form divisible cyclotomic pseudo-monoids. (iii) L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) are linearly disjoint over F(μ_l)·L_C. (iv) Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free, so the conjugation square to Aut^{κ-sol}, Out^{κ-sol} is cartesian.

Obligations.

  • See the child records.

Parts, steps and fragments.

  • IUT1.Rem3_1_7.i (part or step) extracted blocked by missing justification
    Record

    By the definition of F_mod and K-coricity of C_K, C_F has a model C_{F_mod} over F_mod, unique up to unique isomorphism; C_v is its base change to (F_mod)_v. Let L be F_mod or (F_mod)_v, C_L the model over L, L̄_C an algebraic closure of the function field L_C, L̄ the induced algebraic closure of L. The coarse space |C_L| is isomorphic to the affine line over L. A closed point of a proper smooth curve given by a finite subextension of L̄_C is critical if it maps to a point of |C_L|^cpt arising from a 2-torsion point of E_F, and strictly critical if moreover it does not map to the point arising from the unique cusp of C_L. A rational function f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if: whenever f ∉ L, over L̄ f has precisely one pole and at least two distinct zeroes; its divisor of zeroes and poles is defined over a number field and avoids the critical points; f restricts to a root of unity at every strictly critical point of |C_L|^cpt.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • initial Θ-data as in Definition 3.1
    • L = F_mod or L = (F_mod)_v for some v ∈ V_mod

    Conclusion.

    Existence and uniqueness of the model C_{F_mod}; |C_L| ≅ A^1_L; definition of critical and strictly critical points and of κ-coric functions. Consequences stated: for f ∉ L, f and f^{-1} are never both κ-coric; if c ∈ L and both f and c·f are κ-coric, then c is a root of unity; restriction to strictly critical points gives a splitting, up to roots of unity, of nonzero constant multiples of κ-coric functions into κ-coric functions times L^×.

    Obligations.

    • Uniqueness of the model and |C_L| ≅ A^1_L are said to follow immediately ("one verifies immediately") from the definitions.
    • The consequences about f^{-1} and c·f are direct from the definition (one pole; values at strictly critical points) and could be checked once the objects are defined.

    Ambiguities.

    • Critical points are defined on proper smooth curves of finite subextensions of L̄_C, but the root-of-unity condition is stated on |C_L|^cpt itself (page 67).

    Pages read: 66 to 67 (rendered images)

  • IUT1.Rem3_1_7.ii (part or step) extracted blocked by missing justification
    Record

    Let L^□ be an intermediate field between L and L̄ that is solvably closed ([GlSol] Definition 1 (i)). Since |C_L|^cpt has precisely 4 critical points, there is a κ-coric f_sol ∈ L_C of degree 4. Hence every element of L (respectively L^□) is a value of some κ-coric function on C_L at some non-critical L- (respectively L^□-) valued point (elementary theory of polynomials on the affine line with Hensel's lemma, as in the proof of [AbsTopII] Lemma 2.1; respectively f_sol and solvability of S_4). With U_L̄ = L̄^× if L = F_mod and the units of L̄ if L = (F_mod)_v: f ∈ L̄_C is ∞κ-coric if some power f^n is a κ-coric element of L_C, and ∞κ×-coric if c·f is ∞κ-coric for some c ∈ U_L̄; f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if and only if it is ∞κ-coric. An ∞κ×-coric f is ∞κ-coric if and only if it restricts to a root of unity at some (equivalently every) strictly critical point. Multiplication gives pseudo-monoid structures on κ-, ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric functions; the latter two are divisible and cyclotomic.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.i
    • L^□ a solvably closed intermediate field between L and L̄

    Conclusion.

    Existence of a degree-4 κ-coric f_sol; every element of L, respectively L^□, is a value of a κ-coric function at a non-critical point; definitions of ∞κ- and ∞κ×-coric functions; the characterization of ∞κ-coric among ∞κ×-coric functions; the pseudo-monoid structures.

    Obligations.

    • Each claim is said to "follow immediately" or to be verified immediately; the existence of f_sol and the value statements need the elementary theory of polynomials on the affine line, Hensel's lemma, and solvability of S_4 (in Mathlib).
    • The claim that |C_L|^cpt has precisely 4 critical points rests on E_F having four 2-torsion points mapping to distinct points of the coarse space.

    Ambiguities.

    • Page 67 says f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if and only if it is ∞κ-coric, although the definition of ∞κ-coric is for f ∈ L̄_C; the statement is read as concerning f ∈ L_C.

    Record

    Assume L = F_mod, L̄ = F̄. f ∈ L̄_C is κ-solvable if it is an F^×_sol-multiple of a ∞κ-coric element of L̄_C; equivalently some power f^n is a ∞κ×-coric element of F_sol·L_C. Let F(μ_l) ⊆ K be generated by the l-th roots of unity, L_C(κ-sol) ⊆ L̄_C generated by κ-solvable elements, L_C(C_K) ⊆ L̄_C generated over L_C by the images of the F(μ_l)·L_C-linear embeddings of the function field of C_K. Since F/F_mod is Galois of degree prime to l (Definition 3.1 (b)), Gal(K/F(μ_l)) ⊆ Gal(K/F_mod) is normal and is the unique subgroup abstractly isomorphic to SL_2(F_l) (Remark 3.1.5; [GenEll] Lemma 3.1 (i)). Since SL_2(F_l) is perfect ([GenEll] Lemma 3.1 (ii)), and by the definition of ∞κ×-coric (zeroes and poles avoid critical points), L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) are linearly disjoint over F(μ_l)·L_C inside L̄_C. Hence Gal(L_C(C_K)/F(μ_l)·L_C) ⥲ Gal(L_C(C_K)·L_C(κ-sol)/F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol)) naturally.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.ii
    • L = F_mod and L̄ = F̄

    Conclusion.

    Characterization of κ-solvable elements; Gal(K/F(μ_l)) is normal in Gal(K/F_mod) and the unique subgroup isomorphic to SL_2(F_l); linear disjointness of L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) over F(μ_l)·L_C; the natural isomorphism of Galois groups.

    Obligations.

    • The linear disjointness is said to "follow immediately" from perfectness of SL_2(F_l) and the definition of ∞κ×-coric; the argument (an abelian or solvable quotient of a perfect group is trivial) must be written out, including why L_C(κ-sol) is a solvable extension.
    • The SL_2(F_l) characterization rests on [GenEll] Lemma 3.1 and on Definition 3.1 (b), (c).

  • IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iv (part or step) extracted blocked by external theorem
    Record

    With the exact sequence 1 → Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) → Gal(L̄_C/L_C) → Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C) → 1, call a subgroup of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) κ-sol-open if it is the intersection with it of a normal open subgroup of Gal(L̄_C/L_C). The groups Aut^{κ-sol} ⊆ Aut and Out^{κ-sol} ⊆ Out of (outer) automorphisms of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) preserving each κ-sol-open subgroup admit compatible homomorphisms to Aut(Q), Out(Q) for each quotient by a κ-sol-open subgroup; their kernels define profinite topologies, for which the conjugation diagram Gal(L̄_C/L_C) → Aut^{κ-sol}, Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C) → Out^{κ-sol} is a commutative diagram of continuous homomorphisms. Moreover Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free, so the diagram is cartesian.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iii

    Conclusion.

    Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free; hence the commutative square formed by Gal(L̄_C/L_C), Aut^{κ-sol}, Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C), Out^{κ-sol} is cartesian.

    Obligations.

    • Proof sketch (page 69): Gal(F̄·L_C(κ-sol)/F̄·L_C) is abelian; by Lemma 2.7 (vi), (vii) applied to the geometric fundamental groups of genus zero affine hyperbolic curves with function field L_C, a central element α acts trivially on such a (center-free) geometric fundamental group; by the Galois injectivity of [NodNon] Theorem C (a case known to Belyi), α is the identity.
    • That center-freeness implies the square is cartesian is elementary group theory and could be checked separately.

So "F^Θ_v up to the l·Z indeterminacy in Θ_v" (Example 3.2 (ii)) may be read as the system of split Frobenioids F^{Θ^α}_v, α ∈ Aut_{D_v}(Ÿ_v), identified by these isomorphisms. (ii) If A ∈ Ob(D_v) is in the image of D^Θ_v ⊆ (D_v)_{Ÿ_v} → D_v and ψ : B → T_A is a linear morphism in the Frobenioid F_v (double underline), then ψ induces an injective homomorphism O^×(T^÷_A) ↪ O^×(B^÷) ([FrdI] Proposition 1.11 (iv)), so sections of O^▷_{C^Θ_v}(−) may be pulled back to B, as is useful for roots of Θ_v ([EtTh] §5).

IUT1.Rem3_2_4Remark 3.2.4
Record

Corrections to the tempered Frobenioids of [EtTh] §§3, 4. Let ℨ^log_∞ be the universal combinatorial covering of the formal log scheme of a stable log curve with split special fiber over the integers of a finite extension of an MLF of residue characteristic p, with generic fiber Z^log. (i) For a nonzero meromorphic function f on ℨ^log_∞ consider: (a) for every N ≥ 1, f has an N-th root over some tempered covering of Z^log; (b) the same for N prime to p; (c) the divisor of zeroes and poles of f is a log-divisor. Then (a) ⇒ (b) is immediate, (b) ⇒ (c) by ramification divisors, and (c) ⇒ (b) via admissible coverings ([PrfGC] §2, §8): a finite log étale covering Y^log → Z^log whose pull-back annihilates ramification over cusps and special fiber (R1) and splits extensions of function fields of irreducible components (R2), so that f has an N-th root over the universal combinatorial covering of Y^log. Hence (a) ⇒ (b) ⇔ (c); whether (c) implies (a) is stated to be unclear to the author. (ii) The theta function of [EtTh] satisfies (a) ([EtTh] §1, Proposition 1.3). (iii) [EtTh] Definition 3.1 (ii) defines log-meromorphic by (c), but the proof of [EtTh] Proposition 4.2 (iii) needs (a). (iv) Remedies: (A) redefine log-meromorphic by (a) (perhaps "tempered-meromorphic"), or (B) require in [EtTh] Definition 4.1 (i) the category-theoretic condition (d): for every N ≥ 1 there is a linear morphism A' → A in C with the pull-back of f admitting an N-th root. (v) (A) changes the definition of tempered Frobenioid slightly; (B) only reduces the range of applicability of [EtTh] §4 (irrelevant for the theta functions); the series adopts (A). (vi) Three textual modifications to [EtTh] Example 3.9 (i), (ii) concerning Φ^ell_W: Y^log of genus 1 with precisely one cusp or two cusps differing by 2-torsion; the lower arrow written Ẋ^log → Ċ^log; unramified over the cusps and the generic points of the special fibers, with tempered admissible coverings.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of [EtTh] §3: ℨ^log_∞, Z^log as above
  • f a nonzero meromorphic function on ℨ^log_∞

Conclusion.

(a) ⇒ (b) ⇔ (c) for meromorphic functions on ℨ^log_∞, with (c) ⇒ (a) left open; the definition of tempered Frobenioid used in the series is that of approach (A), with log-meromorphic meaning condition (a).

Obligations.

  • (b) ⇔ (c) is argued via admissible coverings ([PrfGC]); the open question (c) ⇒ (a) is stated explicitly as unresolved.
  • A formalization of tempered Frobenioids must use definition (A), which differs from [EtTh] as published.

Ambiguities.

  • The remark changes the definition of a cited object; any use of [EtTh] results in the series must be read with this modification (page 77).
  • The universal combinatorial covering is written with a fraktur Z (ℨ^log_∞) on page 75, checked on a 220 dpi render.

    Integral monoids are of characteristic type (erratum 30), so pre-divisorial is equivalent to integral and saturated. The additive monoids N, Q>=0 and R>=0 are divisorial; Q>=0 and R>=0 are perfect and N is not; N is torsion-free and ZMod 2 is not; Z is group-like and not sharp; WithTop N is not integral; WithTop Z is not of characteristic type; the constant functor with value N on Discrete PUnit is a divisorial monoid on that category. General criteria: a cancellative monoid is integral; every element of M^gp is a difference of images; a commutative group is saturated; a canonically ordered monoid is sharp; a linearly and canonically ordered cancellative monoid is saturated and divisorial.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • For isCharacteristicTypeMonoid_of_isIntegralMonoid: M a commutative monoid that is integral. The example theorems have no hypotheses.

    The stated memberships and non-memberships in the monoid classes.

The Kummer structure κ_v : O^▷(C_v) ↪ A_{D_v} of Example 3.4 (i) may be viewed as follows. In the terminology of [AbsTopIII] Definition 2.1 (i), (iv), the CAF structure on Ā_{D_v} determines, by pull-back via κ_v, an Aut-holomorphic structure on the groupification O^▷(C_v)^gp together with a tautological co-holomorphicization O^▷(C_v)^gp → A_{D_v}. Conversely, from this Aut-holomorphic structure and co-holomorphicization one recovers the inclusion of topological monoids κ_v (by [AbsTopIII] Corollary 2.3 and the fact that every holomorphic automorphism of C^× preserving the elements of norm ≤ 1 is the identity). Thus κ_v is equivalent to the pair (Aut-holomorphic structure, co-holomorphicization). The co-holomorphicization, unlike the inclusion of monoids, is compatible with the logarithm of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 4.5.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • v ∈ V^arc and the notation of Example 3.4 (i)

Conclusion.

The Kummer structure κ_v is equivalent to the Aut-holomorphic structure on O^▷(C_v)^gp together with the co-holomorphicization O^▷(C_v)^gp → A_{D_v}; the co-holomorphicization is compatible with the logarithm of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 4.5.

Obligations.

  • The recovery of κ_v "follows immediately" from [AbsTopIII] Corollary 2.3 and the elementary fact about holomorphic automorphisms of C^× (which preserve the closed unit disc only if they are the identity); the latter is classical and could be checked separately.
  • The compatibility with the logarithm is described as a rough summary of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 4.5.

IUT1.Rem3_9_3Remark 3.9.3
Record

(i) The mono-analytic core {D^⊢_v}_{v∈V} may be thought of as a fixed underlying real-analytic surface on which holomorphic structures are imposed, and the Frobenius-picture as a global arithmetic analogue of a Teichmüller geodesic, or of the canonical liftings of p-adic Teichmüller theory. (ii) Along a Teichmüller geodesic one real dimension is dilated and one fixed; in the Frobenius-picture of Corollary 3.8 the local units O^× correspond to the fixed dimension and the local value groups undergo Θ-dilations; treating them independently uses the characteristic splittings of the split Frobenioids of Examples 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, which at bad v correspond to the constant multiple rigidity of the étale theta function. (iii) In complex Teichmüller theory the two real dimensions are the real and imaginary parts of the coordinate obtained by locally integrating the square root of a square differential, whose only indeterminacy, multiplication by −1, preserves real and imaginary parts; for n ≥ 3, integrating n-th roots of sections of the n-th tensor power of differentials gives an indeterminacy by n-th roots of unity that confuses real and imaginary parts. (iv) Linear movement along the oriented graph Γ of Corollary 3.8 corresponds to the linear flow along a Teichmüller geodesic, and the rotation of ⊞ and ⊠ of [IUTchIII] to rotations about a fixed point, or in the p-adic analogy to Frobenius in positive characteristic.

Conclusion.

Heuristic analogy between the Frobenius-picture and Teichmüller geodesics; the only mathematical observation is the classical one in (iii) that multiplication by −1 preserves real and imaginary parts while multiplication by an n-th root of unity, n ≥ 3, does not.

Ambiguities.

  • Heuristic remark; no claim to formalize beyond the elementary observation in (iii).

Let †𝔇 = {†D_v}_{v∈V} be a D-prime-strip (𝔇 fraktur in the paper). For any v, w ∈ V there are bijections LabCusp(†D_v) ⥲ LabCusp(†D_w) uniquely determined by being compatible with the assignments †η_v ↦ †η_w (Definition 4.1 (ii)) and with the F_l^*-torsor structures on both sides; they are preserved by arbitrary isomorphisms of D-prime-strips. Identifying the LabCusp(†D_v) via these bijections defines LabCusp(†𝔇), which carries a canonical element (from the †η_v) and a natural F_l^*-torsor structure, hence a natural bijection LabCusp(†𝔇) ⥲ F_l^* preserved by isomorphisms of D-prime-strips.

Explicit hypotheses.

Conclusion.

Existence and uniqueness of the compatible bijections LabCusp(†D_v) ⥲ LabCusp(†D_w), their invariance under isomorphisms of D-prime-strips, and the natural bijection LabCusp(†𝔇) ⥲ F_l^* determined by the canonical element and the torsor structure.

(i) Assume F = F_mod. Spec(K) → Spec(F) has no section; this is related to the nonexistence of a global multiplicative subspace ([HASurII] Remark 3.7), viewed as the principal obstruction to applying the scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory of [HASurI], [HASurII] to diophantine geometry. Via the arrows φ^NF_j of Example 4.3 (iv), the D-prime-strips may be seen as arithmetic collections of local analytic (local-analytic) sections of Spec(K) → Spec(F) (Fig. 4.1), each yielding an arithmetic local-analytic global multiplicative subspace and global canonical generator. (ii) Their failure to be globally arithmetically holomorphic is seen from three related viewpoints: (a) they do not extend to ring homomorphisms K → F; (b) an identification of a prime v of F with a prime v' of K does not extend to an isomorphism of prime decomposition trees ([NSW] Theorem 12.2.5), compared with [IUTchIV] §3 and the membership relation; (c) the isomorphisms of local absolute Galois groups do not extend to a section G_F ↠ G_K of the inclusion G_K ↪ G_F. By the Neukirch-Uchida theorem (a) and (c) are essentially equivalent, and (b) is closely related. (iii) Understanding this failure is a central theme of the series.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • F = F_mod (assumed for simplicity, page 101)

Conclusion.

Interpretive remark; the mathematical assertions are that Spec(K) → Spec(F) has no section (K ≠ F) and the facts (a), (b), (c) with the essential equivalence of (a) and (c) via Neukirch-Uchida.

Ambiguities.

  • "Essentially equivalent" and "closely related" (page 102) are not made precise.

The incompatibility of the arithmetic local-analytic sections with global prime distributions and global Galois groups is the technical obstacle that requires, in [IUTchIII], the absolute p-adic mono-anabelian geometry of [AbsTopIII] (panalocalization along prime-strips). The desired geometry must satisfy: (a) local independence of global structures; (b) globalizability independent of local structures (Fig. 4.3); (c) being based on étale-like structures, so as to give canonical splittings as in the étale-picture of Corollary 3.9 (i). (a) and (b) almost appear to contradict each other; for function fields of dimension one their simultaneous realization seems to require descending to the base field. It is said to be a highly nontrivial consequence of [AbsTopIII] that its mono-anabelian geometry satisfies (a), (b), (c).

Conclusion.

Methodological requirements (a), (b), (c) and the assertion that the mono-anabelian geometry of [AbsTopIII] satisfies them.

Obligations.

  • Properties (a), (b), (c) are informal; to check the assertion about [AbsTopIII] they must first be made precise.

Analogy between the mono-anabelian theory of [AbsTopIII] and the classical geometry of the upper half-plane H. (i) Composing the analogy with Frobenius-invariant indigenous bundles in p-adic Teichmüller theory and the p-adic/complex analogy of [pOrd], [pTeich] gives an analogy with H, whose canonical Kähler (Poincaré) metric relates the theory to classical Arakelov theory. (ii) The diagram (∗) Π ↷ k̄^× → (log) k̄ ↶ Π (k a finite extension of Q_p, Π the arithmetic fundamental group of a hyperbolic orbicurve over k, log the p-adic logarithm) is compared with the tautological indigenous bundle (E, ∇_E) on H: Hodge filtration 0 → ω → E → τ → 0 with τ = ω^{-1}, complex conjugation ι_E, the Hermitian metric |−|_ω from ω ↪ E → E ↠ τ, and κ_H = (1/2πi) ∂∂̄ log(|f|²_ω) for a trivializing section f, the canonical Kähler metric. The log in κ_H recalls the log-Frobenius operation; Π recalls ∂; ∂̄ recalls Π on the opposite side of log; the Hodge filtration corresponds to the ring structures on either side of log; log-shells as canonical units of volume correspond to κ_H determining volume on H. (iii) Properties (a), (b) of Remark 4.3.2 correspond to local representability of global degree via κ_H on a compact quotient S of H, and to the canonical global extension of κ_H over S. (iv) A table summarizes the analogy.

Conclusion.

Heuristic analogy; the only formula is the standard definition κ_H = (1/2πi) ∂∂̄ log(|f|²_ω) of the Kähler form from the Hermitian metric on ω.

Ambiguities.

  • The remark states analogies, not theorems; no claim requires proof.

The collection of factorizations J ↪ H ↪ G (outer homomorphisms compatible with the structure morphisms), namely the inclusions J^{g1} ↪ H^{g2}, is well defined compatibly with the indeterminacies, while specifying ι independently of ζ : J ↪ H^{g^{-1}} imposes a partial synchronization (deactivation) at the cost of arbitrary choices. (iii) At v ∈ V^bad in Example 4.5 (i), G = π1(D^⊚), H = the image of π1(D_{v_j}), J = the index l subgroup of a cuspidal inertia group; the indeterminacies cannot be naturally synchronized (such a synchronization would amount to a Galois-equivariant splitting of prime decomposition trees, which is absurd), yet by Corollary 2.5 the factorization J ↪ H ↪ G is uniquely determined by the G-conjugate of J. (i), (ii): group-theoretic observations on factorizations J ↪ H ↪ G under conjugacy indeterminacy. (iii): at bad v the factorization is uniquely determined by the composite J ↪ G (Corollary 2.5). (iv): at archimedean v only the H-conjugacy class of the image of J is determined (Corollary 2.8).

(i) At the level of labels, a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater is summarized by Fig. 4.4: [1 < 2 < ... < l*] for †𝔇_>, (1 2 ... l*) for †𝔇_J, the F_l^*-cycle of ∗'s for †D^⊚ = B(C_K)^0, ⇑ for the D-Θ-bridge, ⇒ for the D-NF-bridge. (ii) The labels from †𝔇_> come from irreducible components of the special fiber (a chain of projective lines) of a tempered covering of a Tate curve ([EtTh] Corollary 2.9), counted additively from an origin: geometric, additive, archimedean, hence Frobenius-like (Corollary 3.8). The ∗'s of †D^⊚ come from primes of a number field permuted cyclically by F_l^* = F_l^×/{±1}: arithmetic, multiplicative, nonarchimedean, hence étale-like. The only common ground is an underlying set of cardinality l*, that of †𝔇_J. (iii) (†ζ_*)^{-1} : J ⥲ LabCusp(†D^⊚) relates arithmetic (elements of J as collections of primes) to geometry (cusps), and may be thought of as a combinatorial Kodaira-Spencer morphism ([HASurI] §1.4).

Conclusion.

Heuristic description of the label structure of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Fig. 4.4); no new assertion beyond F_l^* = F_l^×/{±1} and the cardinality l* of J.

If instead each D-prime-strip of †𝔇_J had its own copy of D^⊚ (independent globalization) related by a copy of φ^NF_j known only up to F_l^*, and the mutually disjoint F_l^*-translates of V^{±un} ∩ V(K)^bad (whose union is V^Bor ∩ V(K)^bad) were regarded as labeled by F_l^*, each D-prime-strip would carry an independent indeterminacy (Fig. 4.5), and the possible correspondences J → F_l^* would include non-bijective ones. Since F_l^* also acts faithfully on conjugates of the cusp ε, working with V(K) up to F_l^* requires working with conjugates of ε up to F_l^*; nonsynchronized labels are inconsistent with the bijection †ζ_* of Proposition 4.7 (iii). (ii) The single copy of D^⊚ is a single connected component, a single basepoint. (iii) Since F_l^* acts transitively on itself, independent F_l^*- or S_{l*}-indeterminacies at each index give the same set of possibilities. (iv) The synchronized indeterminacy (†ζ_*) is a combinatorial model of a holomorphic structure, the nonsynchronized one of a real analytic structure. IUT1.Def4_10Definition 4.10
Record

For a category C and a positive integer n, an n-procession (procession of length n) of C is a diagram P_1 ↪ P_2 ↪ ... ↪ P_n in which each P_j (j = 1, ..., n) is a j-capsule of objects of C and each arrow P_j ↪ P_{j+1} denotes the collection of all capsule-full poly-morphisms from P_j to P_{j+1}. A morphism from an n-procession (P_1 ↪ ... ↪ P_n) to an m-procession (Q_1 ↪ ... ↪ Q_m) is an order-preserving injection ι : {1, ..., n} ↪ {1, ..., m} (so n ≤ m) together with a capsule-full poly-morphism P_j ↪ Q_{ι(j)} for each j = 1, ..., n.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • C a category
  • n a positive integer

Conclusion.

Definition of n-processions of C and their morphisms (Fig. 4.6 shows an l*-procession of D-prime-strips).

Obligations.

  • Definition. Unlike most objects of IUT I, it uses only categories, capsules and capsule-full poly-morphisms (§0), so it could be stated in Lean on top of the existing §0 definitions.

Ambiguities.

  • The text does not state how morphisms of processions compose; composition of order-preserving injections and of capsule-full poly-morphisms is the evident candidate.
  • Whether the P_j are required to be related to each other beyond the arrows (for example, subcapsules) is not stated in the definition; in Proposition 4.11 they are subcapsules of one capsule.

IUT1.Prop4_11Proposition 4.11Processions of Base-Prime-Strips
Record

Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) given a D-Θ-bridge †φ^Θ_* : †𝔇_J → †𝔇_>, let Prc(†𝔇_J) be the l*-procession of D-prime-strips formed by the subcapsules of †𝔇_J corresponding to S*_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ S*_j = {1, 2, ..., j} ⊆ ... ⊆ S*_{l*} = F_l^* (positive integers standing for their images in F_l^*), relative to †χ : J ⥲ F_l^* of Proposition 4.7 (i). Then †φ^Θ_* ↦ Prc(†𝔇_J) is a natural functor from D-Θ-bridges and their isomorphisms to processions of D-prime-strips and their morphisms, whose output has, for each n ∈ {1, ..., l*}, precisely n possibilities for the element of F_l^* corresponding to a given index of the n-capsule; taking the product over F_l^*, the indeterminacy of (l*)^{(l*)} possibilities of Proposition 4.9 (ii) is reduced to l*! possibilities (also after pre-composing with †HT^{D-ΘNF} ↦ †φ^Θ_*). (ii) Composing with mono-analyticization gives a natural functor †φ^Θ_* ↦ Prc(†𝔇^⊢_J) to processions of D^⊢-prime-strips with the same indeterminacy properties.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
  • a D-Θ-bridge †φ^Θ_* : †𝔇_J → †𝔇_> (Definition 4.6 (ii))

Conclusion.

Natural functors to l*-processions of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, with label indeterminacy n at the n-th capsule and total indeterminacy l*! instead of (l*)^{(l*)}.

Obligations.

  • Proof (page 121): (i), (ii) "follow immediately from the definitions".
  • The counting step ∏_{n=1}^{l*} n = l*! versus (l*)^{(l*)} is elementary and could be checked in Lean on its own.

Ambiguities.

  • The phrase "precisely n possibilities" counts possibilities prior to applying the functor; the formal meaning of a set of possibilities is not defined.

IUT1.Ex5_1Example 5.1Global Frobenioids
Record

Global Frobenioids attached to the D-NF-bridge portion of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater †HT^{D-ΘNF} (Definition 4.6). From π1(†D^⊚) one constructs group-theoretically, via [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 applied through the Θ-approach of Remark 3.1.2, an isomorph M^⊛(†D^⊚) of F̄^× with its field structure, the category †D^⊛ (B(−)^0 of a profinite group corresponding to C_{F_mod}) with a natural morphism †D^⊚ → †D^⊛, monoids of κ-, ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric rational functions, the quotient π1^rat → π1^{κ-sol}, and a poly-action of F_l^* (parts (i), (ii)); a Frobenioid †F^⊛ over †D^⊛ with its restrictions †F^⊚ and †F^⊛_mod (part (iii)); birationalizations, local monoids O^▷_p and decomposition groups (part (iv)); ∞κ-coric and ∞κ×-coric structures and their uniqueness, and the reconstruction of Prime(†F^⊛_mod) ⥲ V_mod (part (v)); the same for †F^⊚, †D^⊚ (part (vi)); copies †F^⊛_j, the diagonal †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} and products over the capsule index set J, with realifications (part (vii)).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • †HT^{D-ΘNF} = (†D^⊚ ← †D_J → †D_>) a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Definition 4.6), relative to a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in Definition 3.1 (page 123)

Implicit hypotheses.

  • Only the D-NF-bridge portion †φ^NF_* is used (Remark 5.1.2).

Conclusion.

Group-theoretic or category-theoretic constructions of the global Frobenioids †F^⊛, †F^⊚, †F^⊛_mod and their associated monoids and structures, together with the asserted properties of parts (i) to (vii): the κ-sol-conjugate synchronization of part (i), the uniqueness up to a uniquely determined isomorphism of the ∞κ-coric (respectively ∞κ×-coric) structure on †F^⊛ in part (v), and the functorial reconstruction algorithms of part (v).

Obligations.

  • Construct the objects of parts (i) to (vii) and prove the properties asserted in parts (i) and (v); the text derives them from [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9, [AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3 and [FrdI], with phrases such as "it follows formally" and "it follows immediately".
  • Part (vi) is left to the reader as routine.

Ambiguities.

  • Example 5.1 mixes definitions (notation and constructions) with assertions (uniqueness and reconstruction); the assertions are recorded in the child records .i and .v.

The reconstruction algorithms for number fields of Example 5.1 rest on Belyi cuspidalization ([AbsTopIII] §1), whose viewpoint is that elements of number fields can be expressed geometrically by Belyi maps; the rest of [AbsTopIII] (especially §5) is a theory of analytic continuation of these functions under the logarithm maps at the localizations. The remark relates this to Remarks 4.3.2, 4.3.3 and, as an arithmetic analogue, to hyperbolic analytic continuations on the upper half-plane in the Motivating Example of [GeoAnbd], comparing the inequality ≤ 1 for derivatives with the decreasing degrees used to construct Belyi maps.

Conclusion.

Heuristic commentary; no mathematical assertion requiring proof.

Consequence of κ-sol-conjugate synchronization: the Kummer theory of π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ}, of †M^⊛_mod and of π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_sol (abstract analogues of ∞κ-coric functions, F^×_mod, F^×_sol) can be performed compatibly, without conjugacy indeterminacies, with the poly-action of (Aut^SL(†D^⊚) ↠) F_l^*. The remark then argues that a solvable-Uchida-type reconstruction of ring structure would be meaningless for the theory, being incompatible with the localization operations in a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater, since absolute Galois groups of nonarchimedean completions have automorphisms not arising from field automorphisms ([NSW], Closing Remark before Theorem 12.2.7); and that the outer action of the absolute Galois group of a number field on the geometric fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve does not factor through its maximal solvable quotient, as a formal consequence of [NodNon] Theorem C.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of IUT1.Ex5_1

Conclusion.

(1) The κ-sol Kummer theory of Example 5.1 (v) is compatible, without conjugacy indeterminacies, with the poly-action of F_l^*. (2) The outer Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve over a number field admits no solvable factorization.

Obligations.

  • Claim (1) rests on the synchronization of Example 5.1 (i); claim (2) is said to be a formal consequence of the Galois injectivity result [NodNon] Theorem C.

Ambiguities.

  • The assessment that a solvable-Uchida-type reconstruction is "meaningless" for the theory is a methodological judgment, not a mathematical statement.

Correction to [FrdI]: the hypothesis of unit-profinite type in [FrdI] Proposition 5.6 (hence in [FrdI] Corollary 5.7 (iii)) may be removed. In the notation of the proof of [FrdI] Proposition 5.6, writing φ'_p = c_p·φ_p with c_p ∈ O^×(A) for p ∈ Primes, the commutation φ'_2·φ'_p = φ'_p·φ'_2 gives c_2·c_p^2·φ_2·φ_p = c_p·c_2^p·φ_2·φ_p, so c_2·c_p^2 = c_p·c_2^p, that is c_p = c_2^{p−1}; hence φ'_p = c_2^{-1}·φ_p·c_2, and taking u = c_2^{-1} removes the last two paragraphs of that proof.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of the proof of [FrdI] Proposition 5.6: Frobenius-type endomorphisms φ_p, φ'_p = c_p·φ_p with c_p ∈ O^×(A), for p ∈ Primes

Implicit hypotheses.

  • φ_p·c = c^p·φ_p for c ∈ O^×(A) (used in the displayed computation)
  • O^×(A) is commutative and cancellative, so that c_2·c_p^2 = c_p·c_2^p can be solved for c_p
  • φ'_2 and φ'_p commute, and the φ_p commute

Conclusion.

c_p = c_2^{p−1} and φ'_p = c_2^{-1}·φ_p·c_2 for every prime p; consequently [FrdI] Proposition 5.6 and Corollary 5.7 (iii) hold without the unit-profinite hypothesis.

Obligations.

  • The implicit hypotheses are inferred from the displayed computation; the rule φ_p·c = c^p·φ_p is not stated on page 146.

Notation: 𝔉 and 𝔇 denote F- and D-prime-strips. (i) An NF-bridge is (‡𝔉_J → ‡F^⊚ ⇢ ‡F^⊛) with arrow ‡ψ^NF_* where: (a) ‡𝔉_J = {‡𝔉_j}_{j∈J} is a capsule of F-prime-strips over a finite index set J with associated capsule ‡𝔇_J; (b) ‡F^⊚, ‡F^⊛ are categories equivalent to †F^⊚, †F^⊛ of Example 5.1 (iii), with natural Frobenioid structures and base categories ‡D^⊚, ‡D^⊛; (c) the dashed arrow is a morphism ‡D^⊚ → ‡D^⊛ abstractly equivalent to †D^⊚ → †D^⊛, with an isomorphism ‡F^⊚ ⥲ ‡F^⊛|_{‡D^⊚}; (d) ‡ψ^NF_* is a poly-morphism lifting (uniquely, Corollary 5.3 (ii)) a poly-morphism ‡φ^NF_* : ‡𝔇_J → ‡D^⊚ that forms a D-NF-bridge. Morphisms of NF-bridges: a capsule-full poly-isomorphism ¹𝔉_{J1} ⥲ ²𝔉_{J2}, a poly-isomorphism ¹F^⊚ ⥲ ²F^⊚ lifting a poly-isomorphism ¹D^⊚ ⥲ ²D^⊚ such that the induced pair forms a morphism of D-NF-bridges, and an isomorphism ¹F^⊛ ⥲ ²F^⊛, compatible with the ψ^NF and the dashed arrows. (ii) A Θ-bridge is (‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_> ⇢ ‡HT^Θ) with arrow ‡ψ^Θ_* where ‡𝔉_J is as before, ‡HT^Θ is a Θ-Hodge theater, ‡𝔉_> is the F-prime-strip tautologically associated to ‡HT^Θ (with D-prime-strip ‡𝔇_>), and ‡ψ^Θ_* = {‡ψ^Θ_j} is determined (Remark 5.3.1) by a D-Θ-bridge ‡φ^Θ_*. Morphisms: a capsule-full poly-isomorphism of capsules, the full poly-isomorphism ¹𝔉_> ⥲ ²𝔉_>, and an isomorphism of Θ-Hodge theaters (Remark 3.6.2), compatible with the ψ^Θ and dashed arrows. (iii) A ΘNF-Hodge theater is ‡HT^{ΘNF} = (‡F^⊛ ⇠ ‡F^⊚ ← ‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_> ⇢ ‡HT^Θ) in which the left part is an NF-bridge, the right part a Θ-bridge, and the associated data {‡φ^NF_*, ‡φ^Θ_*} form a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater; morphisms are pairs of morphisms of the NF- and Θ-bridges inducing the same bijection of the index sets of the capsules.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1)

Conclusion.

Definitions of NF-bridges, Θ-bridges, ΘNF-Hodge theaters and their [iso]morphisms. The text adds that one verifies immediately that each object determines an associated D-object (D-NF-bridge, D-Θ-bridge, D-ΘNF-Hodge theater) and that each morphism induces a morphism of the associated D-objects, with evident composition.

IUT1.Cor5_6Corollary 5.6Isomorphisms of Θ-Hodge Theaters, NF-Bridges, Θ-Bridges, and ΘNF-Hodge Theaters
Record

Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) the natural functorially induced map from the set of isomorphisms between two Θ-Hodge theaters to the set of isomorphisms between the associated D-prime-strips is bijective; (ii) the natural map from isomorphisms between two NF-bridges (respectively Θ-bridges, ΘNF-Hodge theaters) to isomorphisms between the associated D-NF-bridges (respectively D-Θ-bridges, D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) is bijective; (iii) given an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge, the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms between their capsules of F-prime-strips that glue them into a ΘNF-Hodge theater is an F_l^*-torsor.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1)
  • two Θ-Hodge theaters (i); two NF-bridges, Θ-bridges or ΘNF-Hodge theaters (ii); an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge (iii)

Conclusion.

(i), (ii): the stated maps on isomorphism sets are bijections. (iii): the gluing set is an F_l^*-torsor.

Obligations.

  • Proof of (i) (page 154): one "verifies immediately" that the only data of a Θ-Hodge theater not contained in †𝔉_> are the global data of Definition 3.6 (c) and the tempered Frobenioids at bad v, that †F_{>,v} equals the double-underlined †F_v at good v, and that the global data are recovered by the algorithm 𝔉 ↦ 𝔉^⊩ of Remark 5.2.1 (ii); then (i) follows from Corollary 5.3 (ii) and (iv).
  • Assertions (ii), (iii) are said to follow immediately from (i), the definitions, Corollary 5.3 (i), (ii) and Proposition 4.8 (iii).
  • Frobenioids and Hodge theaters are not in Mathlib.

  • There is no Proposition 5.6 in §5; the statement with that number is Corollary 5.6.

IUT1.Def6_4Definition 6.4
Record

Put l^± = l* + 1 = (l+1)/2. (i) A D-Θ^±-bridge is a poly-morphism †φ^{Θ±}_± : †𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻ with †𝔇_≻ a D-prime-strip, T an F_l^±-group and †𝔇_T = {†𝔇_t}_{t∈T} a capsule of D-prime-strips, such that there are isomorphisms 𝔇_≻ ⥲ †𝔇_≻ and 𝔇_± ⥲ †𝔇_T whose induced bijection F_l ⥲ T is an isomorphism of F_l^±-groups and conjugation by which maps φ^{Θ±}_± ↦ †φ^{Θ±}_±. †𝔇_{|T|} is the l^±-capsule obtained by passing to |T| = T/{±1} and identifying the components in each fiber via the constituents of †φ^{Θ±}_± (each constituent well defined only up to a positive automorphism), and †𝔇_{T*} is the l*-capsule for T* = |T| \ {0}. A morphism is a pair: a capsule-+-full poly-isomorphism †𝔇_T ⥲ ‡𝔇_{T'} inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-groups T ⥲ T', and a +-full poly-isomorphism †𝔇_≻ ⥲ ‡𝔇_≻, compatible with the bridges. (ii) A D-Θ^ell-bridge is a poly-morphism †φ^{Θell}_± : †𝔇_T → †D^{⊚±} with †D^{⊚±} equivalent to D^{⊚±}, T an F_l^±-torsor, such that isomorphisms D^{⊚±} ⥲ †D^{⊚±} and 𝔇_± ⥲ †𝔇_T exist inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-torsors and mapping φ^{Θell}_± ↦ †φ^{Θell}_±. Morphisms: a capsule-+-full poly-isomorphism inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-torsors, and an Aut_csp-orbit of isomorphisms †D^{⊚±} → ‡D^{⊚±}, compatible with the bridges. (iii) A D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater is †HT^{D-Θ±ell} = (†𝔇_≻ ← †𝔇_T → †D^{⊚±}) with T an F_l^±-group, a D-Θ^±-bridge and a D-Θ^ell-bridge (for the induced torsor structure), such that isomorphisms to the models exist mapping φ^{Θ±}_± ↦ †φ^{Θ±}_± and φ^{Θell}_± ↦ †φ^{Θell}_± simultaneously; a morphism is a pair of morphisms of the two bridges inducing the same poly-isomorphism of capsules.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
  • the models of Examples 6.2 and 6.3

Conclusion.

Definitions of D-Θ^±-bridges, D-Θ^ell-bridges, D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters, the capsules †𝔇_{|T|} and †𝔇_{T*}, and their [iso]morphisms, with evident composition.

Obligations.

  • Definition. The indeterminacy up to positive automorphisms in †𝔇_{|T|} is said not to affect later uses (Propositions 6.7, 6.8 (ii), 6.9 (i)); a formalization must check this at each use.

Ambiguities.

  • Each constituent of †𝔇_{|T|} is only well defined up to a positive automorphism (page 162); the definition does not fix a representative.

IUT1.Prop6_8Proposition 6.8Symmetries arising from Forgetful Functors
Record

Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) Associating to a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater its underlying D-Θ^ell-bridge is a natural functor (isomorphisms to isomorphisms) whose output admits an F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry, a symmetry by a finite group with a natural outer isomorphism to F_l^{⋊±}, acting doubly transitively (transitively with stabilizers of order two) on the index set T. (ii) Associating the l^±-capsule †𝔇_{|T|} of the underlying D-Θ^±-bridge is a natural functor to l^±-capsules of D-prime-strips with capsule-full poly-isomorphisms, whose output admits an S_{l^±}-symmetry acting transitively on |T|; it forgets the labels in |F_l| = F_l/{±1}, so that, given only †𝔇_{|T|} up to isomorphism, there are precisely l^± possibilities for the element of |F_l| corresponding to a given index. (iii) Composing (ii) with mono-analyticization (Definition 4.1 (iv)) gives a natural functor to l^±-capsules of D^⊢-prime-strips with the same symmetry properties.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data

Conclusion.

Three natural functors from the category of D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters (with isomorphisms), with output symmetries F_l^{⋊±} (doubly transitive on T), S_{l^±} (transitive on |T|), and the same for the mono-analytic capsules.

IUT1.Rem6_12_3Remark 6.12.3

(i) A ΘNF-Hodge theater may be thought of as a total space of a local system of F_l^*-torsors, and a Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater of F_l^{⋊±}-torsors, over a base space representing a homotopy between a number field and a Tate curve. These torsors arise from l-torsion points (discrete approximations of the elliptic curve over a number field, [HASurI] §1.3.4) and, via tempered fundamental groups at bad v, as finite approximations of the copy of Z that is the Galois group of a tempered covering of the Tate curve ([EtTh] Remark 2.16.2); in a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater the additive and multiplicative structures of this Z occur independently, extracted from the entanglement in a ring. (ii) The local-system copy of Z recalls the Teichmüller-theoretic viewpoint of [AbsTopIII] §I5, corresponding in p-adic Teichmüller theory to a nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundle. (iii) The two combinatorial dimensions (additive F_l^{⋊±}, multiplicative F_l^*) correspond to two real dimensions of transformations of the upper half-plane: z ↦ z + a, z ↦ −z̄ + a, and z ↦ (z·cos t − sin t)/(z·sin t + cos t), z ↦ (z̄·cos t + sin t)/(z̄·sin t − cos t) (a, t ∈ R). The additive symmetry relates to q = e^{2πiz} and fixes the cusp at infinity (combinatorial prototype: cusp); the multiplicative symmetry relates to w = (z − i)/(z + i) and acts transitively on the boundary (prototype: node of a mod p Hecke correspondence). The only coric symmetries, common to both, are {±1} (z ↦ z, −z̄). Fig. 6.4 tabulates the comparison.

Conclusion.

Heuristic analogy. The concrete content is the list of transformations of the upper half-plane on page 176: the additive family z ↦ z + a, z ↦ −z̄ + a, said to fix the cusp at infinity and to relate to q = e^{2πiz}; the multiplicative family, said to act transitively on the boundary and to relate to w = (z − i)/(z + i); and the statement (page 177) that the symmetries common to both are z ↦ z, −z̄, compared with {±1}. Fig. 6.4 on page 178 tabulates the comparison.

Obligations.

  • The statements about the two families of transformations on pages 176 and 177 are elementary and could be checked in Lean independently.

Ambiguities.

  • Whether the multiplicative family with t ∈ R and the additive family with a ∈ R meet exactly in z ↦ z and z ↦ −z̄ depends on the parametrization; the page states this without computation.
