(i) Like the F_l^*-symmetry of Proposition 4.9 (i), the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of Proposition 6.8 (i) will be used ([IUTchII], [IUTchIII]) to build an explicit network of comparison isomorphisms relating objects such as log-volumes on the non-labeled prime-strips it permutes, without label crushing (preserving the bijection between indices and labels in T ⥲ F_l); this synchronization of labels is essentially a consequence of the single connected component (single basepoint) of the global object †D^{⊚±} (respectively †D^⊚). (ii) Concretely, it is realized by the bijections †ζ_* : LabCusp(†D^⊚) ⥲ J and †ζ_± : LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) ⥲ T of Propositions 4.7 (iii), 6.5 (iii); these bijections between index sets of capsules and sets of global (±-)label classes of cusps distinguish the combinatorially holomorphic F_l^*- and F_l^{⋊±}-symmetries (Propositions 4.9 (i), 6.8 (i)) from the combinatorially real analytic S_{l*}- and S_{l^±}-symmetries (Propositions 4.9 (ii), (iii); 6.8 (ii), (iii)). (iii) The additive theory has global ±-synchronization: the isomorphisms †ξ of Proposition 6.5 (i), (ii) between the ±-indeterminacies at the various v. This is a necessary precondition for the additive portion F_l ⊆ F_l^{⋊±} of the symmetry, since the additive action of F_l on itself is not compatible with F_l ↠ |F_l|. (iv) Both the †ζ's and the †ξ's are constructed by functorial algorithms from the intrinsic structure of the Hodge theater, not by comparison with a fixed reference model such as the objects of Examples 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 6.2, 6.3; this matters when combining with the log-shells of [AbsTopIII] in [IUTchIII].

Conclusion.

Interpretive summary; the mathematical claims cited are Propositions 4.7 (iii), 6.5, 4.9, 6.8, plus the elementary observation that translation by F_l does not descend to |F_l| = F_l/{±1}.

(i) A fundamental difference between the F_l^*-symmetry of §4 and the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of §6 is the inclusion of the zero element of F_l, which lets the network of comparison isomorphisms relate the zero-labeled prime-strip to the nonzero-labeled ones, in a combinatorially holomorphic fashion compatible with the bijections †ζ; evaluation at torsion points related to the zero-labeled cusps (Example 4.4 (i)) is important for the normalization of the étale theta function ([EtTh] Theorem 1.10, functions of standard type; [IUTchII]). (ii) The disadvantage is that it does not insulate the nonzero-labeled prime-strips from confusion with the zero-labeled one; this matters for the Gaussian Frobenioids of [IUTchII], arising from the theta values {q_v^{j²}}_j (q double-underlined, j underlined) at the non-zero-labeled evaluation points (Example 4.4), which are later related to global arithmetic line bundles on F using both additive and multiplicative structures, hence §5. (iii) Since no analogues of Gaussian Frobenioids involving the zero-labeled points will be needed, no additive analogue of the global Frobenioids of Example 5.1 is required.

Conclusion.

Methodological remark: the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry relates zero- and nonzero-labeled prime-strips but cannot separate them; no additive analogue of Example 5.1 is needed.

Ambiguities.

  • "Confusion" of zero- and nonzero-labeled prime-strips (page 180) is informal.

IUT1.Rem6_12_6Remark 6.12.6
Record

(i) Another difference: the single basepoint underlying the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry is geometric. The labels in T ⥲ F_l of a (D-)Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater correspond throughout to collections of cusps in a single copy (connected component) of D_v at each v, permuted by the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of the (D-)Θ^ell-bridge (Proposition 6.8 (i)) without permuting the valuations V^± ⊆ V(K) (Definition 6.1 (v)); by contrast the single basepoint of the F_l^*-symmetry of §4 is arithmetic: F_l^* (Proposition 4.9 (i)) permutes the F_l^*-translates of V^± = V^{±un} ⊆ V^Bor ⊆ V(K) (Example 4.3 (i), Remark 6.1.1). (ii) The geometric basepoint suits the Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of the étale theta function ([IUTchII]), where a single connected component of D_v at bad v is central. (iii) The arithmetic basepoint suits the explicit construction of F_mod (Example 5.1), an object invariant under the F_l^*-symmetries Aut(C_K)/Aut_ε(C_K) ⥲ F_l^* of Example 4.3 (iv); carrying out Example 5.1 with D^{⊚±} would sacrifice the F_l^*-rigidity with respect to Aut(D^{⊚±})/Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⥲ F_l^* (Definition 6.1 (v); Example 6.3; Definition 6.4 (ii)), losing the single geometric basepoint and compatibility with [IUTchII]. (iv) This reflects that the Borel subgroup {(∗ ∗; 0 ∗)} ⊆ SL_2(F_l) is normally terminal (Example 4.3), whereas the semi-unipotent subgroup {(±1 ∗; 0 ±1)} ⊆ SL_2(F_l), corresponding to Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⊆ Aut(D^{⊚±}), is not. (v) A (D-)Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater is an intricate relay between geometric and arithmetic basepoints allowing both (a) the evaluation theory of [IUTchII] and (b) the construction of F_mod in Example 5.1; with F_l viewed as a finite approximation of Z, this is a global combinatorial resolution of the additive and multiplicative dimensions of Z ([AbsTopIII] Remark 5.6.1). Computationally it is natural to regard F_l as a good approximation of Z when l is sufficiently large, as in [GenEll] §4 (Remark 3.1.2 (iv)).

Conclusion.

Interpretive remark. Mathematical content: (a) the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry permutes cusps without permuting V^±, while the F_l^-symmetry permutes F_l^-translates of V^±; (b) the Borel subgroup of SL_2(F_l) is normally terminal, the semi-unipotent subgroup is not.

Obligations.

  • Claim (iv) on normal terminality in SL_2(F_l) is elementary finite group theory and could be checked in Lean (for the semi-unipotent subgroup, its normalizer contains the diagonal torus, so it is not normally terminal; for the Borel subgroup, it is self-normalizing); the text gives no proof on these pages, referring to Example 4.3 for the Borel case.
  • The correspondence of the semi-unipotent subgroup with Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⊆ Aut(D^{⊚±}) is asserted with reference to Definition 6.1 (v).

Ambiguities.

  • In the display of the semi-unipotent subgroup (page 181) the two diagonal entries are written ±1 independently; inside SL_2(F_l) the determinant condition forces them to be equal, so the subgroup is {±1} times the unipotent radical.
  • "Normally terminal" means equal to its normalizer; the term is used without definition on these pages.

IUT2.Prop1_2Proposition 1.2Group- and Frobenioid-theoretic Constructions of Mono-theta Environments
Record

Group- and Frobenioid-theoretic constructions of mono-theta environments. (i) For a topological group Pi isomorphic to Pi^tp_{X_k} (X double underline), there is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm Pi -> M^Theta(Pi) constructing a mod N mono-theta environment up to isomorphism ([EtTh] Corollary 2.18 (ii)) such that its composite with M^Theta -> Pi_X(M^Theta) of Definition 1.1 (i) admits a functorial isomorphism Pi -> Pi_X(M^Theta(Pi)); the isomorphism indeterminacy of M^Theta(Pi) is relative to a group of mu_N-conjugacy classes of automorphisms of order 1 if N is odd and 2 if N is even ([EtTh] Corollary 2.18 (iv)). (ii) For a category C equivalent to the tempered Frobenioid determined by X_k (the C of [EtTh] Section 5, the F_v of [IUTchI] Example 3.2 (i)), which is a Frobenioid over a base category D equivalent to B^temp(Pi^tp_{X_k})^0, there is a functorial algorithm C -> M^Theta(C) constructing a mod N mono-theta environment ([EtTh] Theorem 5.10 (iii)) whose composite with M^Theta -> Pi_X admits a functorial isomorphism D -> B^temp(Pi_X(M^Theta(C)))^0.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • (i): Pi a topological group isomorphic to Pi^tp_{X_k}
  • (ii): C a category equivalent to the tempered Frobenioid determined by X_k
  • N a positive integer

Conclusion.

Functorial algorithms Pi -> M^Theta(Pi) and C -> M^Theta(C) producing mod N mono-theta environments, compatible with recovering Pi (respectively D) via Definition 1.1 (i).

IUT2.Rem1_4_1Remark 1.4.1
Record

Recollection from [EtTh] Sections 1, 2 of the theory of etale theta functions of standard type. (i) X double underline_k -> X single underline_k -> C single underline_k are the hyperbolic orbicurves of type (1, l-tors), (1, l-tors)_+- determined by X double underline_k ([EtTh] Proposition 2.4); X single underline_k has a unique zero cusp, fixed by Gal(X_k/C_k); mu_- in X single underline_k(k) is the unique torsion point of order 2 whose closure in any stable model over O_k meets the same irreducible component of the special fiber as the zero cusp. (ii) The unique order two automorphism iota of X double underline_k over k lies over an order two automorphism of X single underline_k and corresponds to the unique order two Delta^tp-outer automorphism of Pi^tp over G_k. Y-double-dot_k -> Y_k -> X_k (double underlines) are the tempered coverings for the open subgroups of Proposition 1.4 and Definition 1.1 (i), Proposition 1.2 (i). Since k contains a primitive 4l-th root of unity, there are rational points (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot} and (mu_-)_X over mu_-; iota fixes the Gal(X double underline/X single underline)-orbit of (mu_-)_X, hence (as l != 2 and Aut is Z/2lZ) fixes (mu_-)_X; so there is an order two automorphism iota_{Y-double-dot} lifting iota, unique up to l . Z-conjugacy and composition with Gal(Y-double-dot/Y), fixing the Gal(Y-double-dot/Y)-orbit of some point of the Gal(Y-double-dot/X)-orbit of (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot}. These are the inversion automorphisms; D_{mu_-} in Pi^tp of Y-double-dot double underline is the decomposition group of (mu_-)_{Y-double-dot}, well defined up to conjugacy by Delta^tp of Y-double-dot double underline, and determined by iota_{Y-double-dot} up to conjugacy by Delta^tp_{Y_k} := Delta_Y(M^Theta(Pi^tp of X double underline_k)) (Y without underline, notation of Remark 1.1.1 (i)); either pair (iota, point) or (iota as outer automorphism, D_{mu_-}) is a pointed inversion automorphism. An etale theta function of standard type is defined precisely by the condition that its restriction to D_{mu_-} is a 2l-th root of unity ([EtTh] Definition 1.9 (ii), Definition 2.7).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Section 1 (page 20) and of Proposition 1.4

Conclusion.

The inversion automorphisms iota_X and iota_{Y-double-dot} and the decomposition group D_{mu_-} exist with the stated uniqueness, giving pointed inversion automorphisms; an etale theta function is of standard type exactly when its restriction to D_{mu_-} is a 2l-th root of unity.

  • No Lean vocabulary exists for tempered fundamental groups, mono-theta environments, Frobenioids or Hodge theaters; the statement stays a catalog entry.

A formalization depends on [EtTh] Remark 2.6.1 and Definition 2.7 and on [SemiAnbd] Theorem 6.4.

IUT2.Prop1_5Proposition 1.5Projective Systems of Mono-theta Environments
Record

Projective systems of mono-theta environments. Let M^Theta_* = {... -> M^Theta_{M'} -> M^Theta_M -> ...} be a projective system of mono-theta environments, M^Theta_M a mod M mono-theta environment isomorphic to the mod M model one of X double underline_k, M varying multiplicatively in N_{>=1}. (i) Such a system is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by X double underline_k (discrete rigidity, [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (ii)). (ii) The transition morphisms of the system {Pi_X(M^Theta_M)} (X double underline) are all isomorphisms; any isomorphism Pi_X(M^Theta_{M'}) -> Pi_X(M^Theta_M), M dividing M', lifts to a morphism of mono-theta environments; identifying along them gives Pi_X(M^Theta_*), with open subgroup Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*), subquotient (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta_*) and quotient G(M^Theta_*). (iii) The exterior cyclotomes form a projective system with limit Pi_mu(M^Theta_*), with a uniquely determined cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l . Delta_Theta)(M^Theta_*) -> Pi_mu(M^Theta_*) (from those of Definition 1.1 (ii)); transporting theta(Pi) of Proposition 1.4 gives a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> theta_env(M^Theta_*) in H^1(Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*), Pi_mu(M^Theta_*)), and infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*) in the direct limit over finite index open J of H^1(Pi_{Y-double-dot}(M^Theta_*)|_J, Pi_mu(M^Theta_*)) is the set of elements some positive multiple of which coincides up to torsion with an element of theta_env(M^Theta_*). (iv) If M^Theta_* arises from a tempered Frobenioid C (Propositions 1.2 (ii), 1.3), the construction of theta_env(M^Theta_*) is compatible with the Kummer-theoretic construction of the etale theta function from the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function, in particular with the Kummer theory of the base-field-theoretic hull C^{bs-fld}.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • The notation of Remark 1.4.1 and Section 1
  • M^Theta_* a projective system of mono-theta environments M^Theta_M, each mod M and isomorphic to the mod M model mono-theta environment of X double underline_k, M varying multiplicatively in N_{>=1}
  • For (iv): M^Theta_* arises from a tempered Frobenioid C as in Propositions 1.2 (ii), 1.3

Conclusion.

See the part records (i) to (iv).

Record

An important consequence of the discrete rigidity of [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (ii), which allows one to restrict to l . Z-translates (rather than l . Zhat-translates) of the usual theta function, is the compatibility of projective systems of mono-theta environments (Proposition 1.5) with the discrete structure of the isomorphs of the monoid N in the tempered Frobenioids of the theory.

  • The setting of Proposition 1.5

Conclusion.

Discrete rigidity makes projective systems of mono-theta environments compatible with the discrete structure given by the isomorphs of N in tempered Frobenioids.

Radial and coric data I: generalities. Defines radial and coric data, radial environments (R, C, Phi: R -> C), multiradial and uniradial environments, the tautological multiradialization, the switching functor criterion for multiradiality, multiradially, uniradially and corically defined functors Psi_R, and the interpretation of multiradiality as simultaneous execution compatible with gluing of coric portions, in five parts.

Conclusion.

    (i) A type of mathematical data called radial data (formalized in [IUTchIV] Section 3; thought of as input or output of a functorial algorithm, [IUTchI] Remark 3.2.1) gives a category R whose objects are collections of radial data and whose morphisms are isomorphisms; likewise coric data give a category C of collections of coric data and their isomorphisms. A functorial algorithm, called radial, with input radial data and output coric data, gives a functor Phi: R -> C, assumed essentially surjective; R and Phi are called radial and C coric. For a nonempty index set I one considers copies {Phi_i: R_i -> C}_{i in I} with common codomain C (Fig. 1.1), R_i being radial data equipped with a label i.

    • C a category all of whose morphisms are isomorphisms (coric data)
    • Phi: R -> C a functor arising from a functorial algorithm, assumed essentially surjective
    • I a nonempty index set (for the labeled copies)

    Conclusion.

    Definitions of radial data, coric data, the radial functor Phi: R -> C and labeled copies Phi_i: R_i -> C.

    (ii) A triple (R, C, Phi: R -> C) as in (i) is a radial environment; it is multiradial if Phi is full, uniradial otherwise. For a uniradial environment an object of R may lose rigidity (gain indeterminacy) when mapped to C; multiradiality means that applying the radial algorithm causes no loss of rigidity. If any two collections of radial data are isomorphic, the tautological multiradialization (R^mtz, C, Phi^mtz) is defined: objects are triples (R, C, alpha) with R in R, C in C and alpha: Phi(R) -> C a full poly-isomorphism; isomorphisms (R, C, alpha) -> (R*, C*, alpha*) are pairs of isomorphisms R -> R*, C -> C* (necessarily compatible with alpha, alpha*); the coric data are those of the original environment and the radial algorithm is (R, C, alpha) -> C, whose functor is full and essentially surjective; there is a natural functor R -> R^mtz, R -> (R, Phi(R), Phi(R) -> Phi(R)). It forgets the uniradiality in a minimal way.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • (R, C, Phi) a radial environment as in (i)
    • For the multiradialization: any two collections of radial data (objects of R) are isomorphic

    Conclusion.

    Definitions of multiradial and uniradial environments; for a radial environment with all objects of R isomorphic, the tautological multiradialization (R^mtz, C, Phi^mtz) is a multiradial environment with a natural functor R -> R^mtz.

IUT2.Rem1_7_1Remark 1.7.1
Record

The fullness condition in the definition of a multiradial environment allows parallel transport between fibers of the radial functor Phi: R -> C (lifting isomorphisms in C to isomorphisms in R, Example 1.7 (iv), (v)); such liftings are unique up to an indeterminacy arising from the failure of Phi to be faithful. A uniradial environment is an abstraction of a fibration without a connection, a multiradial environment of a fibration with a connection, the coric data being the horizontal part of the radial data.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • A radial environment (R, C, Phi) as in Example 1.7

Conclusion.

Fullness of Phi lets isomorphisms of C lift to R, uniquely up to the indeterminacy coming from non-faithfulness of Phi; multiradial environments are analogous to fibrations with a connection.

Obligations.

  • The uniqueness of liftings up to the non-faithfulness of Phi is called a tautological observation; the fibration and connection analogy is interpretive and has no formal content.

The part of the algorithms of Example 1.9 (ii) to (iv) involving Pi/Delta depends not only on the abstract topological group Pi/Delta but on its structure as a quotient of Pi, i.e. on the arithmetic holomorphic structure. The multiradial terminology of Example 1.7 was introduced to compute which portions of the output of such algorithms depend essentially on the arithmetic holomorphic structure and which are mono-analytic, depending only on the topological group Pi/Delta. The tautological approach of Example 1.9 (ii) ((iv) (a)) corresponds to equipping each spoke Pi/Delta of Fig. 1.2 with a fixed arithmetic holomorphic structure related to the coric G only by an indeterminate isomorphism: a multiradially defined functor compatible with simultaneous execution on multiple spokes. The approach of Example 1.9 (iii) ((iv) (b)) identifies the spokes via arbitrary mono-analytic isomorphisms: a uniradially defined functor that can be executed consistently on one spoke at a time. The approach of Example 1.9 (iv) (c) weakens the rigidity of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism to a specified indeterminacy and obtains a multiradially defined functor compatible with gluing isomorphisms; its multiradiality depends essentially on the content of the algorithm. This is representative of Corollaries 1.10, 1.11 and 1.12, which may be regarded as computations of the indeterminacy needed.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Examples 1.8 and 1.9

Conclusion.

Of the three approaches of Example 1.9 (iv), (a) is tautologically multiradial, (b) is uniradial (one spoke at a time), and (c) is multiradial up to a specified indeterminacy, the model for Corollaries 1.10 to 1.12.

Obligations.

  • Interpretive commentary on Example 1.9; the formal content is that of Example 1.9 (ii) to (iv).

(i) Uniradially defined functors correspond to constructions depending strictly on the arithmetic holomorphic structure, corically defined ones to constructions depending only on the mono-analytic (arithmetic real analytic) structure, and multiradially defined ones to constructions depending on the arithmetic holomorphic structure only in a way compatible with a given description of how it is related to (embedded in) the mono-analytic structure; in Example 1.8 this description is given by the poly-morphisms alpha_(-) of the radial data (summarized in Fig. 1.3, comparing with holomorphic and real analytic structures in classical complex Teichmuller theory). (ii) With the analogy of Remark 1.7.1, a multiradial environment allows parallel transport between distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures related only via the mono-analytic core. (iii) The approaches of Example 1.9 (iv) (a), (c) are analogous to distinct connection structures on one fibration; the tautological approach (a), comparable to the tautological construction of connections in the p-adic crystalline theory via the PD-envelope of the diagonal, works with labels of all possible arithmetic holomorphic structures (choices of one arrow of the poly-morphism alpha of Example 1.8 (i)) and is less interesting than the non-tautological approach (c), which explicitly computes indeterminacies and so describes structures attached to an alien arithmetic holomorphic structure.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Examples 1.7 to 1.9 and Remarks 1.7.1, 1.9.1

Conclusion.

Uniradial, multiradial and corically defined functors correspond to dependence on the arithmetic holomorphic structure, dependence compatible with its relation to the mono-analytic structure, and dependence on the mono-analytic structure only (Fig. 1.3); the non-tautological approach of Example 1.9 (iv) (c) is preferred because it computes indeterminacies explicitly.

IUT2.Rem1_10_3Remark 1.10.3

Recalls ([EtTh] Remark 1.10.4 (ii)) that it is by no means clear that a more general meromorphic function than the theta function satisfies the cyclotomic, discrete and constant multiple rigidity properties of [EtTh]. Cyclotomic rigidity, the basis of Corollary 1.10, depends most explicitly ([EtTh] Remark 2.19.2) on the theta quotient 1 -> Delta_Theta -> Delta^Theta_X -> Delta^ell_X -> 1 ([IUTchI] Remark 3.1.2 (iii)), corresponding to the theta group of classical treatments; since the theta function is essentially characterized among meromorphic functions by the theta symmetries arising from the theta group, it is difficult to see how to generalize the theory to more general meromorphic functions (Remark 1.1.1 (v); [IUTchIII] Remark 2.3.3). Unlike the theta function, which is local (defined a priori at v in V^bad), the theta quotient Delta^Theta_X, hence Delta_Theta, is defined globally over the number fields involved ([IUTchI] Remark 3.1.2), so it can be used in global anabelian reconstruction via the Theta-approach.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollary 1.10

Conclusion.

Cyclotomic rigidity depends explicitly on the theta quotient; generalizing the theory beyond the theta function is not evident; the theta quotient and Delta_Theta are defined globally, unlike the theta function.

Obligations.

  • Commentary; the statements that more general meromorphic functions need not satisfy the rigidity properties and that the theta function is essentially characterized by the theta symmetries are heuristic ('roughly speaking') and are not claimed as theorems.

In the multiradial environment (R, C, Phi) of Example 1.8 (v), (vi), with Gamma^{x mu} := Ism, consider the functorial algorithm that attaches to Pi a commutative diagram (dagger_{x theta})(Pi): the subsets M^x_TM . infinity-theta(Pi) and M^x_TM . infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*(Pi)) of the inductive limits over finite index open J of H^1(Pi_Y(Pi)|_J, (l . Delta_Theta)(Pi)) and of H^1(Pi_Y(M^Theta_*(Pi))|_J, Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi))), joined by the isomorphism induced by the cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.10. With M^{x mu}_TM := M^x_TM / M^mu_TM (M^mu_TM the torsion), the corollary has three parts: (i) pointed inversion automorphisms, (ii) theta evaluation by restriction and the resulting splittings, (iii) multiradiality of the resulting functor.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • (R, C, Phi: R -> C) is the multiradial environment of Example 1.8 (v), (vi): (Pi acting on Pi_mu(M^Theta_*(Pi)) tensor Q/Z, G acting on O^{x mu}(G), alpha_{mu, x mu}) maps to (G acting on O^{x mu}(G))
  • Gamma^{x mu} := Ism
  • J ranges over the finite index open subgroups of Pi; |_J is the fiber product with J over Pi
  • infinity-theta(Pi) is produced by the algorithm of Proposition 1.4; infinity-theta_env(M^Theta_*(Pi)) by the algorithm of Proposition 1.5 (iii)

IUT2.Rem1_12_4Remark 1.12.4
Record

The theta evaluation algorithm of Corollary 1.12 (ii), by restriction to the decomposition groups of the point mu_-, uses only the topological group Pi as input; this is crucial when the theory is combined with log-shells ([AbsTopIII]) in [IUTchIII]. Given some evaluation algorithm (abstract theta function) -> (theta values), not necessarily restriction to the decomposition group of a closed point, it is natural ([EtTh] Remark 1.10.4; the log-wall of [AbsTopIII] Section I4; Remark 1.12.3) to require compatibility with forming Kummer classes by extracting N-th roots of the abstract theta function and of the theta values, hence extension to coverings (e.g. Galois coverings) of input and output; functoriality for the Galois groups on both sides (Fig. 1.5) then leads to the principle of Galois evaluation: the evaluation algorithm arises from a section G -> Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) of the natural surjection Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) -> G. By the Section Conjecture of anabelian geometry one expects such continuous sections to arise from geometric points (compare [IUTchI] Example 4.5 (i), Remark 2.5.1). Group-theoreticity of the evaluation algorithm is an abstract analogue of compatibility with Frobenius crystal structures in p-adic theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollary 1.12

Conclusion.

Requiring an evaluation algorithm to be compatible with Kummer classes and functorial with respect to Galois groups forces, in effect, that it arise from a section G -> Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) of Pi_{Y-double-dot}(Pi) -> G (principle of Galois evaluation); by the Section Conjecture such sections are expected to come from geometric points.

Obligations.

  • Page 61: the passage from 'natural requirements' (Kummer compatibility, extension to coverings, Galois functoriality) to the conclusion that the evaluation arises from a section is described as leading 'in effect' to that conclusion; the requirements are not made precise and no argument is given. The Section Conjecture is an open conjecture and is invoked only as an expectation.

IUT2.Rem1_12_5Remark 1.12.5
Record

Analogy with the Gaussian integral, in three parts. (i) Scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory ([HASurI], [HASurII]) is a scheme-theoretic version of the computation of the Gaussian integral, integral over R of e^{-x^2} dx = sqrt(pi), via the square of the integral over R^2 in polar coordinates: its comparison isomorphism ([HASurI] Theorem A) between a de Rham side (sections of an ample line bundle on the universal extension of an elliptic curve, with Hodge filtration) and an etale side (functions on the l-torsion points, with GL_2(F_l)-action) parallels cartesian versus polar coordinates (Fig. 1.6); e^{-x^2} appears in the Gaussian poles of the de Rham side ([HASurI] Section 1.1); sqrt(pi) corresponds to negative tensor powers of the sheaf omega, via the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism between omega^{tensor 2} and the restriction of the log differentials of the moduli stack ([HASurII] Theorems 2.8, 2.10); the relation is explicit at archimedean primes via the Hermite model. (ii) Inter-universal Teichmuller theory may be thought of as a global arithmetic/Galois-theoretic version of the Gaussian integral: the step-like cartesian representation resembles the Frobenius-picture ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.8, Remark 3.8.1), the rotational symmetry of polar coordinates resembles the etale-picture ([IUTchI] Corollary 3.9); the etale-picture of the multiradial functor of Corollary 1.12 (Fig. 1.7: copies of infinity-theta(Pi) on spokes around the mono-analytic core G acting on O^{x mu}(G) acted on by Ism), from the series sum over n in Z of q^{n^2} U^n ([EtTh] Proposition 1.4), resembles the polar representation; the change of variables e^{-r^2} to u in 2 (integral e^{-x^2} dx)^2 = 2 double integral e^{-x^2-y^2} dx dy = double integral e^{-r^2} 2r dr dtheta = double integral d(e^{-r^2}) dtheta = double integral du dtheta is formally reminiscent of the Theta-link Theta_v -> q_v ([IUTchI] Remark 3.8.1 (i)). (iii) As the equivalence of cartesian and polar representations is used to compute the Gaussian integral, the relation between Frobenius- and etale-pictures plays a central role ([IUTchIII] Section 3; [IUTchIV] Section 1).

Conclusion.

Analogies: Hodge-Arakelov theory and inter-universal Teichmuller theory are compared with the polar-coordinate computation of the Gaussian integral; Frobenius-picture versus etale-picture corresponds to cartesian versus polar coordinates, and the Theta-link to the substitution u = e^{-r^2}.

Obligations.

  • Analogy only; no mathematical claim about IUT objects. The classical identity integral over R of e^{-x^2} dx = sqrt(pi) is a standard result (available in Mathlib as the Gaussian integral).

Ambiguities.

  • Page 63: in the displayed chain, double integral e^{-r^2} 2r dr dtheta = double integral d(e^{-r^2}) dtheta holds only up to sign, since d(e^{-r^2}) = -2r e^{-r^2} dr; the integration limits are not written, so the sign is absorbed by orientation. The page calls the analogy 'formal'.
  • The index gives pages 61 to 64; the render of page 64 shows Section 2 starting at its top, so the remark ends on page 63.

(i) Relative to the standard cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism of Proposition 1.3 (ii) and the resulting Kummer map (delta of Corollary 2.5 (ii) taken to be the identity), for j in |F_l| the set theta^j(Pi_v) consists of precisely the mu_{2l}-orbit of the theta value qq_v^{j^2}, where j is the element of {0, 1, ..., l*} determined by j. (ii) The reciprocals of the l-th powers of these theta values (not the theta values themselves) correspond to the values Theta-ddot(+-sqrt(-1) . q_X^{j/2}) of the theta series Theta-ddot of [EtTh] Proposition 1.4, i.e. to values at points separated by periods from +-sqrt(-1); they have the property that Theta-ddot(c)/Theta-ddot(c') is a root of unity for c' obtained from c by an automorphism of Pi_v with c'/c a unit. (iii) The mu_{2l}-multiple indeterminacies for different j in |F_l| are independent, not synchronized; each arises from the action of (Delta^+-_v / Delta_v)^delta, of order 2l.

Conclusion.

theta^j(Pi_v) = mu_{2l} . qq_v^{j^2} (as orbits) for j = 0, ..., l*; the reciprocals of the l-th powers of these values correspond to Theta-ddot(+-sqrt(-1) . q_X^{j/2}); the mu_{2l}-indeterminacies for distinct j are independent.

(i) Viewing the sets of conjugates {I_t^{gamma_1}} and {Pi^{gamma_2}_{v black-triangle-double-dot}} up to Delta-hat^+-_v-conjugacy as quotients by Delta-hat^+-_v, the inclusions I_t -> Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} and the decomposition groups D_{t, mu_-} give morphisms between such quotients; since all inclusions lie in the single ambient container Pi-hat^+-_v, the evaluation algorithm of Corollary 2.5 (iii) is a nested version of the Galois evaluation of Remark 1.12.4, but here the subgroups Pi_{v black-triangle}, Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} are far from normal in Pi-hat^+-_v. (ii) With Pi^{circledcirc +-} := Pi_{X_K} and Delta^{circledcirc +-} := Delta_X ([IUTchI] Definition 3.1 (d), 6.1 (v)), Delta^{circledcirc +-} is identified up to inner automorphism with Delta-hat^+-_v, is independent of v, and is recovered from the global portion of a D-Theta^ell-bridge; it is a common bridge between local data such as Delta_{v black-triangle-double-dot} and global labels t in LabCusp^+-(Pi^{circledcirc +-}). (iii) Passing between distinct v through this bridge, the groups Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} do not globalize, which is why the conjugacy indeterminacies on conjugates of I_t and of Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} are independent; since neither Pi-hat^+-_v -> G_v nor Pi^{circledcirc +-} -> G_K has a section normalizing all I_t, a G_v- or G_K-conjugacy indeterminacy yields a Delta-hat^+-_v-conjugacy indeterminacy; since Delta-hat^cor_v -> Delta-hat^cor_v / Delta-hat^+-_v does not split, the outer action of F_l^{x+-} induces independent indeterminacies on the I_t for distinct t; and since G_v is not a direct summand of G_K, a G_K-conjugacy indeterminacy induces independent G_v-conjugacy indeterminacies. (iv) Fig. 2.1 pictures these independent indeterminacies by two lines with unsynchronized translation actions, so the inclusion of a conjugate of I_t into the left end of a conjugate of Pi_{v black-triangle-double-dot} cannot be separated from its inclusion into the right end.

(i) A central property of the evaluation algorithm of Corollary 2.5 (iii) is that it is performed relative to a single basepoint, the group Pi^gamma_{v black-triangle-double-dot} of the connected subgraph Gamma^{black-triangle}_X; so the theta values theta^{|t|} for the various |t| are all computed relative to a single copy of G_v(Pi^gamma_{v black-triangle-double-dot}) and a single cyclotome (l . Delta_Theta), independent of |t|. This is called conjugate synchronization, and it is needed for the Kummer theory of Section 3. (ii) For Gaussian Frobenioids this means the theta values for |t| in F_l^* are treated as a single entity whose Kummer theory uses one Galois group and one cyclotome acting simultaneously on N-th roots of all the values, compatibly with the base field; this requires a single basepoint of a connected geometric object, and the Kummer-theoretic representation of the monoid generated by the theta function is compatible with the log-wall, which is used in IUT III.

(i) In terms of D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theaters ([IUTchI] Definition 6.4 (iii)), one may view Pi_v as the tempered group of dagger D_{>,v}, Pi-hat^+-_v as the commensurator of the closure of Pi_v in the profinite group of dagger D^{circledcirc +-} via the zero-labeled portions of the bridges, and the outer action of Delta-hat^cor_v / Delta-hat^+-_v = F_l^{x+-} as the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry of [IUTchI] Proposition 6.8 (i). Then the single basepoint of conjugate synchronization is compatible with the single basepoint of label synchronization ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.4), so conjugate synchronization is compatible with the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry; this compatibility is essentially Corollary 2.4 (iii). (ii) This contrasts with the incompatibility with the F_l^*-symmetry of [IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i) for D-Theta NF-Hodge theaters, which permutes multiple copies of local objects at the expense of label crushing. (iii) The F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, unlike the F_l^*-symmetry, allows comparison with the label zero, hence with the copies of O_k^x in the splittings of Corollary 1.12 (ii) giving constant multiple rigidity; this is the content of Corollary 2.6.

Record

For a subgraph Gamma' of the line graph Gamma_Y (vertices Z), single-basepoint and splitting considerations force Gamma' connected and containing 0. For finite Gamma' define ||Gamma'|| = |Gamma'|^{-1} . sum over j in F_l* of min over integers j in (fiber of j) intersect Gamma' of j^2, where |Gamma'| is the cardinality of the image in F_l* of the nonzero vertices and the min over the empty set is 0. Claim (d): as a function of |Gamma'| this is a monotone increasing but not strictly increasing positive rational function that attains its maximum at |Gamma'| = l* and is constant for |Gamma'| >= l*.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • Gamma' a finite connected subgraph of Gamma_Y containing the vertex 0

Conclusion.

Maximizing ||Gamma'|| is achieved by Gamma'_Y-black-triangle (vertices 0, ..., l*), and the values qq_v^{j^2} are thereby distinguished.

Obligations.

  • Kernel-checked only for the elementary arithmetic: for Gamma' with vertex set [-a, b], |Gamma'| = min(max(a,b), l*) and ||Gamma'|| = (n+1)(2n+1)/6 with n = |Gamma'|, which is strictly increasing in n; hence ||Gamma'|| is monotone in max(a,b), maximal exactly when max(a,b) >= l*, with maximum l(l+1)/12. Infinite Gamma' (part (iii)) is not treated.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 79 defines |Gamma'| as the size of a subset of F_l*, so |Gamma'| <= l* always. Read literally, item (d) on page 80 then says ||Gamma'|| is a strictly increasing function of |Gamma'| on {1, ..., l*} (the Lean file proves this), which conflicts with 'not strictly increasing' and makes 'constant for |Gamma'| >= l*' vacuous beyond l*. The wording matches exactly if the variable is the radius max(a,b) of Gamma'; the Lean file proves both readings and adopts neither as the definition.
  • qq_v denotes the q with a double underline of IUT I, Example 3.2 (iv), page 71 (rendered): qq_v = q_v^{1/2l}, a chosen 2l-th root of the Tate parameter q_v, determined up to a mu_{2l}-multiple; relative to q_v the value qq_v^{j^2} is q_v^{j^2/(2l)}.
  • Page 79 defines ||Gamma'|| = |Gamma'|^{-1} . (sum); for Gamma' = {0} one has |Gamma'| = 0 and the page gives no value. The Lean function gammaNorm returns 0 there by division by zero; every Lean lemma that evaluates it assumes |Gamma'| >= 1.

Mono-theta-theoretic theta monoids. Let M^Theta_* be a projective system of mono-theta environments with Pi_X(M^Theta_*) isomorphic to Pi_v (abbreviated M^Theta_* inside parentheses). (i) Split theta monoids: by Proposition 1.5 (iii) and Corollary 2.8 (i) there is a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> {M^x_TM(M^Theta_*), theta^iota_env, infinity-theta^iota_env, M^x_TM . infinity-theta^iota_env within the limit over finite index open J of H^1(Pi_Y(M^Theta_*)|_J, Pi_mu(M^Theta_*))}_iota, iota ranging over the inversion automorphisms of Proposition 2.2 (i), with a natural conjugation action by Pi_X(M^Theta_*); hence an algorithm for the theta monoids Psi_env(M^Theta_*) := {Psi^iota_env = M^x_TM . theta^iota_env(M^Theta_*)^N}_iota and infinity-Psi_env := {M^x_TM . infinity-theta^iota_env(M^Theta_*)^N}_iota (submonoids of the direct limit of cohomology modules), and for their splittings up to torsion determined by M^x_TM, theta^iota_env, infinity-theta^iota_env (Corollary 2.8 (iii)). (ii) Constant monoids: using the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Corollaries 2.8 (i), 2.9 and the inverse image of Z within Zhat under the surjection of Remark 1.11.5 (i) for G_v(M^Theta_*), there is a functorial algorithm M^Theta_* -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*) := M_TM(M^Theta_*) within the same limit of H^1 with Pi_mu coefficients, a monoid of constants naturally isomorphic to O^{triangleright}_{F_v} (Example 1.8 (ii)), with a conjugation action by Pi_X(M^Theta_*).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • M^Theta_* = {... -> M^Theta_{M'} -> M^Theta_M -> ...} a projective system of mono-theta environments (Proposition 1.5, Corollary 2.8) with Pi_X(M^Theta_*) isomorphic to Pi_v

Conclusion.

(i) a functorial algorithm for the theta monoids Psi_env(M^Theta_*), infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*) and their splittings up to torsion; (ii) a functorial algorithm for the constant monoid Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), with conjugation actions by Pi_X(M^Theta_*).

(ii) Constant monoids: likewise an isomorphism Psi_{dagger C_v} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), defined up to an inner automorphism and compatible with the conjugation actions.

Kummer isomorphisms Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> Psi_env(M^Theta_*) (with infinity versions) and Psi_{dagger C_v} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*), each up to an inner automorphism, compatible with conjugation actions and splittings.

Group-theoretic theta monoids. Let dagger F_v be as in Proposition 3.3 and consider the full poly-isomorphism M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v) of projective systems of mono-theta environments (M^Theta_*(Pi_v) from Proposition 1.2 (i)). (i) Multiradiality of split theta monoids: each isomorphism induces compatible diagrams of isomorphisms Pi_v -> Pi_X(...) acting on infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) -> infinity-Psi_env(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)) -> infinity-Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} (and on Psi_env), and G_v acting on the unit groups Psi_env(...)^x -> (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^x, compatible with splittings up to torsion; with (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^{x mu} the quotient of the units by torsion, the functorial algorithms Pi_v -> Psi_env(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)), infinity-Psi_env (composing Propositions 1.2 (i), 3.1 (i)) are compatible with arbitrary automorphisms of the pair G_v(M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)) acting on (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^{x mu} that are Ism-multiples of automorphisms induced by automorphisms of the pair with (Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v})^x, so that Psi_R of Corollary 1.12 (iii) is multiradially defined. (ii) Uniradiality of constant monoids: each isomorphism induces analogous diagrams for Psi_cns and Psi_{dagger C_v}, but the algorithm Pi_v -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*(Pi_v)) depends on the cyclotomic rigidity of Corollary 1.11 (b) (through the surjection of Remark 1.11.5 (i) used in Proposition 3.1 (ii)), hence fails to be compatible with automorphisms of the pair G_v acting on (Psi_{dagger C_v})^{x mu} that arise from automorphisms of the pair with (Psi_{dagger C_v})^x; it only admits a uniradial formulation.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • dagger F_v a tempered Frobenioid as in Proposition 3.3
  • an isomorphism of projective systems of mono-theta environments M^Theta_*(Pi_v) -> M^Theta_*(dagger F_v)

Conclusion.

(i) The split theta monoid algorithms are compatible with Ism-multiples of automorphisms of the unit pair, so the theta monoids are multiradially defined; (ii) the constant monoid algorithm is not compatible with such automorphisms and only admits a uniradial formulation.

Significance of the symmetrizing isomorphisms of Corollary 3.5 (i). (i) Combinatorial model: for the ordered set E = {0, 1} with 0 < 1 and underlying unordered set S, Aut(S) = Z/2Z, a factorization of a construction F on ordered two-element sets through a construction F^sym(S) with Aut(S)-action is a collection of symmetrizing isomorphisms, i.e. descent data to the orbiset quotient, which never violates the bijection between E and S (though via an indeterminate bijection). The naive approach, collapsing to the coarse quotient Q = {*}, forces an Aut(S)-equivariant assignment of each s in S to all points of E_Q = {0_Q, 1_Q}, giving 4 possibilities, some not bijective; synchronizing them would need an automorphism of the order on E_Q swapping its two points, which cannot exist. This contrast of crushing E to a point versus symmetrizing without violating the bijection is the topic of [IUTchI] Remarks 4.9.2 (i), 6.12.4 (i), Fig. 4.5. (ii) Without an F_l^{x+-}-symmetry the single basepoint (Remark 2.6.1 (i)) rigidifies the labels as well as the conjugates; the symmetry eliminates this, allowing (a) symmetrizing isomorphisms, (b) a bijective link with the labels LabCusp^+-(Pi_X(M^Theta_*)), needed for Gaussian monoids with distinct values at distinct labels, (c) relative to a single basepoint, needed for conjugate synchronization. (iii) The symmetry arises from a Delta_X-outer action, conjugation by geometric rather than arithmetic elements, which is crucial for conjugate synchronization of the copies of G_v(M^Theta_*) ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.6 (ii)). (iv) Conjugate synchronization via symmetry is a nonarchimedean counterpart of conjugate synchronization via the connectedness of Gamma^{black-triangle}_X (Remarks 2.6.1 (i), 2.8.3). (v) Section 4 extends these ideas to the global portion and to good v of a D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater.

Conclusion.

Commentary: symmetrizing isomorphisms act as descent data preserving the bijection with labels, unlike collapsing labels; the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry gives (a), (b), (c) simultaneously.

Obligations.

On the diagram in the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii), summarized as Fig. 3.1 (Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids => group-theoretic theta monoids via Kummer, Galois evaluation down to group-theoretic Gaussian monoids, and 'forget' back to Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids). (i) The three portions correspond to Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting; forgetting yields post-anabelian monoids; the composite of Kummer and evaluation is a comparison isomorphism between Frobenius-like and etale-like structures, as in classical Hodge-Arakelov theory where the comparison isomorphism comes from evaluating theta functions and their derivatives at torsion points. (ii) Etale-like structures (etale or tempered fundamental groups) are invariant under non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters such as the Theta-link and the log-wall and are rigid via anabelian algorithms; Frobenius-like structures (abstract monoids) are not so rigidified, which allows such filters to be constructed; the two play complementary roles with respect to binding to conventional scheme theory (Fig. 3.2), and Kummer theory relates them within a Hodge theater. (iii) Composing the Theta-link qq_v -> Theta_v with the arrows of Fig. 3.1 gives the correspondence qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*}, a 'modified Theta-link', viewed as an abstract combinatorial Frobenius lifting, a homotopy between the identity qq_v -> qq_v and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; the exponents {j^2} are highly distinguished (Remark 2.6.3). (iv) Grothendieck Conjecture-type results in anabelian geometry are comparison isomorphisms between polynomial-function-theoretic and group-theoretic collections of morphisms, obtained by combining considerations particular to the situation with Galois evaluation via Kummer theory of polynomial functions or differential forms at rational points.

Conclusion.

Interpretation of the diagram of Corollary 3.6 (ii): Kummer, Galois evaluation and forgetting as in Fig. 3.1; the complementary roles of etale-like and Frobenius-like structures; the modified Theta-link qq_v -> {qq_v^{j^2}}_{1<=j<=l*} as a homotopy between the identity and qq_v -> qq_v^{(l*)^2}; Grothendieck Conjecture-type results as comparison isomorphisms.

IUT2.Rem3_6_3Remark 3.6.3
Record

Observations on basepoints for the non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters of Remark 3.6.2. (i) In the theory of etale fundamental groups the fiber functor of a basepoint is defined by points of a finite etale covering, valued in a separably closed field, over a fixed point of the base; over the spectrum of a field these are ring homomorphisms into a separably closed field, so the scheme-theoretic notion of basepoint depends essentially on ring/scheme structure. Consequently the distinct ring structures on either side of a non-ring/scheme-theoretic filter (the log-wall of [AbsTopIII], the Theta-link of [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7) give rise to distinct, unrelated basepoints ([AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.7 (i)). (ii) The same applies to N-th power morphisms (N > 1), the morphisms of Frobenius type of Frobenioids: in the tempered Frobenioids of [EtTh] Section 5 they induce N-th power morphisms between monoids isomorphic to O^triangleright_{K_v}, which fail to preserve the ring structure of K_v and so give distinct, unrelated basepoints on domain and codomain. Unlike (i), these take place compatibly with the projection functor to the base category of the Frobenioid, so the unrelated basepoints only give rise to inner automorphisms of the topological group determined by the base category; N-th power morphisms are milder, algebraic operations that fit into a single category (the tempered Frobenioid, definable via formal flat O_{K_v}-schemes, [EtTh] Section 1), whereas the log-wall and Theta-link are drastic, non-algebraic, and difficult to fit into a single category lying over the same base category (Remark 1.11.2 (ii); [AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.7). The study of the structures generated by the log-wall and Theta-link is a main theme of the series ([IUTchIII]).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Remark 3.6.2

Conclusion.

The log-wall and the Theta-link, being incompatible with ring structures, give distinct, unrelated basepoints on either side; N-th power morphisms of Frobenioids also give unrelated basepoints, but only up to inner automorphisms of the base group, because they are compatible with the projection to the base category.

Obligations.

  • Page 105: the claim that the unrelated basepoints of N-th power morphisms give only inner automorphisms of the base group is stated as a consequence of compatibility with the projection functor without a written argument. The rest is commentary on the scheme-theoretic definition of basepoints.

Explains why objects are known only up to isomorphism: Kummer N-th power morphisms respect multiplication but not addition, hence act as Frobenius-type morphisms between distinct ring structures, forcing the rigidity theory of [EtTh]. Galois evaluation is linear, so the first power of the theta function (and of its values) is the only power that crosses the mono-theta bridge; N-th powers for N > 1 are only defined as (-)^N of the first power, and other powers are not horizontal for the multiradial connection structure.

IUT2.Rem3_6_5Remark 3.6.5
Record

Philosophical observations on mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity. (i) A cyclotome is a kind of skeleton of the arithmetic holomorphic structure (Remark 1.11.6), motivated by the circle S^1 as skeleton of C^x at archimedean primes. (ii) The commutator structure [-,-] of the theta group (a) is central to mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity ([EtTh] Introduction, Remark 2.19.2) and (b) in the classical theory of algebraic theta functions implies irreducibility of certain representations of the theta group; both are instances of (c): the commutator structure embodies the coherence of holomorphic structures. In Hodge-Arakelov theory ([HASurI], [HASurII]) the irreducible representations among functions on l-torsion points are, for large l, discrete analogues of holomorphic functions among real analytic ones; conjugate synchronization (Remarks 3.5.2, 3.8.3), using the connected subgraph Gamma^triangle of Gamma_X (Remark 2.6.1 (i)), is a discretely parametrized coherence of arithmetic holomorphic structures, and mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity a continuously parametrized version supported on Y-double-dot_v; their interaction via restriction is central in the Galois evaluation of Corollaries 2.8 (i), 3.5 (ii), 3.6 (ii). (iii) With cyclotomes at localizations as local skeleta, mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity is a local uniformization of the number field (exterior cyclotome of Proposition 1.3 (i)) via a local portion (interior cyclotome) of the geometric tempered fundamental group Delta_v of a covering of X_F (Definition 2.3 (i); [IUTchI] Definition 3.1 (e)); it says the theta function from a mono-theta environment is free of Zhat^x-power indeterminacies, and constant multiple rigidity says the local uniformization is free of constant multiple indeterminacies. Analogies with p-adic Teichmuller theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5, [pTeich] Section 0.9): X_F corresponds to nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundles, local uniformizations to canonical coordinates, cyclotomic rigidity to the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism, Theta-links of the Frobenius-picture to transitions mod p^n to mod p^{n+1} of Witt vectors ([IUTchI] Section I4; [IUTchIII] Remark 1.4.1 (iii)), the multiradiality of Corollary 1.12 to the Frobenius invariance of canonical coordinates, and discrete rigidity of [EtTh] to canonical coordinates being power series rather than PD-formal power series; without discrete rigidity one would need Zhat-powers of U and q ([EtTh] Remarks 1.6.4, 2.19.4), analogous to O-hat-powers of canonical parameters requiring PD-formal power series ([pOrd] Chapter III).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Remark 3.6.4 and Section 1

Conclusion.

Mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity is interpreted as a continuously parametrized coherence of arithmetic holomorphic structures and as a local uniformization free of Zhat^x-power indeterminacies; constant multiple rigidity as freedom from constant multiple indeterminacies; discrete rigidity as analogous to canonical coordinates being genuine power series.

Obligations.

  • Philosophical commentary with analogies; the mathematical statements it interprets (cyclotomic, constant multiple and discrete rigidity) are those of [EtTh] and of Corollaries 1.10, 1.12.

What Section 3 gains from the conjugate synchronization of Section 2 (Remark 3.5.2), in three parts. (i) Direct technical consequences: (a) the isomorphisms of monoids Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t1|} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t2|}, (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t1|} -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t2|}, (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{|t|} -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{|t|}, for |t|, |t1|, |t2| in |F_l|, the third well defined up to an inner automorphism indeterminacy independent of |t| (Corollaries 3.5 (i), 3.6 (i)); (b) the well-defined diagonal submonoids Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<|F_l|>} in the product over |t| in |F_l| and Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} in the product over |t| in F_l^* (Corollary 3.5 (i)), and the diagonal embeddings of categories (constant distributions) of Definition 3.8 (iii); (c) the well-defined isomorphisms Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_0 -> Psi_cns(M^Theta_*)_{<F_l^*>} and (Psi_{dagger C_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger C_v})_{<F_l^*>} (Corollaries 3.5 (iii), 3.6 (iii)); (d) the restriction to units of the composite isomorphism Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v, alpha} -> Psi_{F_xi}(dagger F_v) of the third display of Corollary 3.6 (ii). (b), (c) are formal consequences of (a), and (d) is an alternate formulation of the units part of (a) for |t| in F_l^*. The main application (Section 4) of conjugate synchronization is the isomorphism of units of (d), composed with the Theta-link (coricity of O^x, [IUTchI] Corollary 3.7 (iii)); the isomorphisms of monoids in the Theta-link or in Corollary 3.6 (ii) make sense only for post-anabelian abstract monoids/Frobenioids (Frobenius-like structures). (ii) In [IUTchIII], etale-like versions of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta and Gaussian monoids able to penetrate the log-wall are constructed via Kummer theory, which uses the cyclotomes in the unit groups; this needs conjugate synchronization in an essential way: without it, by the unrelated basepoints on either side of the log-wall (Remark 3.6.3 (i)), one could only form diagonal embeddings of submonoids of Galois invariants or of sets of Galois orbits of the constant monoids Psi_cns, which are insufficient for Kummer theory ([IUTchIII] Remark 1.5.1 (ii)), and passing to Galois orbits is incompatible with the ring (additive) structure of the constant monoids (with {0} adjoined), which the log-wall requires within each Hodge theater (Remark 3.6.4 (i)). (iii) Conjugate synchronization and mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity (Remark 3.6.5 (ii)) are instances of the theme of explicitly describing one arithmetic holomorphic structure from another related only by a mono-analytic core; classically the natural isomorphisms between cyclotomes are taken for granted, with no explicit intrinsic reconstruction algorithms.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollaries 3.5, 3.6 and Definition 3.8

Conclusion.

Conjugate synchronization yields the isomorphisms (a) to (d), of which (b), (c) are formal consequences of (a) and (d) is a reformulation of the units part of (a); its main use is the isomorphism of units (d) composed with the Theta-link, and it is essential for the Kummer theory needed to pass the log-wall, since Galois invariants or orbits are insufficient and incompatible with ring structure.

Frobenioid-theoretic Gaussian monoids at archimedean v. With the notation of Proposition 4.3, dagger F_v = (dagger C_v, dagger D_v, dagger kappa_v) the data at v in V^arc of a Theta-Hodge theater dagger HT^Theta, dagger F^vdash_v = (dagger C^vdash_v, dagger D^vdash_v, dagger tau^vdash_v) the data at v of the associated F^vdash-prime-strip, dagger U_v := dagger D_v and dagger U^{+-}_v, dagger U^cor_v the corresponding Aut-holomorphic orbispaces. (i) (Constant monoids) The Kummer structure dagger kappa_v: Psi_{dagger F_v} := O^triangleright(dagger C_v) -> A_{dagger D_v} and the tautological equality dagger D_v = dagger U_v determine a unique isomorphism of topological monoids Psi_{dagger F_v} -> Psi_cns(dagger U_v). (ii) (Mono-analytic semi-simplifications) With Psi_{dagger F^vdash_v} := O^triangleright(dagger C^vdash_v), there is a unique {+-1}-orbit of isomorphisms of topological groups Psi^x_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi_cns(dagger D^vdash_v)^x and a unique isomorphism of monoids Psi^R_{dagger F^vdash_v} := Psi_{dagger F^vdash_v}/Psi^x_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi^R_cns(dagger D^vdash_v) = R_{>=0}(dagger D^vdash_v) sending the distinguished element determined by p_v = e = 2.71828... (the element whose natural logarithm is 1) to log^{dagger D^vdash_v}(p_v); with Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} := Psi^x x Psi^R, these give a natural poly-isomorphism Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} -> Psi^ss_cns(dagger D^vdash_v) compatible with the splittings, and Psi^ss_{dagger F_v} := Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v} gives a natural isomorphism Psi^ss_{dagger F_v} -> Psi^ss_{dagger F^vdash_v}. (iii) (Labels, F_l^{x+-}-symmetries, conjugate synchronization) The isomorphism of (i) determines, for each t in LabCusp^{+-}(dagger U_v), compatible isomorphisms (Psi_{dagger F_v})_t -> Psi_cns(dagger U_v)_t and F_l^{x+-}-symmetrizing isomorphisms (from F_l^{x+-} = Gal(dagger U^{+-}_v/dagger U^cor_v) acting on the Gal(dagger U_v/dagger U^{+-}_v)-orbits of cusps) between data indexed by distinct t, determining diagonal submonoids and an isomorphism (Psi_{dagger F_v})_0 -> (Psi_{dagger F_v})_{<F_l^*>}. (iv) (Theta and Gaussian monoids) The monoids Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v}, Psi_{F_gau}(dagger F_v) with natural splittings, determined via (i) to (iii) by Psi_env(dagger U_v), Psi_gau(dagger U_v) of Proposition 4.3 (iv), come with natural isomorphisms Psi_{dagger F^Theta_v} -> Psi_env(dagger U_v) -> Psi_gau(dagger U_v) -> Psi_{F_gau}(dagger F_v) that restrict to the identity or to (the restriction to units of) the isomorphism of (i) or its inverse on the copies of Psi^x_{dagger F_v}, Psi_cns(dagger U_v)^x, and are compatible with the natural splittings.

Group-theoretic monoids associated to base-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theaters. Five functorial algorithms: (i) constant monoids from a D-prime-strip; (ii) mono-analytic semi-simplifications and a global realified Frobenioid from its mono-analyticization; (iii) labels, F_l^{x+-}-symmetries and conjugate synchronization; (iv) local theta and Gaussian monoids with evaluation isomorphisms; (v) global realified theta and Gaussian Frobenioids D_env, D_gau and a global formal evaluation isomorphism.

  • the mono-analyticization double-dagger D^{|-} ([IUTchI] Definition 4.1 (iv)) with double-dagger D^{|-}_v = B^temp(double-dagger G_v)^0 for v in V^non

Conclusion.

Significance of the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry giving the symmetrizing isomorphisms of Corollary 4.5 (iii) (Remark 3.5.2). (i) Conjugate synchronization (Corollaries 3.5 (i), 4.5 (iii); Propositions 4.1 (iii), 4.3 (iii)) is possible for the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry but not for the F_l^*-symmetry precisely because of the connectedness, at each v, of the local components involved (Remarks 2.6.1 (i), 2.6.2 (i), 3.5.2 (ii); [IUTchI] Remark 6.12.4 (i), (ii)); similar, easier remarks hold at good v. A related property, not shared by F_l^*, is the geometric nature of the automorphisms giving the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (Remark 3.5.2 (iii)). (ii) Comparison of the single-basepoint symmetrizing isomorphisms with multi-basepoint symmetries (Remarks 3.5.3, 4.5.2 (ii)): (a) unlike mono-analytic capsules/processions, the ring structure (arithmetic holomorphic structure) stays intact, which is essential for the log-wall (Remark 3.6.4 (i); [IUTchIII]); (b) unlike holomorphic capsules/processions, the single basepoint gives conjugate synchronization and a bijective link with the labels LabCusp^{+-}(-) (Remark 3.5.2), both crucial for Galois-theoretic theta evaluation (Corollaries 3.5, 3.6; Remark 3.8.3); (c) the F_l^{x+-}-symmetries of D-Theta^ell-bridges keep a bijective link with LabCusp^{+-}(-) ([IUTchI] Remarks 4.9.2 (i), 6.12.4 (i)) but, being multi-basepoint, do not give conjugate synchronization. (iii) Gluing the local F_l^{x+-}-symmetries of Corollary 3.5 (i) and Propositions 4.1 (iii), 4.3 (iii) into the global F_l^{x+-}-symmetry of Corollary 4.5 (iii) requires the global portion dagger D^{circledcirc +-} of the D-Theta^{+-ell}-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Proposition 6.5, Remark 6.12.4 (iii)), which synchronizes the +- indeterminacies at each v; this is the content of [IUTchI] Proposition 6.5, and these local +- indeterminacies are an important cause of the profinite conjugacy (Delta-hat-conjugacy) indeterminacies of Corollaries 2.4, 2.5 (Remark 2.5.2), hence of the need for the complements on tempered coverings of [IUTchI] Section 2 in the proof of Corollary 2.4.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollary 4.5 and of Sections 2, 3

Conclusion.

Conjugate synchronization holds for the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (single basepoint, connected local components, geometric automorphisms) and not for the F_l^*-symmetry; it keeps the ring structure and the bijective link with labels; the global F_l^{x+-}-symmetry needs the global portion dagger D^{circledcirc +-} to synchronize the local +- indeterminacies.

IUT2.Rem4_7_2Remark 4.7.2
Record

In the context of Corollary 4.7 (ii): unlike the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, the F_l^*-symmetry does not allow the conjugate synchronization of Corollary 4.5 (iii), since it arises from conjugation by elements with nontrivial image in the arithmetic portion (the absolute Galois group of the base field) of the global arithmetic fundamental groups (Remarks 3.5.2 (iii), 4.5.3 (i); Remark 2.5.2 (iii) on G_K-conjugacy indeterminacies giving G_v-conjugacy indeterminacies). This forces Corollary 4.7 (ii) to work with (a) F-prime-strips rather than ind-topological monoids with Galois actions, and (b) objects of Corollary 4.7 (i) with sub- or superscripts mod, sol, kappa-sol, infinity-kappa (F_mod, F_sol, pi_1^{kappa-sol}(-), infinity-kappa-coric rational functions), or (as for pi_1^{rat/kappa-sol}(-)) objects defined only up to certain conjugacy indeterminacies. Both let one ignore the independent, non-synchronizable conjugacy indeterminacies at distinct labels arising from the single basepoint (Remark 3.5.2 (ii)). With the objects marked mod, sol or kappa-sol, on which the conjugacy indeterminacies act in a synchronized way, the diagonal subcategories of the Frobenioids can be built without the subtleties of independent indeterminacies at distinct labels (Remark 3.8.3 (ii)). In [IUTchIII] the ring structure on the objects with subscript mod serves as a translation apparatus between boxplus-line bundles (additive) and boxtimes-line bundles (multiplicative, as in Frobenioids) ([AbsTopIII] Definition 5.3 (i), (ii)).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollary 4.7

Conclusion.

Conjugate synchronization is impossible for the F_l^*-symmetry, because it arises from conjugation by elements with nontrivial image in the absolute Galois group of the base field; therefore Corollary 4.7 (ii) works with F-prime-strips and with objects (mod, sol, kappa-sol, infinity-kappa) on which conjugacy indeterminacies are synchronized or which are defined only up to conjugacy.

Obligations.

  • Page 143: the impossibility of conjugate synchronization for the F_l^*-symmetry is recalled from Remarks 3.5.2 (iii) and 4.5.3 (i) and is not proved; no precise statement of 'impossible' is given.

IUT2.Rem4_7_3Remark 4.7.3
Record

F_l^{x+-} versus F_l*-symmetry: F_l approximates Z; F_l^{x+-} corresponds to addition, involves the zero label and units, and is applied for conjugate synchronization (uniradial, but coric after mono-analyticization); F_l* corresponds to multiplication, separates the zero label, describes the Gaussian monoids as functions of j in F_l*, and is multiradial. Volumes at each j in F_l* are given weight 1/l* so that the diagonal constant distribution has weight 1.

Conclusion.

F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (additive, with the zero label, used for conjugate synchronization) and F_l*-symmetry (multiplicative, separating the zero label, used for the Gaussian monoids as functions of j) play different roles; the volume at each j in F_l* gets weight 1/l*, so the diagonal constant distribution has total weight 1.

Obligations.

Combinatorial models of the uniradiality of the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry and the multiradiality of the F_l^*-symmetry (Remark 4.7.3 (ii), (iii)). (i) Relative to an arithmetic holomorphic structure (a Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, [IUTchI] Definition 6.13 (i)), the etale-picture of each symmetry ([IUTchI] Corollaries 4.12, 6.10) is a collection of copies of F_l (respectively |F_l| = F_l^* union {0}), one per arithmetic holomorphic structure (spoke alpha), glued at the coric label 0, each with an action of a copy of F_l^{x+-} (respectively F_l^*) (Figs. 4.1, 4.2). (ii) (a) For F_l^{x+-} the actions on distinct spokes fail to commute; (b) for F_l^* they commute and are compatible with the permutations of spokes ([IUTchI] Corollary 4.12 (iii)). The noncommutativity (incompatibility with simultaneous execution at distinct spokes, Remark 1.9.1) is a direct consequence of including the zero label in the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry, a prototypical combinatorial representation of uniradiality; the commutativity follows from excluding the zero label from F_l^*, a prototype of multiradiality; and for F_l^{x+-}, invariance under the actions on all spokes is a kind of uniformity, hence coricity (Remark 4.7.3 (ii)). (iii) A formulation as radial environments (Example 1.7 (ii)): coric data are objects 0_alpha, with exactly one arrow (alpha, beta) from 0_alpha to 0_beta; radial data are copies (F_l)_alpha (respectively |F_l|_alpha), and the set of arrows (F_l)_alpha -> (F_l)_beta (respectively |F_l|_alpha -> |F_l|_beta) has exactly one element if the actions of (F_l^{x+-})_gamma on (F_l)_gamma (respectively (F_l^*)_gamma on |F_l|_gamma), gamma = alpha, beta, determine an action of (F_l^{x+-})_alpha x (F_l^{x+-})_beta (respectively (F_l^*)_alpha x (F_l^*)_beta) on the coproduct (F_l)_alpha coprod_0 (F_l)_beta (respectively for |F_l|) obtained by identifying 0_alpha and 0_beta, and is empty otherwise; the radial functor sends (F_l)_alpha to 0_alpha (respectively |F_l|_alpha to 0_alpha). The resulting radial environment is said to be easily seen to be uniradial (respectively multiradial); details left to the reader. The product formulation recalls the switching functor of Example 1.7 (iii) and parallel transport (Remark 1.7.1).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Remark 4.7.3; F_l^{x+-} acting on F_l and F_l^* acting on |F_l| as in [IUTchI] (not redefined on these pages)

Conclusion.

(ii) The F_l^{x+-}-actions on distinct spokes of the etale-picture fail to commute (uniradiality), while the F_l^-actions commute and are compatible with permutations of spokes (multiradiality); (iii) the combinatorial radial environment built from these actions is uniradial for F_l^{x+-} and multiradial for F_l^.

IUT2.Rem4_7_5Remark 4.7.5
Record

The F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries correspond to the additive and multiplicative structures of F_l, a finite approximation of Z (Remark 4.7.3 (i)): (a) to the two combinatorial dimensions, addition and multiplication, of a ring ([AbsTopIII] Section I3); (b) to the units and value group of a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean or complex archimedean local field; or (c) to the two cohomological dimensions of the absolute Galois group of a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field, or the two real dimensions of a complex archimedean field. The hierarchy of these dimensions (multiplication piled on addition) is reflected in (d) the subordination structure (nonzero labels <<< zero label) for weighted volumes (Remark 4.7.3 (iii)), and (e) in the fact that the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry arises from conjugation by the geometric fundamental group (Remarks 3.5.2 (iii), 4.5.3 (i)) and the F_l^*-symmetry from conjugation by the absolute Galois group of the global base field (Remark 4.7.2), the arithmetic fundamental groups having a hierarchical extension structure.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Remarks 4.7.3, 4.7.4

Conclusion.

The two symmetries are interpreted as the additive and multiplicative dimensions of a ring, with corresponding interpretations (units and value group; cohomological or real dimensions), and their hierarchy appears in the subordination of nonzero to zero labels and in the geometric versus arithmetic origin of the symmetries.

Obligations.

  • Interpretive commentary; the statement in (e) about the origin of the symmetries is recalled from the cited remarks.

In the context of Corollary 4.7 (i), non-realified global Frobenioids (corresponding to F_mod) make sense only for the F_l^*-symmetry. To treat F_mod anabelianly one needs the full profinite group Pi_{C_F}, not only its open subgroups Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} (underlined) giving the global portions of the F_l^*- and F_l^{x+-}-symmetries ([IUTchI] Definitions 4.1 (v), 6.1 (v)); for the abstract topological group Pi_{C_F} these subgroups are well defined only up to Pi_{C_F}-conjugacy, i.e. up to automorphisms from their normalizers in Pi_{C_F} ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.6 (iii), (iv)), so they are subject to indeterminacies from the natural F_l^*-poly-actions ([IUTchI] Example 4.3 (iv)), i.e. the natural F_l^*-symmetries. One cannot form the quotient by this indeterminacy, since this would give label-crushing, identifying the distinct labels j in F_l^* that are crucial for the Gaussian monoids ([IUTchI] Remark 4.7.1). Then the F_l^*-symmetries of Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} necessarily involve conjugation by elements of the absolute Galois groups of the global base fields, hence are fundamentally incompatible with conjugate synchronization (Remark 4.7.2). So one must (a) isolate the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry from the F_l^*-symmetry to establish conjugate synchronization and (b) isolate the F_l^*-symmetry from the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry to work with Galois-theoretic representations of the global base field F_mod: the dismantling of the two a priori intertwined combinatorial dimensions of a ring (Remarks 4.7.3, 4.7.5; [AbsTopIII] Section I3).

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Corollary 4.7 (i)

Conclusion.

Non-realified global Frobenioids such as F_mod are available only with the F_l^-symmetry; working with the abstract group Pi_{C_F} subjects Pi_{C_K}, Pi_{X_K} to F_l^-indeterminacies that cannot be quotiented out without label-crushing and are incompatible with conjugate synchronization, so the two symmetries must be isolated from each other.

Obligations.

  • Page 148: the claim that non-realified global Frobenioids make sense only for the F_l^*-symmetry is supported by the discussion of Pi_{C_F}-conjugacy but not proved; the incompatibility with conjugate synchronization (page 149) rests on Remark 4.7.2.

(i) The realified localization functor of Remark 4.8.1 (iii) concerns only the realification of F_gau(dagger HT^Theta); the unit portion of the Gaussian monoids is used in the log-wall theory of IUT III as an additive object via log, the non-realified global Frobenioids of Corollary 4.8 (i) serving as a translation apparatus between multiplicative and additive line bundles (Remark 4.7.2); this depends essentially on the natural splittings of the Gaussian monoids (Corollary 4.6 (iv); Remark 1.12.2 (iv)). (ii) That these non-realified Frobenioids appear only with the F_l^*-symmetry (Remark 4.7.6) is no obstacle, since Gaussian monoids are naturally functions of j in F_l^* (Remark 4.7.3 (iii)). (iii) In the analogy with p-adic Teichmuller theory ([AbsTopIII] Section I5), log-shifted units with non-log-shifted value groups resemble writing an indigenous bundle with Hodge filtration 0 -> omega -> E -> tau -> 0 as a direct sum Phi^* tau + omega under Frobenius liftings, Phi corresponding to log.

Kummer structures and prime-strips. (i) For a Frobenioid C whose base category D is isomorphic to the connected finite etale coverings of the spectrum of an MLF or a CAF, and a universal covering pro-object A of D with G := Aut(A), evaluating O^{triangleright}(-) ([FrdI] Proposition 2.2) at A gives G acting on O^{triangleright}(A), with mu_N(A) within O^mu(A) within O^x(A) and quotients O^x(A) -> O^{x mu_N}(A) -> O^{x mu}(A). For G nontrivial (the MLF case), a x-Kummer structure (respectively x mu-Kummer structure) on C is a Zhat^x-orbit (respectively Ism-orbit) of isomorphisms of ind-topological G-modules kappa^x: O^x(G) -> O^x(A) (respectively kappa^{x mu}: O^{x mu}(G) -> O^{x mu}(A)), independent of the choice of A; any x-Kummer structure is unique (Remark 1.11.1 (b)); a x mu-Kummer structure determines and is determined by the submodules I^kappa_H(A) := Im(O^x(G)^H) within O^{x mu}(A) for open H within G. (Split-)Kummer Frobenioids are (split) Frobenioids with such a structure. (ii) For an F^{|-}-prime-strip double-dagger F^{|-} and w in V^bad, double-dagger F^{|-}_w is split with base category double-dagger D^{|-}_w; the 2l-torsion mu_{2l} of O^x and the images of the splittings generate O^perp within O^{triangleright}, O^{black-triangle} := O^perp / mu_{2l} (so O^{triangleright}/O^x -> O^{black-triangle}), and O^{black-triangle x mu} := O^{black-triangle} x O^{x mu}; Remark 1.11.1 (b) gives a unique Zhat^x-orbit kappa^{|- x}_w: O^x(double-dagger G) -> O^x(double-dagger A), inducing an Ism-orbit kappa^{|- x mu}_w. (iii) The rational function monoid of O^{black-triangle x mu} with the divisor monoid of double-dagger F^{|-}_w gives a split model Frobenioid ([FrdI] Theorem 5.2 (ii)) with a x mu-Kummer structure, written double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_w; double-dagger F^{|-}_w also denotes the split-Kummer Frobenioid with the x-Kummer structure. (iv) For w in V^good intersected with V^non, the same with O^{black-triangle} := O^perp (no quotient by mu_{2l}). (v) For w in V^arc, double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_w replaces the split Frobenioid by the inductive system of its quotients by N-torsion, N in a cofinal subset of N>=1, with compatible surjections (double-dagger D^{|-}_w)^x -> O^{x mu_N}(A) defined up to the nontrivial automorphism of (double-dagger D^{|-}_w)^x, a sort of Kummer structure. (vi) double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu} := {double-dagger F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_v}_{v in V} from (iii), (iv), (v); replacing split Frobenioids by those with trivial splittings (subcategories of isometries, [FrdI] Theorem 5.1 (iii), [FrdII] Example 3.3 (iii)) gives double-dagger F^{|- x} and double-dagger F^{|- x mu}, split-x- and split-x mu-Kummer Frobenioids at v in V^non. (vii) For |-box in {|-x, |-x mu, |-black-triangle x mu}, an F^{|-box}-prime-strip is a collection {*F^{|-box}_v}_{v in V} with each member isomorphic to double-dagger F^{|-box}_v; morphisms are collections of isomorphisms indexed by V. (viii) An F^{||- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strip is *F^{||- black-triangle x mu} = (*C^{||-}, Prime(*C^{||-}) -> V, *F^{|- black-triangle x mu}, {*rho_v}_{v in V}) satisfying (a) to (f) of [IUTchI] Definition 5.2 (iv) with the F^{|-}-prime-strip replaced by an F^{|- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strip; the generators of the monoids O^{black-triangle}(-) (each abstractly isomorphic to N) at v in V^bad (nonempty), with the rho_w, determine up to isomorphism an object of the global realified Frobenioid *C^{||-} of negative arithmetic degree, the pilot object; morphisms are isomorphisms of the data.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • For (i): C a Frobenioid with base category isomorphic to the finite etale coverings of Spec of an MLF or CAF
  • For (ii) to (viii): double-dagger F^{|-} = {double-dagger F^{|-}v}{v in V} an F^{|-}-prime-strip relative to the initial Theta-data

Conclusion.

Definition (no proof obligation): x- and x mu-Kummer structures and Kummer Frobenioids; the split-Kummer Frobenioids F^{|- black-triangle x mu}_v; F^{|-x}-, F^{|-x mu}-, F^{|- black-triangle x mu}- and F^{||- black-triangle x mu}-prime-strips with their morphisms; the pilot object.
