IUT2.Rem4_11_2Remark 4.11.2
Record

Summary of the theory so far, in four parts. (i) A Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Definition 6.13 (i)) is a model of conventional scheme-theoretic arithmetic geometry around the theta function at primes of bad reduction in V^bad of the elliptic curve; it is a bridge between the number field and theta functions, realized by the Gaussian distribution, a globalized version of the theta values {q_v^{j^2}}, 1 <= j <= l^*, at l-torsion points (Remark 3.6.2 (iii); the value at label j is the mu_{2l}-orbit of q_v^{j^2} with q_v the chosen 2l-th root of the Tate parameter, Remark 2.5.1 (i)); 'Gaussian distribution' informally includes Gaussian monoids and Gaussian Frobenioids; it allows the non-scheme/ring-theoretic Theta^{x mu}_gau-link between distinct Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theaters (Corollary 4.10 (iii)). (ii) Within one Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater, the theta functions of [EtTh] give a single connected geometric Kummer theory-compatible theater for evaluating the theta function; its etale realization has a multiradial formulation (Section 1, Corollary 1.12), and its connectedness gives conjugate synchronization between the copies of the absolute Galois group of the base field at the evaluation points (Remark 2.6.1), compatible with the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry (Remark 3.5.2; Corollaries 4.5 (iii), 4.6 (iii)) of the D-Theta^ell-bridge ([IUTchI] Proposition 6.8 (i)); conjugate synchronization is essential for the coricity of the units (Corollary 4.10 (iv)) compatibly with the anabelian (etale) and post-anabelian (Frobenioid) representations of the Gaussian monoids (Remark 3.8.3); the post-anabelian representation is needed for the Theta^{x mu}_gau-link (Remarks 3.6.2 (ii), 3.8.3 (i)), the anabelian one for the log-wall in [IUTchIII] (Remark 3.8.3 (ii)); the canonical splittings into unit and value group components at bad v correspond to the non-deformed and Teichmuller-dilated real dimensions of complex Teichmuller theory (Remark 4.10.3 (i), (ii)) and are crucial for log-shells. (iii) The number fields of the underlying ThetaNF-Hodge theater ([IUTchI] Section 5) will relate, via their ring structure, boxtimes-line bundles to boxplus-line bundles (Remark 4.7.2), which needs all primes ([AbsTopIII] Remark 5.10.2 (iv)); such constructions are compatible with the F_l^*-symmetry ([IUTchI] Proposition 4.9 (i)), which is combinatorially multiradial and associated with value groups, while the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry is combinatorially uniradial and associated with units (Remarks 4.7.3 to 4.7.5); the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry is compatible with conjugate synchronization, which can only be established after isolating the prime-strips from the conjugacy indeterminacies inherent in the global absolute Galois group (Remark 4.7.2), i.e. free of the combinatorial constraints of the prime-trees ([IUTchI] Remark 4.3.1). Both symmetries share connectedness of the global objects of their Theta^ell- and NF-bridges, essential for bookkeeping of the labels of evaluation points (Remarks 3.5.2, 4.5.3 (iii); [IUTchI] Remark 4.9.2 (i)), which cannot be done with formal products of local objects instead of a global number field ([AbsTopIII] Remark 3.7.6 (v)); with the profinite global geometric fundamental groups this requires the complements on tempered coverings of [IUTchI] Section 2 (Remark 4.5.3 (iii)). (iv) The Gaussian-distribution bridge is built by dismantling the characteristic topography obstructing the relation of theta functions to number fields: for theta functions, the geometric dimension of the tempered coverings at bad v, resolved by evaluation at l-torsion points (a rough finite approximation, [HASurI] Section 1.3.4); for number fields, the prime-trees that give conjugacy indeterminacies obstructing conjugate synchronization, resolved by working with prime-strips labeled by F_l^* ([IUTchI] Remark 4.3.1); combinatorially this is dismantling the ring F_l, a rough finite approximation of Z ([IUTchI] Remark 6.12.3 (i)), into its additive and multiplicative parts, the F_l^{x+-}- and F_l^*-symmetries.

Implicit hypotheses.

  • The setting of Sections 1 to 4 and of [IUTchI]

Conclusion.

A Theta^{+-ell}NF-Hodge theater bridges number fields and theta functions through the Gaussian distribution of theta values q_v^{j^2} at l-torsion points; conjugate synchronization (from connectedness and the F_l^{x+-}-symmetry) gives coricity of units; the F_l^*-symmetry is compatible with the global ring structure; the bridge is built by dismantling the geometric dimension (via evaluation) and the prime-trees (via labeled prime-strips), i.e. the additive and multiplicative parts of F_l.

Obligations.

  • Summary commentary; the assertions it summarizes are those of the cited corollaries and remarks, whose records carry the corresponding statuses.

Ambiguities.

This juggling of boxplus and boxtimes is a combinatorial counterpart of the juggling of boxplus and boxtimes in the theory of the log-wall ([AbsTopIII] Section I3).

Conclusion.

The combinatorial correspondences (Theta^ell with addition, NF with multiplication) are reversed at the level of line bundles (Theta^ell with multiplicative, boxtimes, line bundles; NF with boxplus via the global ring structure); this is a combinatorial counterpart of the log-wall.

    (i) In scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory the l-torsion points of an elliptic curve are a rough finite approximation of the two real dimensions of the underlying one-dimensional complex torus ([HASurI] Section 1.3.4), corresponding to a holomorphic dimension and a one-dimensional deformation of it ([HASurI] Section 1.4.2). The present theory works with an elliptic curve isogenous to the given one by an isogeny of degree l (X underlined rather than X), so the holomorphic dimension can be neglected and one concentrates on its deformations ([EtTh] Introduction): the possible values at the l-torsion evaluation points are possible deformations of the holomorphic structure and the specific theta values a specific deformation. The parameter 0 != t in LabCusp^{+-}(-) indexing these values, linear in the group structure like the tangent space of the elliptic curve, descends (especially for the ThetaNF-Hodge theater) to j in F_l^*, a kind of square (F_l^x)^2 of F_l^x, hence quadratic like the square of the tangent space, naturally isomorphic to the tangent space of the moduli space of elliptic curves at the given curve. As in Remark 3.6.2 (iii), in the context of the Theta^{x mu}_gau-link the theta values are a deformation between the identity and a Frobenius morphism, and the theta function a continuous version of it.

    Implicit hypotheses.

    • The setting of Remark 4.11.2

    Conclusion.

    Theta values at l-torsion points are interpreted as a specific deformation of the holomorphic structure; the label j in F_l^* is quadratic in t, like the square of the tangent space, i.e. the tangent space of the moduli of elliptic curves.

    Obligations.

Introductory version of Theorem 3.11 (multiradial algorithms for LGP-monoids). For distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, with n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Theorem 1.5 (i)): (i) the multiradial representation n,◦R^LGP, consisting of (a) tensor packets of log-shells, (b) splitting monoids of LGP-monoids acting on them, (c) copies labeled by j ∈ F*_l of the number field F_mod acting on them, regarded up to the indeterminacies (Ind1) (automorphisms of the procession Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T)) and (Ind2) (the non-(Ind1) portion arising from automorphisms of the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips in the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link, at v ∈ V^non the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on local copies of O^{×μ}), is constructed by an algorithm in Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T), functorial for isomorphisms of processions, and the permutation symmetries of the étale-picture induce compatible poly-isomorphisms Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T) ≅ Prc(n',◦D^⊢_T), n,◦R^LGP ≅ n',◦R^LGP, compatible with the bi-coricity poly-isomorphisms n,◦D^⊢_0 ≅ n',◦D^⊢_0; (ii) the log-Kummer correspondence: inverse Kummer isomorphisms between (a), (b), (c) and the Frobenioid-theoretic data of each n,mHT, mutually compatible as m varies for (b) and (c) up to roots of unity, and for (a) only upper semi-compatible (Ind3), but precisely compatible with log-volumes; (iii) compatibility of the Kummer isomorphisms with the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links, up to (Ind2).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1
  • a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data, thought of as arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii))

IUT3.Rem1_1_1Remark 1.1.1
Record

(i) log-links are correspondences between portions of the ind-topological monoids in their domain and codomain; in iterates of log-links these correspondences are understood as defined only on the local units in the domains. For a global number field embedded in an idèlic product, the log-links are defined only on the product of the groups of local units. The only reason for introducing log-links is the construction of log-shells from the local units, which does not use the local or global value group portions. (ii) At v ∈ V^arc, the local units are regarded as 'Aut-holomorphic semi-germs': projective systems of arbitrarily small neighborhoods of S^1 in C^× (O^×(C_v) in O^▷(C_v)^gp), with the restricted Aut-holomorphic structure, the restricted group germ, and a choice of one of the two connected components of the complement of the units in a small neighborhood.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • for (i): iterates of log-links as in Definition 1.1
  • for (ii): v ∈ V^arc, in the notation of IUTchI, Example 3.4 (i) and Remark 3.4.2

Conclusion.

(i) A convention: log-links in iterates are defined only on local units, and on products of local unit groups in the idèlic setting. (ii) Aut-holomorphic semi-germs are rigid: they admit no nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms ('one verifies immediately', page 29); hence the approach to Kummer structures via Aut-holomorphic structures and co-holomorphicizations of IUTchI, Remark 3.4.2, carries over without change (AbsTopIII, Corollary 2.3 (i)); by the discreteness of the image of the units of a number field under the logarithms of the archimedean valuations ([Lang], page 144, Theorem 5), the idèlic aspects of (i) are unaffected.

Obligations.

  • Define Aut-holomorphic semi-germs precisely (a germ of neighborhoods of S^1 in C^× with the induced holomorphic structure up to Aut, group germ and choice of component) and prove that they admit no nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms (page 29: 'one verifies immediately'; no argument is given).
  • The discreteness of the logarithmic image of the unit group of a number field is the Dirichlet unit theorem setting; Mathlib has the logarithmic embedding of units (NumberField.Units), which may cover the cited fact.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 29: the rigidity statement 'do not admit any nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms' does not say whether automorphisms must preserve the chosen connected component and the group germ; the list on page 29 suggests all four data are preserved.

IUT3.Rem1_1_2Remark 1.1.2
Record

(i) For the tautological log-link †F_v → log(†F_v) of Definition 1.1 (i) there is a tautological identification between the †Π_v's in the data giving rise to its domain and codomain; for the full log-link †F_v → ‡F_v, †Π_v and ‡Π_v are related only by a full poly-isomorphism. The specific isomorphism of the tautological log-link is a 'rigidifying path' constructed using the Frobenius-like monoids related by the p_v-adic logarithm (Galois-equivariance of its power series). 'Path' is meant as in the étale groupoid, but allowing arbitrary automorphism indeterminacies. The paper works mainly with the full log-link, because the multiradial algorithms of §3 must express the relation between the étale-like Π_v's in purely étale-like terms, free of dependence on Frobenius-like monoids; this is achieved by the 'tautologically indeterminate isomorphism' underlying the full log-link. (ii) An analogous discussion applies for v ∈ V^arc (Definition 1.1 (ii)); routine details are left to the reader.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Definition 1.1 (i) (for (i)) and Definition 1.1 (ii), v ∈ V^arc (for (ii))

Conclusion.

(i) The full log-link relates †Π_v and ‡Π_v only up to a full poly-isomorphism, whereas the tautological log-link carries a specific isomorphism depending on Frobenius-like monoids; the full log-link is the one used in the paper, so that the relation between domain and codomain Π_v's is free of any dependence on Frobenius-like monoids. (ii) The same holds at v ∈ V^arc (details left to the reader, page 30).

Obligations.

  • Formalize the difference between the two links as: the tautological link carries one distinguished isomorphism of the Π_v's, the full link carries the full poly-isomorphism (the set of all isomorphisms).

Ambiguities.

  • Page 30: for v ∈ V^arc 'we leave the routine details to the reader'; the archimedean analogue is not written out.

(i) the log-link induces poly-isomorphisms †D ≅ ‡D, †D^⊢ ≅ ‡D^⊢ and Ψ_cns(†D) ≅ Ψ_cns(‡D); (ii) the diagrams are compatible with the ring structures on both ends; (iii) they are compatible with p_v-adic, angular and radial log-volumes; (iv) the Kummer isomorphisms are not compatible with the poly-isomorphism of (i); (v) holomorphic log-shells are compact, of finite log-volume, and contain the stated invariant submonoids; (vi), (vii) mono-analytic log-shells are constructible from D^⊢_v, with compatible (poly-)isomorphisms to the holomorphic ones; (viii) these assemble over V; (ix) for the full log-link from F(*D) to itself there is an algorithm in *D giving coric holomorphic log-shells; (x) a Z-chain of full log-links gives chains of full poly-isomorphisms of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, the Frobenius-picture, with a Z-translation symmetry and no arbitrary permutation symmetries. Statements in the part records.

Ambiguities.

IUT3.Rem1_2_1Remark 1.2.1
Record

(i) In the situation of Definition 1.1 (ii), Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N} carries the metric descended from Ψ^gp but is given weight N, so its log-volume equals that of Ψ^×. (ii) The archimedean compatibility of Proposition 1.2 (iii) between angular and radial log-volumes can be read as invariance of metrics: on a complex archimedean field k, metrics (Riemannian, compatible with both almost complex structures, translation invariant) form an R_{>0}-torsor, and via k^× ≅ O^×_k × R_{>0} any metric is determined by its restriction to O^×_k or to R_{>0}.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • for (i): the situation of IUT3.Def1_1.ii, N ∈ N_{≥1}
  • for (ii): a complex archimedean field k

Conclusion.

(i) A convention: the weight N makes log-volumes on Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N} agree with those on Ψ^×, so passing to the quotient does not affect log-volume computations. (ii) Any metric on k (in the stated sense) is uniquely determined by its restriction to O^×k ⊆ k or to R{>0} ⊆ k; hence the compatibility of Proposition 1.2 (iii) is equivalent to invariance of the natural metrics under the log-link.

Obligations.

  • Prove that translation-invariant Riemannian metrics on C compatible with both complex structures form an R_{>0}-torsor and are determined by their restriction to the unit circle or to R_{>0} (stated on page 35 as verified 'immediately'). This is elementary and within reach of Mathlib.

Ambiguities.

  • 'Compatible with the two natural almost complex structures' (page 35) is not defined further; the natural reading is that the metric is Hermitian for both i and −i, which for a translation-invariant metric means a positive multiple of the standard one.

IUT3.Rem1_2_3Remark 1.2.3
Record

(i) In the notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), a multiplicative indeterminacy by a subgroup H ⊆ O^×_k acting on O^▷_k at some '•' of the diagram Γ⃗ gives rise to an additive indeterminacy by log_k(H) on the copy of O_k at the subsequent '•'; if H consists of roots of unity, then log_k(H) = {0}, so the additive indeterminacy ceases to exist. This is to be applied in §3 to the constant multiple rigidity of the canonical splittings of theta and Gaussian monoids. (ii) Global arithmetic line bundles amount to multiplicative translates by f ∈ F^×_mod of the product of the O^×_k's over v ∈ V; such translates are disjoint except when f is a unit at all v ∈ V, which by elementary algebraic number theory happens exactly when f is a root of unity; hence quotients by F^×_mod at one '•' give an additive indeterminacy by logarithms of roots of unity at the next '•', which vanishes at v ∈ V^non and at v ∈ V^arc amounts to quotients of the copies of O^×_k (i.e., S^1) by some finite subgroup.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), (ii): local fields k, the diagram Γ⃗ of iterated log-links
  • for (i): a subgroup H ⊆ O^×_k
  • for (ii): f ∈ F^×_mod, v ranging over V

Conclusion.

(i) A multiplicative indeterminacy by H ⊆ O^×_k becomes an additive indeterminacy by log_k(H) after one log-link, and log_k(H) = {0} when H consists of roots of unity. (ii) Multiplicative translates of ∏_v O^×_k by f ∈ F^×_mod are disjoint unless f is a root of unity, so the multiplicative action of F^×_mod yields at the next step an additive indeterminacy by logarithms of roots of unity, trivial at v ∈ V^non and a finite-subgroup quotient of S^1 at v ∈ V^arc.

Obligations.

  • Prove that log_k vanishes on roots of unity of a p-adic field (log of a torsion element is zero) and that the image of a subgroup H under log_k is the additive indeterminacy described.
  • The fact used in (ii), that an element of F^×_mod with absolute value 1 at every place is a root of unity, is cited from [Lang]; Mathlib has NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_eq_one for algebraic integers with all archimedean absolute values 1, which together with integrality at all finite places covers it.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 39, (ii): 'unit at all v ∈ V' must include the archimedean v (absolute value 1); the text uses 'unit' for both kinds of place.

IUT3.Rem1_2_4Remark 1.2.4
Record

(i) The log-link is incompatible with the ring structures of Ψ^gp_{†F_v} and Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)} (it does not arise from a ring homomorphism); this barrier is the 'log-wall' of AbsTopIII, §I4. Hence objects whose structure depends on these ring structures cannot be transported via the log-link by transport of structure: the log-wall is incompatible with conventional scheme-theoretic basepoints, with Galois groups defined as automorphism groups of rings, and with Kummer theory (Proposition 1.2 (iv)). The only structure of interest manifestly compatible with the log-link is the associated D-prime-strip (abstract topological groups at v ∈ V^non, abstract Aut-holomorphic spaces at v ∈ V^arc). (ii) Further structures incompatible with the log-wall: (a) the additive structure on the image of the Kummer map; (b) in the birational situation, the collection of closed points determining the affine curve, equivalently the natural outer surjection Π^birat_v ↠ Π_v. (iii) Writing Δ^birat_v, Δ_v for the kernels of Π^birat_v ↠ G_v, Π_v ↠ G_v, the groups G_v, Δ^birat_v, Δ_v with their outer G_v-actions make sense on both sides of the log-wall, but a particular outer surjection Δ^birat_v ↠ Δ_v fails to be compatible with the log-link (Fig. 1.2: independent basepoint indeterminacies obstruct the relation between birational and affine geometric fundamental groups); this is reminiscent of compatibility of outer homomorphisms (IUTchI, Remark 4.5.1 (i)).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Proposition 1.2 (ii)
  • for (ii) (b), (iii): the birational situation, with Π^birat_v the absolute Galois group of the function field of the affine curve giving rise to Π_v; for simplicity v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non

Conclusion.

Structures that depend essentially on ring structures (scheme-theoretic basepoints, Galois groups as ring automorphism groups, Kummer theory, the additive structure on the Kummer image, the outer surjection Π^birat_v ↠ Π_v and the induced Δ^birat_v ↠ Δ_v) are not compatible with the log-link, whereas the associated D-prime-strip is compatible with it (Proposition 1.2 (i), (ii)).

Obligations.

  • Make 'incompatible with the log-link' precise (for instance: no ring homomorphism induces the log-link; or: a given structure is not preserved by some automorphism of the domain data that the log-link does not see) and prove each instance; the arguments are deferred to AbsTopIII, Remark 3.7.7.

Ambiguities.

  • 'Incompatible' and 'manifestly compatible' (pages 39 to 40) are not given a formal meaning; the remark is explanatory.
  • Fig. 1.2 (page 41) is labeled with a question mark between the birational and affine geometric fundamental groups; its content is the sentence of (iii), not a separate claim.

(ii) Horizontal arrows identify the O^{×μ}'s on both sides; to use log-shells, the Hodge theater in which one works must be the codomain of a log-link, so each horizontal arrow obligates a subsequent vertical arrow; by (i), multiradiality can then only be realized with objects invariant under the vertical arrows (vertical cores). (i) Horizontal and vertical arrows of the log-theta-lattice (Definition 1.4) are both incompatible with the local ring structures and with conventional scheme-theoretic basepoints. The linking data of the vertical arrows (the log-link) is rigid and corresponds to a single fixed rigid arithmetic holomorphic structure in which addition and multiplication are subject to 'rotations' (AbsTopIII, §I3); the linking data of the horizontal arrows (Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links), concretely the O^{×μ}'s at v ∈ V^non, is subject to a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy, which obliterates the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line. (ii) If one tries to force the horizontal arrows to be compatible with the arithmetic holomorphic structures by declaring, as for the log-link, that they induce isomorphisms of the Π_v's at v ∈ V^non, the common structure rigidified by the isomorphic copies of Π_v is obliterated whenever a nontrivial element of Ẑ^× acts on the O^{×μ}; one must then record paths of 'Π_v-rigidifying' and 'Ẑ^×-indeterminacy' operations, and the horizontal lines of the lattice amount to universal covering spaces of the resulting loops; so such an attempt gives no substantive simplification.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the log-theta-lattices of Definition 1.4
  • for simplicity v ∈ V^non

Conclusion.

The horizontal arrows of the log-theta-lattice carry a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy on the O^{×μ}'s that obliterates the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line, unlike the rigid vertical arrows; forcing the horizontal arrows to induce isomorphisms of the Π_v's leads to recording paths of rigidifying and Ẑ^×-indeterminacy operations and does not simplify the theory.

Obligations.

IUT3.Rem1_5_1Remark 1.5.1
Record

(i) Conjugate synchronization (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.5 (iii), 4.6 (iii)) is essential for the bi-coricity of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v): it is a descent mechanism from label-dependent data (labels t ∈ LabCusp^±(−), which depend on the arithmetic holomorphic structure and make sense only within a vertical line) to label-independent data, which allows horizontally coric objects; vertically coric objects require passing to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms. Bi-coricity of the O^{×μ} at v ∈ V^non is thus a consequence of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization. (ii) A naive replacement: for a topological group G (e.g. G_v, v ∈ V^non), instead of a diagonal embedding G ↪ G × ... × G use its (G × ... × G)-conjugacy class. For two factors, identifying the diagonal with its conjugates forces identifications (g, g) ~ (g, hgh^{-1}) = (g, [h, g]·g), which is incompatible with using distinct copies of G to carry distinct Galois-theoretic Kummer classes (distinct theta values); this incompatibility is a consequence of the highly nonabelian nature of G. (iii) Combinatorially, conjugate synchronization resembles the label synchronization of IUTchI, Remark 4.9.2; both are combinatorial representations of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the situation of Theorem 1.5
  • for (ii): a topological group G, for instance G_v with v ∈ V^non; for simplicity two copies of G

Conclusion.

(i) The bi-coricity of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v) may be thought of as a consequence of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization. (ii) Replacing conjugate synchronization by working with the conjugacy class of the diagonal forces identifications (g, g) ~ (g, [h, g]·g), incompatible with distinct Kummer classes at distinct components; this naive approach is inadequate. (iii) Conjugate and label synchronization are both combinatorial representations of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line.

(i) Unlike the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry on labeled copies of G_v (v ∈ V^non), no analogous conjugate synchronization exists for the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F̄ (IUTchII, Remark 4.7.2); the closest analogue is the action of the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F_mod ⊆ F_sol ⊆ F̄ and on the pseudo-monoid of ∞κ-coric rational functions. A consequence is that the reconstruction of the ring structure on labeled copies of F_sol subject to the F*_l-symmetry fails to be compatible with the localization operations of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (IUTchI, Remark 5.1.5); this is one essential reason bi-coricity analogous to Theorem 1.5 (iii) cannot be established for F^×_sol. The bi-coric mono-analytic global realified Frobenioids of Theorem 1.5 (v), i.e. the notion of log-volume, are a closest possible approximation to a bi-coric F^×_sol, which does not exist; alternatively, the bi-coric O^{×μ}'s, in the form of the bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells of Theorem 1.5 (iv), serve in §3 as 'multiradial containers' for labeled copies of F_mod via the localization functors (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (iii), 4.8 (iii)), transporting F^×_mod up to certain indeterminacies between distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures. (ii) Kummer theory is crucial for constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links); the incompatibility of solvable reconstructions of the ring structure with localization reflects the dismantling of the global prime-tree structure and the requirement of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization relative to the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. (iii) Although labeled copies of F^×_mod have no natural bi-coric structure, the global Frobenioids attached to them contain genuine conventional arithmetic line bundles (unlike the realified Frobenioids of Theorem 1.5 (v)); using the ring structure of F_mod one can push them forward to arithmetic vector bundles over Z and form tensor products, which is used in §3 and in IUTchIV.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • v ∈ V^non for the local Galois groups G_v
  • the subfields F_mod ⊆ F_sol ⊆ F̄ and the F*_l-symmetry of IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (ii), 4.8 (ii)

Conclusion.

There is no conjugate synchronization for the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F̄, and no bi-coric F^×_sol; log-volumes (Theorem 1.5 (v)) and the bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells (Theorem 1.5 (iv)) used as multiradial containers are the substitutes; the global Frobenioids attached to copies of F^×_mod contain genuine arithmetic line bundles, which can be pushed forward to arithmetic vector bundles over Z and tensored.

IUT3.Rem1_5_3Remark 1.5.3
Record

(i) In [QuCnf], holomorphic structures on Riemann surfaces are represented by squares or rectangles and quasiconformal Teichmüller deformations by parallelograms (affine linear deformations dilating one real dimension by a factor in R_{>0}). Conjugate synchronization, a rigidity representing the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line, may be thought of as a nonarchimedean arithmetic analogue of this: the right angles of squares synchronize the metrics of the two real dimensions (Fig. 1.4). (ii) The naive approach of Remark 1.5.1 (ii) (identifying the conjugates of the diagonal embedding) corresponds to treating a holomorphic structure as an equivalence class modulo Teichmüller deformations, which avoids rigidifying the relation between the two metrics but makes any theory of deformations of a holomorphic structure unfeasible. (iii) The analogy applies also to κ-sol-conjugate synchronization (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (ii), 4.8 (ii)) between labeled non-realified and realified global Frobenioids via the F*_l-symmetry, especially for realified ones, which carry a natural R_{>0}-action: the synchronization of global realified Frobenioids by the F*_l-symmetry may be related, via the isomorphisms of Frobenioids of IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (iii), 4.8 (iii), to the global realified Frobenioid portion of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii)); the synchronization of non-realified global Frobenioids is a further rigidification, used in §3.

Conclusion.

An analogy, not a mathematical assertion: conjugate synchronization is to the arithmetic holomorphic structure what right angles of squares and rectangles are to a complex holomorphic structure; the naive alternative of Remark 1.5.1 (ii) corresponds to holomorphic structures modulo Teichmüller deformation; the F*_l-synchronization of realified global Frobenioids relates to the global realified Frobenioid portion of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link, and that of non-realified ones is a further rigidification.

Obligations.

IUT3.Rem1_5_4Remark 1.5.4
Record

(i) A main theme (IUTchII, Remark 3.8.3 (iii)) is an explicit description of one arithmetic holomorphic structure (a vertical line of the log-theta-lattice) from the point of view of a distinct one, related to it only via a mono-analytic core such as the bi-coric structures of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v). The objects of interest are Frobenius-like (main example: the Gaussian monoids of IUTchII, §3, §4), needed for constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links). The description splits into (a) passing from Frobenius-like to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms and (b) transporting étale-like structures between arithmetic holomorphic structures by multiradiality; the indeterminacies ('departures from rigidity') arising in (a) are called Kummer-detachment indeterminacies, those in (b) étale-transport indeterminacies. (ii) Étale-transport indeterminacies typically arise from anabelian or group-theoretic algorithms; a fundamental example is given by automorphisms of the local absolute Galois groups G_v, v ∈ V^non, not of scheme-theoretic origin (Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv); AbsTopIII, §I3). (iii) Examples of Kummer-detachment indeterminacies: the non-commutative Frobenius-picture diagrams of Propositions 1.2 (x), 1.3 (iv) (which path to take from a '•' to the coric '◦'), whose upper semi-commutativity for the coric holomorphic log-shells (Remark 1.2.2 (iii)) is an upper estimate of this indeterminacy; and the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of Remark 1.4.2 (cf. the Kummer isomorphisms of the final display of Theorem 1.5 (iii)).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the log-theta-lattice of Definition 1.4 and the bi-coric structures of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v)

Conclusion.

Terminology: indeterminacies arising when Frobenius-like objects are passed to étale-like ones via Kummer isomorphisms are 'Kummer-detachment indeterminacies'; those arising when étale-like objects are transported by multiradiality are 'étale-transport indeterminacies'. Examples: automorphisms of G_v (v ∈ V^non) not of scheme-theoretic origin are étale-transport indeterminacies; the non-commutativity of the Frobenius-picture diagrams of Propositions 1.2 (x), 1.3 (iv), estimated from above by upper semi-commutativity of the coric log-shells, and the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of Remark 1.4.2 are Kummer-detachment indeterminacies.

Obligations.

  • Give a precise definition of each indeterminacy class as a set of maps or a group action, so that the classification of the examples in (ii) and (iii) becomes checkable.

Ambiguities.

  • A terminological remark: the two classes of indeterminacy are named by the step in which they arise, with no formal definition; 'typically amount to' (page 56) does not delimit étale-transport indeterminacies.

IUT3.Rem2_1_1Remark 2.1.1
Record

Summary of the main properties of mono-theta environments established in [EtTh] and their roles: (a) cyclotomic rigidity, (b) discrete rigidity, (c) constant multiple rigidity, (d) isomorphism class compatibility, (e) Frobenioid structure compatibility. (d) refers to compatibility with the convention that objects of the tempered Frobenioids (and base categories) are known only up to isomorphism; the compatibility with the topology of the tempered fundamental group mentioned in the Introduction of [EtTh] is a consequence of (d). (i) (e): the Frobenius-like monoidal portion with its Galois action is used in constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (log-, Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links) and related to étale-like structures by Kummer theory. (ii) (d): each object of a Kummer tower corresponds to a single field, whose ring structure is needed for the log-link (vertical coricity, Proposition 2.1 (i)); the N-th power morphisms of a Kummer tower are 'algebraic', so fundamental groups on either side are related up to inner automorphisms; the objects of these towers arise from nontrivial line bundles on tempered coverings of a Tate curve, so extracting N-th roots yields mutually non-isomorphic objects, related algorithmically only via indeterminate isomorphisms. (iii) (c): used for the canonical splittings of theta monoids via restriction to the zero section. (iv) (a): a consequence of the nondegeneracy of the commutator [−, −] of the theta groups ('the degree of the commutator is precisely 2'); concretely a specific isomorphism between interior and exterior cyclotomes, a rigidification of a 'projective line of cyclotomes', nonlinear in nature: composing it with an N-th power morphism sacrifices (c); its multiradiality (IUTchII, Corollary 1.10), in contrast with MLF-Galois pair cyclotomic rigidity, is central in §2. (v) (b): a consequence of 'the degree of the commutator is ≤ 2' (EtTh, Proposition 2.14 (ii), (iii)); it allows restriction to Z-multiples and powers rather than Ẑ-multiples and powers of divisors, line bundles and rational functions (such as the q-parameter) on tempered coverings of a Tate curve. The author's answer to whether a theory of Ẑ-divisors, line bundles and rational functions parallel to perfections and realifications of Frobenioids exists is 'no': Ẑ has no notion of positivity (−1 ∈ Ẑ is a limit of positive integers), so such a theory would confuse effective and negative divisors, i.e. work birationally, sacrificing the isomorphisms between line bundles needed for the Frobenioid-theoretic mono-theta environment.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • mono-theta environments arising from tempered Frobenioids at bad primes, as in Proposition 2.1 (iii) and [EtTh]

Conclusion.

Expository: the roles of properties (a) to (e) of mono-theta environments in the theory; in particular cyclotomic rigidity is multiradial (IUTchII, Corollary 1.10) and nonlinear, discrete rigidity restricts to Z-multiples, and in the author's view no theory of Ẑ-divisors parallel to realifications is available because Ẑ has no positivity.

Obligations.

  • The rigidity properties (a) to (e) are results of [EtTh]; none is proved here.
  • The elementary fact that −1 ∈ Ẑ is a limit of positive integers (page 63) holds: −1 = lim (n! − 1) in Ẑ.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 63: the negative answer to the question on Ẑ-divisors is stated as 'as far as the author can see at the time of writing'; it is an opinion, not a theorem.
  • 'The degree of the commutator is precisely 2' and 'is ≤ 2' (pages 62 to 63) are informal; their precise content is in [EtTh], Proposition 2.14.

IUT3.Rem2_1_2Remark 2.1.2
Record

(i) The global bookkeeping operations on labels of evaluation points in the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, together with the profinite nature of the global étale fundamental groups, force the use of the 'complements on tempered coverings' of IUTchI, §2 at v ∈ V^bad, so as to restrict to discrete Z-conjugates rather than profinite Ẑ-conjugates of the theta functions; this is called 'evaluation discrete rigidity'. (ii) In the situation of IUTchII, Proposition 2.1, fix v ∈ V^bad, Π := Π_v, Π̂ its profinite completion, with natural surjections Π ↠ l·Z ⊆ Z and Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ ⊆ Ẑ, and Π† := Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z ⊆ Π̂. Evaluation discrete rigidity concerns whether the coordinates of the evaluation points lie in Z or in Ẑ. The partially tempered group Π† cannot replace Π: there is an '[easily verified]' natural isomorphism N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z, so Π† fails various absolute anabelian properties of Π (SemiAnbd, Theorems 6.6, 6.8) and its profinite conjugacy indeterminacies give Ẑ-translation indeterminacies of the coordinates of evaluation points, which for Π are avoided by the complements on tempered coverings, a consequence of the highly anabelian nature of Π.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • for (ii): the situation of IUTchII, Proposition 2.1; v ∈ V^bad; Π := Π_v the tempered fundamental group, Π̂ its profinite completion
  • the natural surjections Π ↠ l·Z (⊆ Z), Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ (⊆ Ẑ), and Π† := Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z ⊆ Π̂

Conclusion.

(i) The complements on tempered coverings (IUTchI, §2) provide an 'evaluation discrete rigidity'. (ii) N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z naturally; consequently Π† lacks absolute anabelian properties of Π and its profinite conjugacy indeterminacies act by Ẑ-translations on the coordinates of evaluation points, so Π† cannot replace the full tempered fundamental group Π.

Obligations.

  • Prove the natural isomorphism N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z (page 64: '[easily verified]'; no argument is given).
  • Make precise which absolute anabelian properties Π† fails, with reference to SemiAnbd, Theorems 6.6, 6.8.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 64: Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ is written with the target underlined as a subgroup of Ẑ; the fiber product Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z is taken over the composite Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ ⊆ Ẑ and the inclusion Z ⊆ Ẑ, which is the natural reading.

(i) Write Π_v := Π_X(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), G_v := G_v(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), Π_μ := Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), (l·Δ_Θ) := (l·Δ_Θ)(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), an object constructed from Π_v (IUTchII, Proposition 1.4). The projective system of mono-theta environments is an 'amalgamation of Π_v and Π_μ' allowing reconstruction of the mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l·Δ_Θ) ≅ Π_μ itself (IUTchII, Proposition 1.5 (iii)), not just its Ẑ^×-orbit. (ii) The Kummer classes in ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v of the étale theta functions are, for suitable characteristic open H ⊆ Π_v, twisted homomorphisms H → Π_μ restricting on (l·Δ_Θ) to the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism. The essential content of Theorem 2.2 (ii): since the Kummer-theoretic link between étale-like and Frobenius-like data at v ∈ V^bad is made via mono-theta environments, which do not involve the monoids (−)^{×μ}, the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (not just its Ẑ^×-orbit) is immune to the automorphisms of the (−)^{×μ} arising from isomorphisms of coric data; this is a decoupling of geometric (Δ_v ⊆ Π_v) and base-field-theoretic (Π_v ↠ G_v) data, a splitting into purely radial (Π_μ) and purely coric ((−)^{×μ}) components. (iii) This contrasts with the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of cyclotomic rigidity from MLF-Galois pairs, whose input data is O^▷: in the diagram O^μ ⊆ O^× ⊆ O^▷ ⊆ O^gp ⊆ O^{gp^} with O^× ↠ O^{×μ}, a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy on O^{×μ} lifts naturally only to Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on O^×, O^{gp^} (Fig. 2.1), so only the Ẑ^×-orbit of the MLF-Galois-pair cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism is recovered; mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity is insulated (Fig. 2.2: identity action on Π_μ ≅ O^μ, Ẑ^× on O^{×μ}). (iv) Mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity insulates the étale theta function from the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies acting on the coric log-shells; the techniques do not apply immediately to Gaussian monoids, whose multiradiality (§3) requires log-shells but depends essentially on that of theta monoids. Treating theta values q^{j^2}_v merely as elements of the base field, without the étale theta function, leaves only MLF-Galois pairs to rigidify cyclotomes, giving Ẑ^×-indeterminacies, i.e. confusion between q^{j^2}_v and their Ẑ^×-powers.

(i) Naive question: can the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link q ↦ q^{(1^2, ..., (l*)^2)} (IUTchII, Remark 4.11.1) be replaced by q ↦ q^λ for an arbitrary positive integer λ? The answer given is 'no': such a correspondence lacks the multiradiality machinery of the étale theta function (mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity, splittings by zero-labeled evaluation points), so there is no insulation of its Kummer classes from the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on (−)^{×μ}, and no decoupling of the coric log-shells from its purely radial (value group) portion; realizing such a splitting by Galois evaluation with λ = j^2 raises symmetry issues between the zero-labeled evaluation point and the one for λ, which the theory resolves via the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, and leads to conditions on the collection of evaluation points (IUTchII, Remark 2.6.3); 'it is difficult to see' how to build the theory with evaluation points other than those of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link. (ii) The multiradial formulations of Gaussian monoids in §3 are subject to indeterminacies sufficiently mild for the volume computations of IUTchIV but substantially more severe than those for theta monoids in §2, which essentially consist of multiplication by roots of unity (IUTchII, Proposition 3.1 (i)), are essentially negligible and come from the Kummer theory of mono-theta environments; this exactness would be lost with correspondences q ↦ q^λ. (iii) The Kummer-compatibility of the multiradial splitting via Galois evaluation relates the Kummer theory of theta monoids in the domain of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link to the ×μ-Kummer structures in its horizontally coric portion (Fig. 2.3): restricted to ∞θ, the Ism-orbit of arrows from O^× to O^{×μ} becomes a single arrow because ∞θ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ}; the multiradial structure on the theta monoid O^×·∞θ given by the splittings into coric and radial components is compatible with the Kummer theories of O^× and of the coric O^{×μ}. For a naive correspondence q ↦ q^λ the analogous arrows map q^λ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ} and are incompatible with passage to Kummer classes, since the Kummer class of q^λ in a cohomology group of Π/Δ is by no means mapped, via the poly-isomorphism Π/Δ ≅ G, to the trivial element of the corresponding cohomology group of G.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the situation of Theorem 2.2 and of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (IUTchII, Remark 4.11.1)
  • for (i): λ an arbitrary positive integer

Conclusion.

A naive correspondence q ↦ q^λ cannot replace the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link: it lacks mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity and zero-labeled splittings, its indeterminacies would not be essentially negligible, and its analogue of Fig. 2.3 (q^λ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ}) is incompatible with passage to Kummer classes because the Kummer class of q^λ is not mapped to the trivial class of G.

IUT3.Rem2_3_3Remark 2.3.3

Comparison of multiradiality in the theta case (Remarks 2.2.1, 2.2.2, Corollary 2.3) and the number field case (Remark 2.3.2), summarized in Fig. 2.7 (page 84). (i) Similarity: both use the geometric dimension of the elliptic curve as a 'multiradial geometric container' for radial arithmetic data (theta values q^{j^2}_v, resp. copies of F_mod): theta functions on Tate curves [EtTh], resp. Belyi maps as Belyi cuspidalizations [AbsTopIII]; both pass to the data by Galois evaluation. (ii) Interpretation of the dismantling of the two combinatorial dimensions of a number field, by analogy with base change from R to C: multiradial containers as realizations of two-dimensional scheme-theoretic data (an elliptic curve over a number field) and the multiradial representations of Theorem 3.11 as realizations of 'suitable descent data'; compare parallel transport (IUTchII, Remark 1.7.1) and PD-envelopes (IUTchII, Remark 1.9.2 (iii)). (iii) Both Galois evaluations occur in the context of the log-link; difference: theta values depend on the labels j ∈ F*_l (which correspond to cuspidal inertia groups in Δ ⊆ Π), copies of F_mod do not. It is called a 'quite nontrivial fact' that Galois evaluation and Kummer theory in the theta case are compatible with both the labels and the arithmetic holomorphic structures. (iv) It is called a 'highly nontrivial fact' that the construction of the mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism admits F^{⋊±}_l-symmetries consistently with the label dependence of the theta values; from the naive Kummer approach of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), this would require a rational function invariant under the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetries with distinct valuations on an orbit, which is self-contradictory. (v) Replacing Π by a closed subgroup of infinite index (to kill Kummer classes of the obstruction to symmetry) has two deficiencies: absolute anabelian results of AbsTopIII, §1 may not generalize to such subgroups, and vanishing of Kummer classes on restriction need not be compatible with ring structures. (vi) Using distinct rational functions (a symmetric one for cyclotomic rigidity, a non-symmetric one for evaluation) conflicts with the identification of the cuspidal cyclotomes μ^*_et into μ^∀_et (AbsTopIII, Proposition 1.4 (ii)) and the tautological identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et needed for multiradial containers; the cyclotomic rigidity of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) identifies the μ^*_et with sub-cyclotomes of μ_Fr via multiplication by the orders of zeroes and poles, so under the identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et one must allow indeterminacy by the submonoid I^ord ⊆ ±N_{≥1} := N_{≥1} × {±1} generated by those orders, with images I^ord_{≥1} ⊆ N_{≥1}, I^ord_± ⊆ {±1}. Nontrivial I^ord is incompatible with constructions analogous to theta values ('it follows immediately' that independent indeterminacies at distinct v contradict the product formula). In the theta case I^ord = {1} because the order of zeroes and poles of the theta function at every cusp is 1 ([EtTh], Proposition 1.4 (i)), impossible for an algebraic rational function, whose orders sum to 0. In the number field case the I^ord_{≥1} part is avoided by Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}, which remains valid after the identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et, while the I^ord_± part, avoided in IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) by the non-κ-coricity of inverses of nonconstant κ-coric functions, is incompatible with that identification; hence the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms, and the copies of F^×_mod ∪ {0}, are subject to an indeterminacy {±1}, which causes no obstacle since F^×_mod is stabilized by {±1} (Remark 3.11.4); the copies of F^×_mod are constructed globally and compatibly with the F*_l-symmetry, without product formula compatibilities between distinct v. (vii) These are a multiple cusp version of the 'N-th power versus first power' and linearity issues (IUTchII, Remark 3.6.4 (iii)); mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity is compatible with the topology of the tempered fundamental group, whereas the algorithms of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) depend on Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}, which is incompatible with the profinite topology (N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ). (viii) The same indeterminacy issues occur for the cyclotomic rigidity algorithms of IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (vi) for mixed-characteristic local fields, which yield the same isomorphism as AbsTopIII, Proposition 3.2 (iv) (IUTchII, Proposition 4.2 (i)) and are compatible with the profinite topology because they use uniformizers (one zero of order 1, no poles), reflecting the canonical valuation of an MLF; so theta functions, resp. one-dimensional function fields, are a 'qualitative geometric model' of MLFs, resp. number fields, at the level of valuations. (ix) Analogy with the upper half-plane: q = e^{2πiz} (eigenfunction for additive symmetries, theta case) is highly transcendental, w = (z − i)/(z + i) (multiplicative symmetries, number field case) is algebraic. (x) Fig. 2.7 summarizes the comparison.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the theta case of Remarks 2.2.1, 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.3 and the number field case of Remark 2.3.2
  • for (vi): rational functions on hyperbolic curves with cusps '*', the cuspidal cyclotomes μ^*_et, μ^∀_et, μ_Fr and the submonoid I^ord ⊆ ±N_{≥1} := N_{≥1} × {±1} generated by the orders of zeroes and poles

Conclusion.

Expository comparison (Fig. 2.7). Mathematical assertions made along the way: in the theta case the indeterminacy submonoid I^ord is {1}, because the theta function has order 1 at every cusp; for algebraic rational functions the orders sum to 0; Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}; N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ; nontrivial independent indeterminacies at distinct v ∈ V are incompatible with the product formula; in the number field case the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms and the copies of F^×_mod ∪ {0} are subject to a {±1}-indeterminacy, under which F^×_mod is stable.

Obligations.

  • Elementary facts used, all provable: Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1} (a positive rational that is a unit at every prime is 1); N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ; the orders of zeroes and poles of a nonconstant rational function on a proper curve sum to 0 (degree of a principal divisor); w = (z − i)/(z + i) is a rational function of z.

IUT3.Rem2_3_4Remark 2.3.4
Record

The essential content of [EtTh] in light of Remark 2.3.3. (i) Non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters (log-links and Θ-links) are built from Frobenius-like structures; étale-like structures relate the two sides; Kummer theory relates the two kinds and must be multiradial, which is achieved by radial/coric decouplings via multiradial geometric containers followed by Galois evaluation, since direct use of theta values or number fields gives a Kummer theory without the desired multiradiality (Remarks 2.2.1, 2.3.2). (ii) The naive Kummer theory of algebraic rational functions (IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v); Definition 5.2 (vi)) is, at v ∈ V^bad, incompatible with the profinite topology (Remark 2.3.3 (vi), (vii), (viii); Figs. 2.5, 2.6), so one uses the Kummer theory of theta functions truncated modulo N; the naive version of that is incompatible with discrete rigidity (Remark 2.1.1 (v)), owing to the lack of 'shifting automorphisms' (EtTh, Proposition 2.14 (ii); Remark 2.14.3), and with the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry; one therefore uses the Kummer theory of the first Chern classes of the line bundles associated to theta functions. Summary: truncated Kummer theory of theta functions is compatible with profinite/tempered topologies; truncated Kummer theory of first Chern classes of line bundles is compatible with discrete rigidity and the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. (iii) This amounts to the partially truncated arithmetic fundamental group of the G_m-torsor of such a line bundle, i.e. the topological group portion of a mono- or bi-theta environment (EtTh, Definition 2.13 (ii) (a), (iii) (a)), which carries two distinguished classes of sections, theta sections and algebraic sections. With neither: indeterminacy by multiplication by constant units O^×, incompatible with constant multiple rigidity. With both (bi-theta environments): the lack of symmetries of the truncated theory, incompatible with discrete rigidity and the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. With algebraic sections only: not enough data for the commutator property of EtTh, Proposition 2.12, incompatible with cyclotomic rigidity. With theta sections only (mono-theta environments): compatible with the tempered topology, the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry and all three rigidities. (iv) The approach of [EtTh] differs from the function-theoretic (explicit series, EtTh, Proposition 1.4) and representation-theoretic (irreducible representations of theta groups) approaches, which depend on ring structures and are ill-suited to theta functions in distinct ring/scheme theories related only via tempered Frobenioids (multiplicative monoids) and tempered fundamental groups (Galois actions).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • v ∈ V^bad for the local discussion of (ii), (iii)
  • line bundles associated to theta functions on tempered coverings of a Tate curve, as in [EtTh]

Conclusion.

Of the four options for the sections carried by the partially truncated arithmetic fundamental group of the G_m-torsor of the theta line bundle, only working with theta sections and not algebraic sections (mono-theta environments) is compatible with the tempered topology, the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry and all three rigidities (cyclotomic, discrete, constant multiple); the other three options each fail one of these.

Obligations.

  • Each of the four compatibility claims of (iii) rests on results of [EtTh] (Propositions 2.12, 2.14; Definition 2.13) that are cited, not proved here.

Ambiguities.

  • 'Fatal drawback' and 'incompatible' (pages 85 to 87) are not given formal meanings.

IUT3.Prop3_1Proposition 3.1Local Holomorphic Tensor Packets
Record

Local holomorphic tensor packets. For an n-capsule {α𝔉}_{α∈A} of F-prime-strips and v | v_Q, log(αF_v) is an inductive limit of topological modules of finite dimension over Q_{v_Q}; the 1-tensor packet is v_Q ↦ log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{v|v_Q} log(αF_v), and the n-tensor packet is log(AF_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α∈A} log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{{v_α}} {⊗_α log(αF_{v_α})}, tensor products of ind-topological modules (page 92). (i) The ind-topological field structures on the log(αF_v) determine an ind-topological ring structure on log(AF_{v_Q}), an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields; the decompositions are determined by the ring structure and compatible with the action of αΠ_v. (ii) For α ∈ A, v | v_Q: log(A,αF_v) = log(αF_v) ⊗ {⊗_{β∈A∖{α}} log(βF_{v_Q})} ⊆ log(AF_{v_Q}) is a direct summand and an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields. Tensoring with 1's in the factors β ≠ α gives a natural injective ring homomorphism log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) which, for suitable cofinal objects of the inductive systems, induces an isomorphism of an object of the domain onto each direct summand field of the corresponding object of the codomain. Hence the integral structure Ψ̄ = Ψ_{log(αF_v)} ∪ {0} ⊆ log(αF_v) determines integral structures on each direct summand field of log(A,αF_v) and log(AF_{v_Q}) (page 93). Remark 3.1.1 (i) (page 94): log(αF_v) ≅ k̄, Ψ̄ ≅ O_k̄, log(A,αF_v) ≅ ⊗ k̄ ≅ lim ⊕ k̄ ⊇ lim ⊕ O_k̄, so the integral structures are copies of O_k̄ in the copies of k̄.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • initial Θ-data as in IUTchI Def 3.1
  • an n-capsule {α𝔉}_{α∈A} of F-prime-strips (IUTchI §0, Def 5.2 (i))
  • v ∈ V, v_Q ∈ V_Q with v | v_Q (part (ii) also fixes α ∈ A)

Implicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Def 1.1 (i), (ii), (iii)

Conclusion.

(i) log(AF_{v_Q}) carries an ind-topological ring structure, an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields, with decompositions determined by the ring structure and αΠ_v-compatible; (ii) log(A,αF_v) is a direct summand of the same kind, the map log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) is injective and induces isomorphisms onto each direct summand field for cofinal objects, and Ψ̄ determines, through these isomorphisms, an integral structure on each direct summand field.

Obligations.

  • Formalize topological tensor products of local fields and their decomposition into products of fields.
  • Record two lattices and the map between them. Lattice L1 (the one on page 93): the product, over the direct summand fields of a finite object of log(A,αF_v) or log(AF_{v_Q}), of the copy of the ring of integers transported from Ψ̄ by the isomorphism of page 93; this is the normalization (integral closure) in the product of fields. Lattice L2 (not on page 93): the image of the tensor product of the rings of integers of the factors. The map is the inclusion L2 → L1 induced by the inclusions of rings of integers. Assessment, not from the page: L2 can be a proper order in L1, so the two must not be identified. Every later use (log-volume 0 of the integral structures, Prop 3.9 (i)) refers to L1.
  • Prove that the integral structure transported to a summand field does not depend on the cofinal object chosen.

(ii) Weights: log-volumes on the portion of log(αF_v) for K_v are taken with weight [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1}; for direct sums over v | v_Q the normalized weight is 1/([K_v:(F_mod)_v]·Σ_{w|v_Q}[(F_mod)_w : Q_{v_Q}]); for tensor products over α ∈ A the weight 1/∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}], normalized to 1/((∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}])·Σ_{{w_α}}∏_α[(F_mod)_{w_α}:Q_{v_Q}]); all normalized so that multiplication by p_{v_Q} adds or subtracts log(p_{v_Q}) (pages 94 to 95). (iii) Such weighted sums of log-volumes do not in general arise as a positive real multiple of the logarithm of a measure in the usual sense. For a direct product region (a product of compact subsets of positive measure of the direct summands) the weighted sum is computed directly; a direct product pre-region uses relatively compact factors; for arbitrary Borel sets the construction of (iv) applies, with V = ∏_α V_{v_Q}, N_v = ∏_α [K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}], M_v the (radial, if archimedean) summand of Prop 3.1; on direct product regions a suitable positive normalization factor times the log of the E-weighted measure gives the weighted sums of (ii) (pages 95 to 96). (iv) For a nonempty finite set V, nonempty finite sets E_v and measure spaces (M_v, μ_v), the E-weighted measure μ_E(S) ∈ R_{≥0} ∪ {+∞} of a Borel set S ⊆ M_V is the measure of S_E = (∏_{e∈E} S) ∩ M_{E*V} in M_{E*V} ≅ M_W; it depends only on N = {N_v = |E_v|}; for S = ∏_v S_v with S_v compact of positive measure, (1/N_E)·μ^log_E(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v)·μ^log_v(S_v), N_E = ∏_v N_v (pages 96 to 97).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the situation of Prop 3.1
  • for (iv): V a nonempty finite set, E_v nonempty finite sets, (M_v, μ_v) nonempty measure spaces in the sense of (iii)

Conclusion.

Weighted sums of log-volumes are defined with the weights of (ii); on direct product regions they equal (1/N_E)·log μ_E(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v)·log μ_v(S_v), and the E-weighted measure μ_E extends them to arbitrary Borel sets; they are in general not a positive multiple of the log of an ordinary measure on the original product.

Obligations.

  • Verify the (iv) identity as a product-measure computation on M_{E*V} ≅ M_W (elementary once the spaces are fixed). Done on direct product regions, with the measure defined on M_W directly (IUT3.Rem3_1_1.frag.wpkt_e_weighted); M_{E*V} and its homeomorphism with M_W are not formalized.
  • Fix the normalization factor of (iii) that relates (1/N_E)·log μ_E to the weighted sums of (ii); the page says only 'a suitable positive real number'.
  • The normalized weight of (ii) is defined as printed (IUT3.Rem3_1_1.frag.wpkt_weight), with sum_t w_t dim_t = 1 (IUT3.Rem3_1_1.frag.wpkt_weight_dim_sum, a model test); the warning of (iii) is made precise in a model (IUT3.Rem3_1_1.frag.wpkt_warning_model, a model test).

Ambiguities.

  • The value set of μ_E is R_{≥0} ∪ {+∞}; finiteness for the regions used later is not stated at this point.
  • Pages 95 to 96: the weighted sums of log-volumes of (ii) are in general not a positive real multiple of the logarithm of a volume or measure in the usual sense; only for direct product (pre-)regions is their computation straightforward, and for these a suitable positive normalization factor times the logarithm of the E-weighted measure μ_E (a measure on M_{E*V} ≅ M_W, not on the original product of the direct summands) gives them.

IUT3.Prop3_2Proposition 3.2Local Mono-analytic Tensor Packets
Record

Local mono-analytic tensor packets: for an n-capsule {αD^⊢}_{α ∈ A} of D^⊢-prime-strips, defines the 1-tensor packet v_Q ↦ log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{v | v_Q} log(αD^⊢_v), the n-tensor packet log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α ∈ A} log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) (tensor product of ind-topological modules), and the submodules log(A,αD^⊢_v); the same notation is used for capsules of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips. Then (i) mono-analytic and holomorphic packets are related by natural poly-isomorphisms and (ii) mono-analytic log-shells give integral structures.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • an n-capsule {αD^⊢}_{α ∈ A} of D^⊢-prime-strips relative to the given initial Θ-data (IUTchI, §0, Definition 4.1 (iii))

Conclusion.

(i) If the capsule arises from the capsule of F-prime-strips of Proposition 3.1, the poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii) induce natural poly-isomorphisms of ind-topological modules from the mono-analytic packets log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}), log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}), log(A,αD^⊢v) through the F^{⊢×μ}-versions to the holomorphic packets of Proposition 3.1. (ii) The mono-analytic log-shells determine integral structures: topological submodules I(αD^⊢{v_Q}), I(A D^⊢_{v_Q}), I(A,αD^⊢_v) on the Q-spans (by direct sums and tensor products at nonarchimedean v_Q; as closed unit balls of the induced direct sum and tensor product Hermitian metrics at archimedean v_Q), with Q-spans I^Q((−)) and the same notation for F- and F^{⊢×μ}-versions via the poly-isomorphisms of (i).

Obligations.

  • Define tensor products of ind-topological modules and show that the poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii) induce poly-isomorphisms of packets.
  • Define the integral structures at nonarchimedean v_Q from the mono-analytic log-shells and at archimedean v_Q as closed unit balls of the induced Hermitian metrics.
  • The proof (page 99) says the assertions follow immediately from the definitions and cited references; the blocking is inherited from Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii).

Ambiguities.

  • At archimedean v_Q the mono-analytic log-shell is regarded as the closed unit ball of a Hermitian metric (page 98); that this subset is indeed such a unit ball is taken for granted.

Local packet-theoretic Frobenioids: (i) single packet monoids obtained as images of Ψ_{log(αF_v)}, its units and its realification inside log(A,αF_v); (ii) local LGP-monoids Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v, ∞Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v constructed by a functorial algorithm in a log-link ‡HT → †HT of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, whose components labeled j act on I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j;‡F_v). Fig. 3.1 depicts the splitting monoids q^{j^2} acting on the (j+1)-capsules S^±_{j+1}.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • for (i): the situation of Proposition 3.1, with α ∈ A, v ∈ V, v_Q ∈ V_Q, v | v_Q
  • for (ii): a log-link ‡HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters as in Proposition 1.3 (i)

Conclusion.

(i) The images of Ψ_{log(αF_v)}, Ψ^×_{log(αF_v)}, Ψ^R_{log(αF_v)} under log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) are monoids with G_v(αΠ_v)-actions (v nonarchimedean) or with an Aut-holomorphic orbispace and Kummer structure (v archimedean), acting multiplicatively on subquotients of log(A,αF_v); they determine a Frobenioid (resp. collection of data) naturally isomorphic to log(αF_v). (ii) There is a functorial algorithm in the log-link ‡HT → †HT producing the LGP-monoids Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)v and ∞Ψ{F_LGP}(†HT)v; for v ∈ V^bad the component labeled j ∈ {1, ..., l*} of the Galois invariants of the entire LGP-monoid is a subset of I^Q(S^±{j+1},j;‡F_v) acting multiplicatively on it, and for any v the component labeled j of the Galois invariants of the unit portion is likewise a subset of I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j;‡F_v) acting multiplicatively on it.

(i) Vertically coric LGP-monoids and their Kummer isomorphisms. (ii) Upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence: (a) at nonarchimedean v_Q the mono-analytic integral structure contains the Kummer images of units, also after the m'-th iterate of the log-link; (b) at archimedean v_Q the closed unit ball contains the units and the closed balls of radius π, with a surjection via iterates; (c) at bad v the splitting monoids are mutually compatible up to roots of unity, which via the log-link is 'addition by zero'. Invariance under the column translation symmetry.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,m HT}_{n,m∈Z} relative to the given initial Θ-data, arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Def 1.4)
  • for each n, the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater n,◦HT determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Thm 1.5 (i))

Conclusion.

Upper semi-compatibility (containments) along each column.

Obligations.

  • State and prove the containments (a), (b) as inclusions of explicit subsets of p-adic and complex fields. The containment (a) is proved for one tensor factor with the Kummer maps taken to be identities, over Q_p and over finite extensions of Q_p in the normed-field model (IUT3.Prop3_5.frag.padic_upper_semi, IUT3.Prop3_5.frag.ext_upper_semi); tensor products over |t|, Galois invariants, Kummer isomorphisms and the archimedean surjections of (b) are open.
  • Prove that roots of unity in the domain map to 0 under the p-adic logarithm (c).

    Record

    Rational function torsor version. For each v ∈ V, the valuation of K_v gives a group homomorphism β_v : F^×_mod → K^×_v/O^×_{K_v}. An object T = (T, {t_v}_{v∈V}) of F^⊛_MOD consists of (a) an F^×_mod-torsor T and (b) for each v ∈ V a trivialization t_v of the torsor T_v obtained from T by change of structure group along β_v, such that some t ∈ T induces t_v for all but finitely many v. An elementary morphism T_1 → T_2 is an isomorphism T_1 ≅ T_2 of F^×_mod-torsors that is integral at each v (maps t_{1,v} into the O^▷_{K_v}-orbit of t_{2,v}); a morphism T_1 → T_2 is a positive integer n with an elementary morphism T_1^{⊗n} → T_2. 'One verifies immediately' that F^⊛_MOD has a natural Frobenioid structure ([FrdI], Definition 1.3) with base category the one-arrow category, linear morphisms the elementary morphisms and Frobenius degree n; and 'one verifies immediately' that sending an arithmetic line bundle on S_mod to its restriction to the generic point (an F^×_mod-torsor) with the local trivializations from the local integral structures gives a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity on the rational function monoids F^×_mod ([FrdI], Corollary 4.10).

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the hypotheses of IUT3.Ex3_6
    • for each v ∈ V, K_v and the homomorphism β_v : F^×_mod → K^×v/O^×{K_v} determined by the valuation of v

    Conclusion.

    F^⊛_MOD is a category with a natural Frobenioid structure (one-arrow base category; elementary morphisms linear; n the Frobenius degree), and there is a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity F^×_mod → F^×_mod on rational function monoids.

    Obligations.

    • Page 107: 'evident notion' of composition of morphisms and of tensor powers is not spelled out; the natural composite of (n_1, φ_1) and (n_2, φ_2) is (n_1 n_2, φ_2 ∘ φ_1^{⊗ n_2}).

    Record

    Local fractional ideal version. An object J = {J_v}_{v∈V} of F^⊛_mod (fraktur) is a collection of 'fractional ideals' J_v ⊆ K_v: a finitely generated nonzero O_{K_v}-submodule of K_v for v ∈ V^non, a positive real multiple of O_{K_v} := {λ ∈ K_v : |λ| ≤ 1} for v ∈ V^arc, with J_v = O_{K_v} for all but finitely many v. F^×_mod acts by f·J = {f·J_v}; there are tensor powers J^{⊗n}, n ∈ Z. An elementary morphism J_1 → J_2 is an f ∈ F^×_mod integral with respect to J_1, J_2, i.e. f·J_{1,v} ⊆ J_{2,v} for every v ∈ V; a morphism is a positive integer n with an elementary morphism J_1^{⊗n} → J_2. 'One verifies immediately' that this category has a natural Frobenioid structure (one-arrow base category, elementary morphisms linear, n the Frobenius degree), and that associating to J the arithmetic line bundle on S_mod obtained from the trivial one by modifying its integral structure at each v as prescribed by J_v gives a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_mod inducing the identity on F^×_mod ([FrdI], Corollary 4.10).

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the hypotheses of IUT3.Ex3_6

    F^⊛_mod (fraktur) is a category with a natural Frobenioid structure, and there is a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_mod inducing the identity F^×_mod → F^×_mod on rational function monoids.

IUT3.Rem3_6_2Remark 3.6.2
Record

(i) Frobenioids isomorphic to the realification of F^⊛_mod lying on opposite sides of an enhanced version of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link are to be related; at the level of objects only isomorphism classes preserved by the isomorphisms of Frobenioids make sense, and these are determined by the divisor and rational function monoids of the model Frobenioid ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (i), (ii)). The rational function monoid F^×_mod of F^⊛_mod has the fundamental property that F^×_mod ∪ {0} admits a natural additive structure; this fails for (a) the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification of F^⊛_mod and (b) subgroups Γ ⊆ F^×_mod (such as {1} or the S-units for a nonempty finite S ⊆ V_mod) that are not the multiplicative group of a subfield of F_mod (AbsTopIII, Remark 5.10.2 (iv)). This allows objects of F^⊛_mod to be represented additively, as modules (Example 3.6 (ii)): 'adding' two elements of a Γ-torsor is meaningful only if Γ is additively closed. The additive representation is used to relate objects of F^⊛_mod on opposite sides of the enhanced Θ^{×μ}_gau-link, a priori related only multiplicatively at the level of realifications, by means of additive mono-analytic log-shells (IUTchII, Remark 4.7.2). (ii) The construction of F^⊛_mod (fraktur) depends essentially on the additive structure of F^×_mod, whereas that of F^⊛_MOD is strictly multiplicative; the construction of Example 3.6 (i) is essentially that of [FrdI], Example 6.3 ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (i)); F^⊛_MOD is identified with F^⊛_mod via the natural isomorphism of Example 3.6 (i), as often done below.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the Frobenioids of Example 3.6
  • for (b): a subgroup Γ ⊆ F^×_mod; S ⊆ V_mod a nonempty finite subset

Conclusion.

Isomorphism classes of objects of the relevant Frobenioids are determined by divisor and rational function monoids; F^×_mod ∪ {0} carries a natural additive structure, which fails for the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification of F^⊛_mod and for subgroups Γ ⊆ F^×_mod not of the form K^× for a subfield K ⊆ F_mod; this is what allows the additive (module) representation of objects of F^⊛_mod used to relate the two sides of the enhanced Θ^{×μ}_gau-link via log-shells. Convention: F^⊛_MOD is identified with F^⊛_mod via Example 3.6 (i).

Obligations.

  • Formalize 'admits a natural additive structure' for a subgroup Γ ⊆ F^×_mod as: Γ ∪ {0} is closed under addition (then it is K^× ∪ {0} for a subfield K); prove that {1} and the S-unit groups for nonempty finite S are not additively closed (elementary), and that the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification carry no such structure.
  • The determination of isomorphism classes by the divisor and rational function monoids is cited from [FrdI], Theorem 5.2.

Ambiguities.

IUT3.Rem3_8_1Remark 3.8.1
Record

The LGP-Gaussian and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices are closely related; the theory mainly uses the LGP-Gaussian one (reasons in Remark 3.10.1 (ii)), but the computation of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link involves the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link and related Θ-pilot objects essentially. Both the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link map Θ-pilot objects to q-pilot objects. The terminology 'Θ-pilot/q-pilot objects' is consistent with the notion of pilot object associated to an F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip (IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the links and pilot objects of Definition 3.8

Conclusion.

The Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links each map Θ-pilot objects to q-pilot objects, and these pilot objects are pilot objects in the sense of IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii).

Obligations.

  • Prove that every isomorphism of the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}LGP ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}△ (resp. lgp) carries the Θ-pilot object to the q-pilot object (page 114: 'we note, for future reference'; no argument is given). This requires that the Θ-pilot object is the pilot object of †F^{⊩▶×μ}LGP and the q-pilot object that of *F^{⊩▶×μ}△ in the sense of IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii), and that isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips preserve pilot objects.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 114 states the mapping property and the consistency of terminology without argument.

The local holomorphic integral structures have log-volume 0; multiplying by p_v adds −log(p_v) (nonarchimedean); multiplying by e adds 1 (archimedean). μ^log_{A,v_Q} is invariant under permutations of A. Procession-normalization: average over the capsules of a procession.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • v ∈ V, v | v_Q, α ∈ A

    Conclusion.

    Log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,α,v} : M(I^Q(−)) → R exist, determined by the p_{v_Q}-adic (respectively radial) log-volumes on the direct summand fields and the normalized weights of Rem 3.1.1 (ii) to (iv); the integral structures of Prop 3.1 (ii) have log-volume 0; multiplication by p_v adds −log(p_v) (respectively by e adds 1); μ^log_{A,v_Q} is invariant under permutations of A; on products over the capsules of a procession (as in Prop 3.4 (ii)) the procession-normalized log-volume is the average over the capsules.

    Obligations.

    • Define the local log-volume on each direct summand field K_v as the logarithm of Haar measure normalized by μ(O_{K_v}) = 1 (p_{v_Q}-adic; radial at archimedean v_Q), and form the packet log-volume with the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, namely 1/([K_v : (F_mod)v]·Σ{w | v_Q} [(F_mod)w : Q{v_Q}]). These weights already contain the division by the local degree: with one place over v_Q, (F_mod)_v = Q_p and K_v quadratic, the plain Haar log-volume of p·O_{K_v} is −2·log(p) and the weight is 1/2, giving −log(p) as page 115 requires. Equivalently, one may divide each local Haar log-volume by its degree (as IUT IV, Proposition 1.4 (i), page 13, does) and then use weights without that factor; doing both divides twice and gives −(1/2)·log(p) in the example. A formalization must use exactly one of the two conventions and check that the total shift under multiplication by p_v is −log(p_v). Done for tensor packets of finite extensions of Q_p on direct product regions with the first convention, weights applied to unnormalized summand log-volumes (IUT3.Prop3_9.i.frag.wpkt_logvol_def, IUT3.Prop3_9.i.frag.wpkt_logvol_tests); the second convention with the same weights gives the double division (IUT3.Prop3_9.i.frag.wpkt_double_division, a model test). IUT3.Rem3_9_1Remark 3.9.1
Record

Explicit descriptions in the spirit of Remark 3.1.1 (i). (i) For v_Q ∈ V^non_Q, let v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} be the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i} with ring of integers O_{k_i}, and I_i := (p*_{v_Q})^{-1}·log_{k_i}(O^×_{k_i}) ⊆ k_i, where p*_{v_Q} = p_v if p_{v_Q} is odd and p*_{v_Q} = p^2_{v_Q} if p_{v_Q} is even (Remark 1.2.2 (i)). Roughly, the mono-analytic integral structures of Proposition 3.2 (ii) in I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊕_i k_i and I^Q(AF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊗_{α∈A} I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) are I(αF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊕_i I_i and I(AF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊗_{α∈A} I(αF_{v_Q}), while the local holomorphic integral structures O_{αF_{v_Q}}, O_{AF_{v_Q}} of Proposition 3.9 (i) are the subrings of integers of these direct sums of finite extensions of Q_{p_{v_Q}}; by the formula of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (iii), for the log-volume of I_i, '[one verifies easily that]' the log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}(I(αF_{v_Q})) and μ^log_{A,v_Q}(I(AF_{v_Q})) can be computed entirely in terms of the initial Θ-data (details left to the reader). (ii) For v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q, with v_i, k_i as before, O_{k_i} := {λ ∈ k_i : |λ| ≤ 1} and I_i := π·O_{k_i} (Remark 1.2.2 (ii)), the discrepancy between the mono-analytic integral structures of Proposition 3.2 (ii), determined by I(†F_{v_i}) ≅ I_i ⊆ k_i, and the local holomorphic integral structures of Proposition 3.9 (i), in the topological rings I^Q(αF_{v_Q}), I^Q(AF_{v_Q}) (direct sums of complex archimedean fields), determined by taking the product of the respective sets of integers, may be computed entirely in terms of the initial Θ-data by two '[easily verified]' observations: (a) with the standard Hermitian metric on C, the tensor product metric on C ⊗_R C and the direct sum metric on C ⊕ C, any isomorphism of topological rings C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C (from the Chinese remainder theorem) is compatible with the metrics up to a factor of 2 (the metric on the right corresponds to 2 times the metric on the left); (b) the decomposition C ⊕ C with its Hermitian metric is preserved, relative to that isomorphism, by complex conjugation on either factor of C ⊗_R C and by multiplication by ±1 or ±√−1 via either factor; details left to the reader. (iii) The discrepancy between local holomorphic and mono-analytic integral structures is discussed further in IUTchIV, §1.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Proposition 3.9 (i) and Proposition 3.2 (ii)
  • for (i): v_Q ∈ V^non_Q, v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i}
  • for (ii): v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q, v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i}

Conclusion.

(i) At v_Q ∈ V^non_Q the mono-analytic integral structures are, roughly, ⊕_i I_i and its tensor powers, the holomorphic ones the rings of integers, and the log-volumes of the mono-analytic integral structures are computable from the initial Θ-data. (ii) At v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q the discrepancy between the two integral structures is computable from the initial Θ-data, using (a) C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C multiplies the metric by 2 and (b) the decomposition and metric are preserved by conjugations and by multiplication by ±1, ±√−1 on either factor.

Obligations.

  • Prove (ii) (a): for the isomorphism C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C, a ⊗ b ↦ (ab, a·b̄), the image of an element of squared norm 1 (e.g. 1 ⊗ 1 ↦ (1, 1)) has squared norm 2; check that every isomorphism of topological rings (composition with conjugations and the swap) has the same factor. Elementary and within reach of Mathlib.
  • Prove (ii) (b): invariance of the decomposition and metric under the listed operations.
  • Carry out the computation of (i) from AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (iii); page 118 leaves 'the routine details to the reader', as does page 119 for (ii).

Ambiguities.

  • Pages 118 to 119: the identifications are stated 'roughly speaking', so the exact form of the integral structures is not fixed here.
  • Page 119, (a): 'metric' must be read as the quadratic form (squared norm) for the factor to be 2; for the norm itself the factor is √2.
  • Page 118 (checked at 250 dpi): the parenthetical reads p*_{v_Q} = p_v (underlined v, an element of V) for p_{v_Q} odd and p^2_{v_Q} for p_{v_Q} even; the mixed subscripts agree since v lies over v_Q.
