Record

Makes the log-link compatibility of log-volumes of Proposition 3.9 (iv) more explicit through 'realified semi-simplifications' Rss(M) of measure spaces: (i) the formalism Sub(M), Fn(M), ∫_M and Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0}, with restriction to ample compact subsets and products; (ii) why mere dilation of volumes by the log-link would leave log-volumes defined only modulo Z·log(λ); (iii) the nonarchimedean diagram k ⊇ O_k^× → log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k induces compatible R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of the Rss's, compatible with finite extensions; (iv) at bad v, the log-Kummer operations k ⇝ O_k^× × q^N ⇝ O_k^× ⇝ log_k(O_k^×) ⇝ k induce such isomorphisms without interference with q^N, which embeds N in R ∪ {−∞} by 1 ↦ −log(q); (v) extension to topological tensor products k_{i_A}; (vi) the archimedean analogue via |k| = k/O_k^×.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of Proposition 3.9 (iv)

Conclusion.

A reformulation, not a new result: log-link compatibility of log-volumes at v ∈ V^non (iii), at v ∈ V^bad in the log-Kummer setting (iv), for tensor packets (v) and at v ∈ V^arc (vi) is expressed as the existence of R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of realified semi-simplifications compatible with the normalized log-volume maps. Statements in the part records.

  • IUT3.Rem3_9_4.i (part or step) extracted extracted
    Record

    Realified semi-simplification of a measure space. For a measure space (M, μ_M): S ⊆ M is pre-ample if it is a relatively compact Borel set, ample if moreover μ_M(S) > 0, and (M, μ_M) is ample if it has an ample subset. Sub(M) is the set of pre-ample subsets; Fn(M) the Borel functions f: M → R_{≥0} with finite image and f^{-1}(R_{>0}) ∈ Sub(M), a monoid with R_{>0}-action containing Sub(M) via characteristic functions. Integration ∫_M: Fn(M) ↠ R_{≥0} is an R_{>0}-equivariant surjection, Rss(M) is the quotient set it determines, and ∫^Rss_M: Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0}.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • (M, μ_M) an ample measure space in the sense of Remark 3.1.1 (iii)

    Conclusion.

    (a) ∫M: Fn(M) → R{≥0} is an R_{>0}-equivariant surjection restricting to S ↦ μ_M(S) on Sub(M), and induces an R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism of monoids ∫^Rss_M: Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0} with ∫_M = ∫^Rss_M ∘ FnRss_M; on Sub(M) the quotient identifies S₁, S₂ with μ_M(S₁) = μ_M(S₂) and sends a disjoint union to the sum. (b) If S ∈ Sub(M) is ample and compact, (S, μ_M|S) is ample, extension by zero gives inclusions Sub(S) ⊆ Sub(M), Fn(S) ⊆ Fn(M), and there are R{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(S) ≅ R_{≥0}·Rss(Fn(S)) ≅ Rss(M) compatible with ∫^Rss_S and ∫^Rss_M. (c) For ample (M₁, μ₁), (M₂, μ₂) the product is ample, and (S₁, S₂) ↦ S₁ × S₂ induces an R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism Rss(M₁) ⊗ Rss(M₂) ≅ Rss(M₁ × M₂) compatible with ∫^Rss_{M₁} ⊗ ∫^Rss_{M₂} and ∫^Rss_{M₁×M₂}, where a tensor product of monoids isomorphic to R_{≥0} is defined via groupification as a one-dimensional R-vector space with a R_{>0}-torsor of positive elements.

    Obligations.

    • Elementary measure theory within reach of Mathlib: define Fn(M) as simple functions with relatively compact support, prove that integration is an R_{>0}-equivariant monoid surjection onto R_{≥0} (surjectivity uses an ample subset and scaling), so the quotient by the fibers of ∫ is canonically R_{≥0}; prove the product statement from the product measure.

    Ambiguities.

    • Rss(M) is the quotient by the fibers of ∫M, so the isomorphism Rss(M) ≅ R{≥0} holds by construction once ∫M is surjective; the content of the formalism is the bookkeeping of R{>0}-equivariance and compatibilities, not a nontrivial theorem.

  • IUT3.Rem3_9_4.ii (part or step) extracted extracted
    Record

    A very rough heuristic: if one knew only that each application of the log-link dilates volumes by a factor λ ∈ R_{>0} \ {1}, then log-volumes consistent with all arrows of the log-Kummer correspondence would be well defined only in R/Z·log(λ) ≅ S¹, which is unacceptable for the log-volume estimates of Corollary 3.12. Example: on (Q_p, μ_{Q_p}) with μ(Z_p) = 1, multiplication by p induces bijections Sub(α_p), Fn(α_p), Rss(α_p), and Rss(α_p) is compatible with ∫^Rss_{Q_p} on both sides only up to the factor p^{-1}.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • for the example: a prime p, M = Q_p with additive Haar measure normalized by μ(Z_p) = 1

    Conclusion.

    (a) Multiplication by p on Q_p scales Haar measure by p^{-1}, so Rss(α_p) is not compatible with ∫^Rss_{Q_p} on domain and codomain, only up to the factor p^{-1} ≠ 1. (b) Heuristic: under a dilation by λ ≠ 1 per log-link, consistently computed log-volumes would lie in R/Z·log(λ).

    Obligations.

    • (a) is the standard scaling property of Haar measure on Q_p under multiplication by p (whether Mathlib states it in this form was not checked); (b) is a heuristic with no claim to prove.

    Record

    Nonarchimedean formulation of log-link compatibility via Rss, and compatibility with finite extensions.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • k as in Remark 1.2.2 (i) (a finite extension of Q_{p_v}), with additive Haar measure μ_k normalized by μ_k(O_k) = 1
    • for the extension statement: finite extensions k₁ ⊆ k₂ of Q_{p_v}

    Conclusion.

    (a) (k, μ_k) is ample and O_k^× ⊆ k is ample; for any compact ample S ⊆ O_k^× on which log_k is injective, μ_k(S) = μ_k(log_k(S)) (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7 (i), (c)); such S exist. (b) Hence the diagram k ⊇ O_k^× → log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k induces a commutative diagram of R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(k) ← Rss(O_k^×) ← Rss(S) → Rss(log_k(S)) → Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) → Rss(k) over R_{≥0}, the composite Rss(O_k^×) ≅ Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) being independent of S; composing with log: R_{≥0} ≅ R ∪ {−∞} and a normalization factor, these isomorphisms are compatible with the log-volume maps. (c) Since O_{k₂} is free of rank [k₂ : k₁] over O_{k₁} and Haar measure is invariant under automorphisms, k₁ ⊆ k₂ induces Rss(k₁)^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} ≅ Rss(O_{k₁})^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} ≅ Rss(O_{k₂}) ≅ Rss(k₂), compatible with (∫^Rss_{k₁})^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} and ∫^Rss_{k₂}.

    Obligations.

Holomorphic hulls of regions (pages 126 to 145), in ten parts: (i) definition of the holomorphic hull of a region of I^Q(−) containing a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume; (ii) ℙ (direct product regions), ℍ (hulls) and the hull map φ : ℙ → ℍ, characterized by (P1) φ(H) = H, (P2) P ⊆ φ(P), (P3) monotonicity, with φ(P) = ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P} H; (iii) hull-approximants Φ(P) ⊇ Ξ(P) and H_{Φ(P)}, H_{Ξ(P)}, a compact indeterminacy; (iv) φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)}, conditions (Ξ1), (Ξ2) for Ξ(P) ≠ ∅, strictness (Ξ3) and the example I = Q_p × Q_p; (v) the set-theoretic quotient E ⊼ S as a formalization of upper semi-commutativity; (vi) its application to S = φ(P) and to bounded families P_B; (vii) the obstructions (Ob1) to (Ob9) to comparing the output of the multiradial algorithms with the q-pilot object and their elimination via hulls, det_{⊗M}(−), the ⊼-formalism and the log-Kummer correspondence; (viii) to (x) the (sub)quotient operations (sQ1) to (sQ5), the compatibilities (cQ3), (cQ4) versus (iQ5), the 'closed loop', and why hulls and arithmetic line bundles over F_mod cannot be replaced by categories of regions or by line bundles over Q.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the situation of Proposition 3.9 (i)
  • regions of I^Q(αF_{v_Q}), I^Q(AF_{v_Q}), I^Q(A,αF_v) as in Remark 3.1.1 (iii), (iv) and Remark 3.9.4

Conclusion.

Definitions: the holomorphic hull (i), the hull map φ : ℙ → ℍ with φ(P) = ⋂{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P} H (ii), the hull-approximants Φ(P), Ξ(P) (iii), the quotient E ⊼ S (v). Assertions: the hull is well defined (i); φ is uniquely characterized by (P1) to (P3) and any intersection of elements of ℍ of finite log-volume lies in ℍ (ii); φ(P) ∈ Φ(P), φ(P) = H{Φ(P)}, Ξ(P) ≠ ∅ under (Ξ1) or globally (Ξ2), and μ^log(P) < μ^log(H_{Ξ(P)}) can occur (Ξ3) (iv); set maps between nonempty subsets of S induce identities on ⊼_S (v); H_1 ~ H_2 ⟺ H_1, H_2 ⊆ φ(P) under the quotient by φ(P) (vi). Parts (vii) to (x) are interpretive; see the part records.

    Record

    For a subset U of I^Q(−) that contains a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume: if U is relatively compact, its holomorphic hull is the smallest subset λ·O (λ with every component nonzero in the direct sum decomposition) containing U; otherwise the hull is all of I^Q(−). 'One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined.'

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • the situation of Prop 3.9 (i)
    • a subset U of I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) (respectively I^Q(AF_{v_Q}), I^Q(A,αF_v)) containing a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume (> −∞)

    Conclusion.

    The holomorphic hull of a relatively compact U is the smallest subset λ·O (λ with every component nonzero) containing U; the hull of a U that is not relatively compact is all of I^Q(−); 'one verifies immediately' that the hull is well defined.

    Obligations.

    • Prove existence and uniqueness of a smallest λ·O containing a relatively compact U (componentwise this is the smallest scaled ring of integers containing the projection, which exists by discreteness of the value group).
    • Prove the hull is independent of the choice of λ among those giving the same set.
    • On a finite product of finite extensions of Q_p in place of the direct sum of fields of I^Q(-), the smallest set lambda O containing a relatively compact U that contains a subset of positive Haar measure exists and is the hull (IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i.frag.pkt_isLeast_spectral); tensor packets, I^Q(-) itself and the archimedean case are open.
    • On Q_p^2, the log-volume of the hull is not a function of the log-volume of the region (IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i.frag.hull_deg_not_descent, a model test); this concerns the model, not the regions of the proof of Corollary 3.12.

    Ambiguities.

    • At archimedean components the ring O is a closed unit ball in C; 'smallest λ·O' then refers to the smallest closed ball, which exists by compactness; the text does not separate the cases.

On the sets lambda O, mu^log(hull) = mu^log, so equal mu^log gives equal mu^log of hulls.

  • IUT3.Rem3_9_5.v (part or step) extracted extracted
    Record

    The 'upper' quotient: for a set E and a proper subset S ⊆ E of cardinality at least 2, E ⊼ S := (E \ S) ⊔ {S} is the quotient of E collapsing S to a point, with ⊼_S := {S} ⊆ E ⊼ S. Any set map S₁ → S₂ between nonempty subsets of S induces on the quotient the identity map of ⊼_S, lying over the identity of E ⊼ S. This extends to empty S_i treated as formal intersections (formal inverse systems over E of nonempty subsets of S), so 'formal empty sets' in S also map to ⊼_S. Proposed as an abstract set-theoretic formalization of upper semi-commutativity/semi-compatibility (Remarks 1.2.2 (iii), 1.5.4 (iii), Proposition 3.5 (ii)), with S ⊆ E taken to be I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)); there the empty set always arises as the intersection of a nonempty set with the domain of definition of a set-theoretic logarithm map.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • E a set, S ⊆ E a proper subset of cardinality ≥ 2
    • S₁, S₂ ⊆ S nonempty subsets and a map S₁ → S₂ (or formal inverse systems of nonempty subsets of S, for the extension to empty S_i)

    Conclusion.

    Every set map S₁ → S₂ between nonempty subsets of S induces, after passing to E ↠ E ⊼ S, the identity map ⊼_S → ⊼_S (the images of S₁ and S₂ both equal ⊼_S), lying over the identity of E ⊼ S; the same holds for formal inverse systems, so formal empty subsets of S also map to ⊼_S.

    Obligations.

    • Elementary and within reach of Lean and Mathlib: define the quotient of E by the relation collapsing S (for example as a Quot by the relation x ~ y iff x = y or x, y ∈ S) and prove that the image of any nonempty subset of S is the single class of S, so that any map S₁ → S₂ descends to the identity on that class.
    • The extension to empty S_i via formal inverse systems needs a definition of 'formal intersection' before it can be stated.

    Ambiguities.

    • The extension to empty S_i (page 130) is described informally ('treated as a formal intersection'); no definition of the formal inverse system is given.
    • The claim that this is a formalization of upper semi-commutativity (page 130) is interpretive; how the containments of Proposition 3.5 (ii) become maps S₁ → S₂ is not specified.

    Pages read: rendered and checked: pages 129, 130

    Record

    Applies the ⊼-formalism of (v) with S ⊆ E taken to be φ(P) ⊆ I^Q((−)) for P ∈ ℙ, to identify P with its log-volume hull-approximants in Φ(P) or Ξ(P) (nonempty subsets of φ(P) ∈ ℍ), passing to a quotient in which the indeterminacy discussed in (iii) is eliminated; also for bounded families P_B = {P_β}_{β ∈ B} of elements of ℙ with relatively compact union, using φ(P_B) := ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P_β ∀β} H.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • P ∈ ℙ (direct product regions), with hull φ(P) ∈ ℍ and hull-approximants Φ(P), Ξ(P) as in IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii and IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv
    • for the family version: a collection P_B = {P_β}_{β ∈ B} ⊆ ℙ with ⋃_β P_β ⊆ I^Q((−)) relatively compact

    Implicit hypotheses.

    • φ(P) is a proper subset of I^Q((−)) of cardinality ≥ 2, as (v) requires; this holds since φ(P) ∈ ℍ consists of hulls H ⊊ I^Q((−)) with nonempty interior

    Conclusion.

    Under the quotient map I^Q((−)) ↠ I^Q((−)) ⊼ φ(P), the images of H₁, H₂ ∈ ℍ coincide if and only if H₁, H₂ ⊆ φ(P); so the equivalence relation on ℍ induced by the quotient is H₁ ~ H₂ ⟺ H₁, H₂ ⊆ φ(P). The same applies to bounded families P_B with φ(P_B) := ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P_β for all β ∈ B} H.

    Obligations.

    • State and prove the displayed equivalence. The 'if' direction is immediate from (v). The 'only if' direction is not a general fact about quotients: for arbitrary subsets H₁ ≠ H₂ of E that both meet φ(P) and agree outside φ(P), the images coincide. Assessment (drawing on the description of hulls in IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i, page 127, not re-read for this record): it should hold for hulls because a hull is a product over the direct summands of fractional ideals λ·O, and such a product not contained in φ(P) is determined by its part outside φ(P); a formalization must use this shape of hulls.

    Why the hull plays a crucial role in Corollary 3.12: the output of possible images of the multiradial algorithms of Theorem 3.11 cannot be directly compared, in any a priori sense, with the objects of the local and global Frobenioids in the codomain F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link determined by the arithmetic line bundle giving rise to the q-pilot object (Definition 3.8 (i), (ii); IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)). The obstructions and how they are eliminated: (Ob1) O^×-indeterminacies on tensor packets of log-shells: the possible images are regions (elements of ℙ) in tensor packets of log-shells I_k (notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), nonarchimedean), whereas the q-pilot line bundle is locally an ideal in the O_k-module O^mdl_k, which, unlike the ring O_k, has no canonical generator, only one up to multiplication by O^×_k, which does not stabilize I_k. (Ob2) Passing from a region P to its hull φ(P) ∈ ℍ gives a region stabilized by O^×_k that defines the local portion of a global arithmetic vector bundle relative to the ring structure labeled by some α ∈ A (typically the zero label 0 ∈ |F_l| when 0 ∈ A). (Ob3) Taking the determinant of the arithmetic vector bundle given by a hull yields an arithmetic line bundle, comparable with the q-pilot objects: (Ob3-1) weighted tensor powers/determinant: (Ob3-1-1) to be consistent with log-volumes as weighted sums (Remark 3.1.1), one takes suitable positive tensor powers, given by the weights (products of the N_v of Remark 3.1.1 (iv)), of the determinant line bundles of the direct summands of the tensor packet, and (Ob3-1-2) one tensors with the inverse of the 'determinant' of the structure sheaf O_(−) of Proposition 3.9 (i), an adjustment for ramification (routine details left to the reader); (Ob3-2) the exponents need not be relatively prime, so the operation is a 'determinant raised to some positive tensor power', written det_{⊗M}(−), with M the uniquely determined positive integer (cf. N_E of Remark 3.1.1 (iv)) such that det_{⊗M}(−) maps the result of tensoring O_(−) (Proposition 3.9 (i)) with an arithmetic line bundle to the M-th tensor power of that arithmetic line bundle; taking M sufficiently divisible one may assume the localization at each v ∈ V of any output of det_{⊗M}(−) is trivial (stack-theoretic twists at v ∈ V^bad, IUTchI, Remark 3.1.5); (Ob3-3) since the arithmetic degree of the output may be read, with suitable normalization factors, as the log-volume of the original arithmetic vector bundle, the step det_{⊗M}(−) may be omitted when only log-volumes are computed. (Ob4) Hence det_{⊗M}(−) yields objects comparable with the M-th tensor power of the q-pilot object; this 'slightly modified goal' causes no substantive problem (no indeterminacy confusing a line bundle with its M-th power, unlike I^ord in Remark 2.3.3 (vi)), because: (Ob4-1) the tensor-power Frobenioids are copies of the non-tensor-power ones via the naive Frobenius functor of degree M ([FrdI], Proposition 2.1 (i)), which determine them completely; (Ob4-2) conversely, extracting M-th roots determines the non-tensor-power Frobenioids only up to twists, since the rational function monoids ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (ii)) of the local Frobenioids are not divisible at v ∈ V^non; (Ob4-3) these 'tensor-power-twist indeterminacies' have no substantive effect on log-volume estimates (Ob3-3). (Ob5) Selecting a specific element of the collection of possible regions is internal to the algorithm; comparison with external objects such as the q-pilot line bundle requires independence of that choice, achieved by working with the hull φ(P_B) of the bounded collection P_B = {P_β}_{β∈B} of possible regions output by the algorithm and the ⊼-formalism of (v), (vi); the ⊼-formalism applies also, compatibly, to det_{⊗M}(φ(P_B)) and μ^log(φ(P_B)). (Ob6) Replacing P by μ^log(P) is tempting, but comparability with the q-pilot object forces hulls; Ξ(P) may be empty (iv), so Φ(P) is more natural, and independence of the choice (Ob5) forces μ^log(H_{Φ(P)}) or μ^log(H_{Ξ(P)}) in place of μ^log(P), which may be > μ^log(P) and indeed = μ^log(φ(P)) (iv). (Ob7) Why log-volumes cannot be the 'ultimate stage for comparison', i.e. why the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion (for v ∈ V^non, the local Galois groups G_v and units O^{×μ}_{F_v}, with their auxiliary structures, IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (i), (v), (vii)) cannot be eliminated from the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link: (Ob7-1) the G_v are invariant up to isomorphism under the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and log-links (vertical and horizontal coricity, Theorem 1.5 (i), (ii)), which the theory needs; (Ob7-2) eliminating only the Frobenius-like units, i.e. using F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips (Definition 2.4 (iii)), fails because the Frobenius-like units in the link are related only to those at the same vertical coordinate, consistently with the ring structure of their Hodge theater, while their étale-like counterparts O^{×μ}(G_v) (IUTchII, Example 1.8 (iv)) are related by vertical coricity and the log-Kummer correspondences to the Frobenius-like units at every vertical coordinate, subject to arbitrary iterates of the log-link and a complicated confusion of unit group and value group portions; using étale-like units as the sole access route would make the data of the F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips 'over-constrained/over-determined'. So one cannot eliminate the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion; its inclusion underlies the log-Kummer correspondences and log-shells as multiradial containers. (Ob8) The output of the multiradial algorithms, even with hulls, yields a priori objects that differ from the corresponding multiplicative local and global Frobenioids of the input data by a vertical shift (an application of the log-link, which produces additive log-shells from the multiplicative O^{×μ}); applying the log-Kummer correspondence gives objects meaningfully comparable with the input data (Step (xi-d) of the proof of Corollary 3.12), but these belong to Frobenioids subject to the indeterminacies of arbitrary iterates of the log-link (Remark 3.12.2 (v)). (Ob9) Passing to realified semi-simplifications (Remark 3.9.4 (iii) to (vi)) in log-link compatibility of log-volumes is a quotient operation inducing a natural bijection between log-volumes of hulls in domain and codomain of the log-link, unaffected by the use of non-hull regions at intermediate steps, because: (Ob9-1) once comparable objects are obtained via det_{⊗M}(−) of a hull, the formal indeterminacies arising (the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies of (Ob4-3), the ⊼-formalism of (Ob5), the arbitrary iterates of the log-link of (Ob8)) do not affect comparability and act only as compatibility conditions for passing to coarse invariants such as the log-volume; (Ob9-2) by contrast, in (Ob1) to (Ob5) comparable objects had not yet been obtained, so the relation between the non-comparable output and comparable objects had not been explicitly computed. Related issues are discussed in (ix).

    Explicit hypotheses.

The theory may be regarded as a collection of (sub)quotient operation algorithms producing a relatively simple concrete (sub)quotient of the log-theta-lattice, whose goal is the computation of the projection of the 'Θ-intertwining' (the structure on an abstract F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip as arising from the Θ-pilot object in the domain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link) onto structures from the vertical column in the codomain, where the 'q-intertwining' (as arising from the q-pilot object in the codomain) is in force; this computation, 'when suitably interpreted, amounts, essentially tautologically, to the inequality of Corollary 3.12'. Each operation simplifies by introducing indeterminacies, balancing minimal indeterminacy against compatibility with prior structures (discussed for (sQ1) in Remarks 1.5.4, 2.1.1, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.3, 3.10.1 (ii), (iii); (sQ2) in IUTchII, Remark 1.12.4; (sQ3) in (Ob1) to (Ob7); (sQ4) in (Ob8); (sQ5) in Remark 3.9.4 and (Ob9)). [FrdII], Example 5.6 (iii), (iv)) give, with the analogous category of local-global collections (⊼^fQ_2), a 'formal, or stack-theoretic, quotient' ⊼^fQ_2 modulo ⊼^fQ_1, like the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies (Ob4-3) and log-link iterates (Ob8), as opposed to coarse quotients such as the log-volume. The log-link compatibility of Proposition 3.9 (iv) is a coincidence of log-volumes not of arbitrary regions but of certain sufficiently small regions in the domain and codomain of the log-link; the product formula, that is the ratios of conversion between log-volumes at distinct v (IUTchI, Remark 3.5.1 (ii)), can be formulated without loss of generality in terms of such regions.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the context of Proposition 3.9 (iii), (iv)

Conclusion.

Proposition 3.9 (iv) implies compatibility of the product formulas (ratios of conversion between log-volumes at distinct v ∈ V) in the domain and codomain of the log-link, and hence, in the context of Proposition 3.9 (iii), compatibility between global arithmetic degrees in the domain and codomain of the log-link.

Obligations.

  • Define 'sufficiently small region' and 'compatibility of product formulas' and prove that the product formula can be expressed with such regions without loss of generality, as asserted on page 145.

Elementary observations on computing log-volumes of regions as in Proposition 3.9: (i) the condition 'zero log-volume for all but finitely many v_Q' can be met by taking, at all but finitely many nonarchimedean w_Q with p_{w_Q} unramified in K, the component I(A F_{w_Q}) ⊆ I^Q(A F_{w_Q}), which has zero log-volume, is a mono-analytic invariant and equals its own holomorphic hull; (ii) log-volumes of more general relatively compact E ⊆ I^Q((−)) may be defined as the infimum over E* ∈ M(I^Q((−))) containing E, possibly −∞, or essentially equivalently via the inverse system of such E* (of direct product regions when E is a direct product pre-region), which keeps log-volumes finite; (iii) the same for collections {E_{v_Q}} contained in collections {E*_{v_Q}} as in (i).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii), (iii); for (i), w_Q ∈ V_Q^non with p_{w_Q} unramified in K

Conclusion.

(i) For each nonarchimedean w_Q with p_{w_Q} unramified in K, O_{(−)} = I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)) has zero log-volume, is a mono-analytic invariant, and equals its own holomorphic hull. (ii) and (iii) are definitions: log-volume of a relatively compact E (or a collection {E_{v_Q}}) as the infimum of log-volumes of admissible supersets, with value possibly −∞; essentially equivalent to working with the inverse system of such supersets.

Obligations.

  • Prove (i): for p_{w_Q} unramified in K, the subset I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)) has zero normalized log-volume and is its own holomorphic hull (the text cites Proposition 3.2 (ii), Proposition 3.9 (i) and the final sentence of AbsTopIII, Definition 5.4 (iii)).
  • Make 'essentially equivalently' in (ii), (iii) precise: the infimum of the inverse system's log-volumes equals the infimum definition.

Ambiguities.

  • 'Essentially equivalently' (pages 146, 147) is not explained; the inverse-system formulation keeps log-volumes finite while the infimum can be −∞, so the two are not literally the same.

Global Kummer theory and non-interference with local integers, for a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,mHT} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, with n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater determined up to isomorphism by the vertical coricity of Theorem 1.5 (i): (i) vertically coric global LGP- and 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Frobenioids with Kummer isomorphisms; (ii) the global number field meets the product of local integral monoids only in roots of unity, and a log-Kummer correspondence invariant under vertical translation; (iii) log-link-compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD and of F^{⊩⊥}-prime-strips.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m ∈ Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data, thought of as arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii), Proposition 3.5, Remark 3.8.2)
  • for each n, n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} determined up to isomorphism via the vertical coricity of Theorem 1.5 (i)

(i) functorial algorithms in n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} giving vertically coric number fields, monoids, Frobenioids and F^⊩-prime-strips, with Kummer isomorphisms from the corresponding objects of each n,mHT, compatible with the non-coric algorithms of Proposition 3.7; (ii) (†M^⊛_MOD)_α ∩ ∏v Ψ{log(A,αF_v)} = (†M^{⊛μ}_MOD)_α, the roots of unity, inside ∏_v I^Q(A,αF_v) = I^Q(A F_{V_Q}); and the actions of the groups (n,mM^⊛_MOD)j on I^Q(S^±{j+1}F(n,◦D_≻)_{V_Q}) via all pre-composites of Kummer isomorphisms with iterates of log-links are mutually compatible up to identity indeterminacies at adjacent m, giving a log-Kummer correspondence invariant under the vertical translation symmetries; (iii) isomorphisms (n,mF^⊛_MOD)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α, their realifications, and n,m𝔉^{⊩⊥}_LGP ≅ 𝔉^{⊩⊥}(n,◦HT^D)_LGP, all mutually compatible as m varies with the log-links.     (a) (†M^⊛_MOD)α ∩ ∏{v ∈ V} Ψ_{log(A,αF_v)} = (†M^{⊛μ}_MOD)_α, the finite subgroup of roots of unity, the intersection taken in ∏_v I^Q(A,αF_v) = ∏_{v_Q} I^Q(A F_{v_Q}) = I^Q(A F_{V_Q}). IUT3.Rem3_10_1Remark 3.10.1
Record

(i) The log-Kummer correspondence induces the isomorphisms of Proposition 3.10 (iii) for F^⊛_MOD because its construction uses only (†M^⊛_MOD)_α and subquotients of its perfection; F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡 uses local monoids subject only to the upper semi-compatible log-Kummer correspondence of Proposition 3.5 (ii), so no log-link-compatible isomorphisms of that kind exist for it. (ii) The precise compatibility of F^⊛_MOD makes it suited to Kummer-detachment indeterminacies (the mutual compatibility in Proposition 3.10 (iii) asserts in effect that they do not arise), which is why the LGP- rather than 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Gaussian lattice is used; its multiplicative nature makes it ill-suited to étale-transport indeterminacies. (iii) F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡, additive and closely related to coric mono-analytic log-shells, is suited to étale-transport indeterminacies; despite distortions one may compute (estimate) global arithmetic degrees of its objects via bi-coric log-volumes (Proposition 3.9), the topic of Corollary 3.12, with concrete estimates in IUTchIV. (iv) Fig. 3.2 summarizes; the isomorphisms F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡(n,◦HT^D)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α and F^⊩(…)_LGP ≅ F^⊩(…)_𝔩𝔤𝔭 of Proposition 3.10 (i) relate the multiplicatively and additively biased Frobenioids via the global ring structure of the number field.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of IUT3.Prop3_10

Conclusion.

Interpretive. The only mathematical assertions are: (i) one cannot construct log-link-compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids for (†F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_α as in Proposition 3.10 (iii) (page 150); (ii) the mutual compatibility of Proposition 3.10 (iii) amounts to the absence of Kummer-detachment indeterminacies for F^⊛_MOD/LGP-structures (page 150).

Obligations.

  • Make 'cannot construct log-link-compatible isomorphisms for F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡' a precise non-existence statement and prove it.
  • Define Kummer-detachment indeterminacy precisely enough to state that it 'does not arise'.

Ambiguities.

  • The impossibility claim in (i) (page 150) is argued from the imprecise nature of one-sided inclusions, not proved.
  • Fig. 3.2 (page 151) compares the two structures qualitatively ('rigid', 'subject to substantial distortion'); these are not mathematical statements.

The F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP, †F^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-, Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links (Definition 3.8 (ii)) were built from the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip †F^{⊩▶×μ}_env of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii). Working in the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii)), with '†' replaced by '(n, m)' or '(n, ◦)', there is a commutative diagram of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips: upper row F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_env ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_gau ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_LGP ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_lgp, lower row n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_gau ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp, with vertical arrows from lower to upper row. Here 'n,◦' abbreviates n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} (Proposition 3.10 (i)); the first vertical arrow is the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip version of the Kummer isomorphism of the final display of Proposition 2.1 (ii) (cf. Proposition 2.1 (iii), (iv), (v)); the second to fourth vertical arrows are those of the Kummer isomorphisms of the final display of Proposition 3.10 (i); the first lower horizontal arrow is the version of the evaluation isomorphism of the final display of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii); the second and third lower horizontal arrows are the versions of the tautological isomorphisms of the final displays of Proposition 3.7 (iii), (iv); the first upper horizontal arrow is the version of the étale-like evaluation isomorphism implicit (via IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (iv), (v)) in the construction of that evaluation isomorphism; the second and third upper horizontal arrows are the versions of the natural isomorphisms of the second display of Proposition 3.10 (i). In summary, n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP and n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp were constructed from n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env and are related to it by the lower horizontal arrows, each of which may be constructed by conjugating the corresponding upper horizontal arrow by the Kummer isomorphisms (the vertical arrows).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice of Definition 3.8 (iii), with † replaced by (n, m) or (n, ◦)
  • the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 (ii) and Proposition 3.10 (i)

Conclusion.

The displayed diagram of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips commutes ('from the theory developed so far', page 152); hence n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP and n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp are obtained from n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env via the lower horizontal arrows, each of which is the conjugate of the corresponding upper horizontal arrow by the vertical Kummer isomorphisms.

Obligations.

  • Prove commutativity of each square of the diagram on page 152 from the cited constructions; the text recalls it 'from the theory developed so far' and gives no argument.

  • Page 152: the diagram mixes Frobenius-like (lower row, labeled n,m) and étale-like (upper row, labeled n,◦) data; the vertical arrows depend on m through the Kummer isomorphisms, which the notation does not show.

Record

Multiradial algorithms via LGP-monoids and Frobenioids, for an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice. Three parts: (i) multiradial representation, (ii) log-Kummer correspondence, (iii) Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibility. Proof: the assertions 'follow immediately from the definitions and the references quoted'. Not stated as a Lean Prop: the vocabulary does not exist.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in IUTchI Def 3.1
  • a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,m HT}_{n,m ∈ Z} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice

Implicit hypotheses.

  • the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater n,◦HT is determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Thm 1.5 (i), Rem 3.8.2)

Conclusion.

(i) the data (a), (b), (c), regarded up to (Ind1) and (Ind2), are constructible by an algorithm in the procession, functorial in isomorphisms of processions, and the étale-picture permutation symmetries induce compatible poly-isomorphisms; (ii) Kummer isomorphisms relate these coric data to the data of each n,m HT, mutually compatible along columns for (b) and the MOD part of (c), upper semi-compatible for (a) (Ind3), and compatible with log-volumes; (iii) these constructions are compatible with the horizontal arrows, for (iii)(c), (d) up to (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3).

Obligations.

  • See part records; docs/THEOREM_3_11.md separates each claim.

IUT3.Rem3_11_2Remark 3.11.2
Record

(i) Theorem 3.11 (i) does not use the multiradiality formalism of IUTchII, §1, but its approach (data (a), (b), (c) up to (Ind1), (Ind2)) is essentially a special case of the tautological approach of IUTchII, Example 1.9 (ii), applied to the vertically coric, a priori uniradial, constructions of Propositions 3.5 (i), 3.10 (i). (ii) The transitions symmetry to labels to processions (Fig. 3.3: F_l^{⋊±} ⇒ F_l ⇒ |F_l| ⇒ ±-processions; F_l^* ⇒ F_l^* labels ⇒ ⊛-processions, with F_l^* ↪ |F_l|) require all labels; the index sets of mono-analytic ±-processions are naked sets determined up to isomorphism by cardinality, so their construction is independent of the arithmetic holomorphic structures, which is what makes them usable in Theorem 3.11 (i); for j ∈ {0, ..., l*} there are j+1 possibilities for the element labeled j, giving (l*+1)! = l^±! label identifications. (iii) The Kummer isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioids in IUTchII, §4 (Corollary 4.6 (ii), (v)), built from quotients of local value groups by local units, fail to give a log-Kummer correspondence, since a multiplicative quotient by units corresponds across the log-link to an additive quotient by their logarithms; hence Theorem 3.11 (ii) uses F^⊛_MOD and F^⊛ℝ_MOD. (iv) For F^⊛ℝ_MOD-based Frobenioids the localization functors ‡ρ_v can be reconstructed from the effect of multiplication by global monoids on log-volumes of local mono-analytic tensor packets (routine details left to the reader); this, with the incompatibilities in (iii), is why splitting monoids at good v are omitted from Theorem 3.11.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11

Conclusion.

Interpretive. Mathematical claims: (ii) the number of label identifications for the index sets of capsules in mono-analytic ±-processions is (l*+1)! = l^±!; the construction of these index sets is independent of the arithmetic holomorphic structures. (iii) the Kummer isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioids of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (ii), (v), do not satisfy the mutual compatibility of the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (ii). (iv) the localization functors of the F^⊩-prime-strips n,m𝔉^⊩_LGP can be reconstructed from log-volume data.

Obligations.

  • The count (l*+1)! of label identifications is elementary: a choice of j+1 elements for each capsule of size j+1, j = 0, ..., l*, gives ∏_{j=0}^{l*} (j+1) = (l*+1)!; formalizable directly.
  • State and prove the failure in (iii) precisely (which compatibility fails, for which objects).
  • Prove the reconstructibility of the localization functors in (iv); the text leaves the routine details to the reader (page 169).

Ambiguities.

  • Page 168: '(l*+1)! = l^±!' is consistent with l^± = l* + 1; the count reads the procession as having capsules of sizes 1, ..., l* + 1 with one labeled element each to identify.
  • 'Essentially a special case of the tautological approach' (page 167) is not made precise.

IUT3.Rem3_11_3Remark 3.11.3
Record

Relation between the log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 3.11 (ii) and the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii). (i) The squares of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice are far from 1-commutative, but the bi-coricity of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv) may be interpreted as saying the squares are 1-commutative with respect to these bi-coric data. (ii) To relate both unit and value group portions of domain and codomain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link on adjacent vertical lines (n−1,∗), (n,∗), one must use a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (n−1,m) → (n,m); a vertically once-shifted approach (value groups at (n−1,m), (n,m), units at (n−1,m−1), (n,m−1)) fails a priori by the noncommutativity of (i); the single link needs the compatibility properties of Theorem 3.11 (iii) to insulate the cyclotomes of the Kummer theory of the étale theta function and κ-coric functions from the Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies. (iii) Treating units in a once-shifted fashion via bi-coricity requires relating Frobenius-like units to étale-like structures simultaneously via (a) the usual Kummer isomorphisms and (b) their composites with one iterate of the log-link, which is possible only with a relation invariant under pre-composition with iterates of the log-link, as achieved by the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii). (iv) Summary: these correspondences relate unit and value group portions across adjacent vertical lines, insulate the cyclotomes, and are compatible with bi-coricity of mono-analytic log-shells and hence with relating LGP-monoids on adjacent vertical lines; this plays a key role in the proof of Corollary 3.12.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11, an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice

Conclusion.

Interpretive; no new theorem. The claims a formalization would have to address: (i) squares of the lattice commute when restricted to bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells; (ii) a once-shifted correspondence of value groups and unit groups across adjacent vertical lines is not available a priori; (iii) a framework relating Frobenius-like to étale-like structures compatibly with both Kummer isomorphisms and their composites with the log-link exists only if it is invariant under pre-composition with iterates of the log-link, which the log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 3.11 (ii) provides.

Obligations.

  • Make (i) precise: for each square of the lattice, the two composites agree on the bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells up to the stated indeterminacies.
  • Make the 'only if' of (iii) precise ('may only be realized if', page 170) and prove it, or record it as motivation.

Ambiguities.

  • (i) uses 'may be interpreted as the statement that' (page 169): an interpretation of Theorem 1.5, not a separate claim.
  • The necessity claims of (ii), (iii) ('it is necessary', 'fails, at least from an a priori point of view', 'may only be realized if', pages 169 to 170) are not proved; they motivate the use of the log-Kummer correspondence in Corollary 3.12.

IUT3.Rem3_11_4Remark 3.11.4
Record

On the compatibility in the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d). (i) Using the log-Kummer correspondence there amounts to forgetting the labels of the Frobenius-like vertices and identifying their data with the étale-like core, so multiplication of the data of Theorem 3.11 (ii), (b), (c) by roots of unity must be identified with the identity: only orbits under roots of unity are meaningful. This is harmless for theta values, since the theory is invariant under multiplication of the theta values by 2l-th roots of unity (Fig. 3.4: μ_{2l} acting on {q^{j^2}}_{j=1..l*}), and for number fields, since one only uses global Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD, F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡 built from local data and the entire number field, which is stable under roots of unity (Fig. 3.5). The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism indeterminacies from forgetting labels (Remark 2.3.3 (vi)) are trivial for theta values and amount to multiplication by ±1 on copies of F_mod^× for number fields; for the local data at v ∈ V^non giving the holomorphic log-shells they are trivial, because cyclotomic rigidity there only relates geometric and arithmetic cyclotomes and no 'vicious circles' arise. Hence the a priori indeterminacies in the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) are 'invisible': no substantive effect on the objects. (ii) This list of indeterminacies is complete, since Kummer isomorphisms are completely determined by isomorphisms between cyclotomes and the Galois action on roots of elements of the monoid (FrdII, Definition 2.1 (ii)), and compatibility with Galois actions is tautological. (iii) The invisible indeterminacies of (i) are an analogue of (Ind3) for the data of Theorem 3.11 (ii), (a); multiradiality and radial/coric decoupling (Remarks 2.3.2, 2.3.3) assert that (Ind1), (Ind2) have no effect on the geometric containers underlying Theorem 3.11 (ii), (b), (c).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11, in particular the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d)

Implicit hypotheses.

  • the theta values q^{j^2} and copies of F_mod are considered only up to the stated root-of-unity actions

Conclusion.

Claims: (a) the indeterminacies that might arise a priori in the log-Kummer correspondence portions of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) are invisible, i.e., they have no substantive effect on the objects; this is the sense in which the compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d), is to be understood (page 172). (b) The list of such indeterminacies is complete (page 172), because Kummer isomorphisms are determined by (1) isomorphisms of cyclotomes and (2) the Galois action on roots of elements of the monoid (page 173).

Obligations.

  • Define 'no substantive effect' as a precise invariance: for each object used in Corollary 3.12 (log-volumes of hulls of unions of possible images), show it is invariant under the listed indeterminacies (roots of unity on theta values, ±1 on F_mod^×, identity on local cyclotomes).
  • Prove completeness (ii): every indeterminacy of the log-Kummer correspondence in Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) factors through a change of cyclotome isomorphism; the text's argument is a 'general nonsense' observation citing FrdII, Definition 2.1 (ii).
  • The claim that the theory is invariant under multiplication of theta values by 2l-th roots of unity must be traced to the earlier constructions (Remark 2.3.3).

Ambiguities.

  • 'Invisible' and 'no substantive effect' (page 172) are not defined; Corollary 3.12 relies on the compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d), whose meaning this remark fixes, so the precise reading matters for the proof of Corollary 3.12 (Step (xi)).
  • Completeness (ii) (pages 172 to 173) is argued informally; 'no possibility that further indeterminacies might arise' is not derived from a definition of indeterminacy.

IUT3.Cor3_12Corollary 3.12Log-volume Estimates for Θ-Pilot Objects
Record

Log-volume estimates for Θ-pilot objects. In the situation of Thm 3.11, with −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} and −|log(q)| ∈ R as defined in the statement (IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement), −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|. Proof: an opening reduction and Steps (i) to (xii). Not stated as a Lean Prop. Lean lemmas about the two numbers alone are recorded as fragments of IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement, IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction and IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.f; they do not formalize this corollary.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the situation of Thm 3.11

Conclusion.

Two conjuncts: (F) −|log(Θ)| ∈ R, and (I) −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|. The 'i.e.' clause of page 174 (C_Θ ≥ −1 for every real C_Θ with −|log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ·|log(q)|) reformulates (I) only: it holds vacuously when −|log(Θ)| = +∞ (IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.constantForm_of_top). The statement is therefore (F) ∧ (I), equivalently (F) ∧ (the 'i.e.' clause); finiteness is kept as a separate conjunct in both formulations.

Obligations.

  • See the step records and docs/COR312_ANALYSIS.md.

    Record

    −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume (average over j ∈ F*_l) of the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of a Θ-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms of Thm 3.11 (ii), in the multiradial representation of Thm 3.11 (i), subject to Ind1, Ind2, Ind3. −|log(q)| ∈ R is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the image of a q-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms, in the multiradial representation, not subject to the indeterminacies; △ is the result of identifying the labels 0 and ⟨F*_l⟩. |log(q)| > 0 is 'easily computed' from the q-parameters at v ∈ V^bad (≠ ∅).

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • situation of Thm 3.11

    Implicit hypotheses.

    • V^bad ≠ ∅ (IUTchI Def 3.1 (b))
    • the union of possible images is a subset of the packets on which the hull is defined (Rem 3.9.5 (i) requires a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume)

    Conclusion.

    (F) −|log(Θ)| ∈ R, and (I) −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|; the 'i.e.' clause on page 174 is equivalent to (I) only under (F).

    Obligations.

    • Define the set of possible images: the orbit of the image under the action generated by (Ind1) and (Ind2), together with the containments allowed by (Ind3).
    • Define the hull of the union and its log-volume.
    • Prove |log(q)| > 0 from ord_v(q_v) > 0 at bad v and V^bad ≠ ∅.
    • Prove finiteness (F) as its own claim: the compactness of each 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} asserted on page 175, and the support condition of Prop 3.9 (iii) (page 117) for the family of hulls.
    • The comparison is with the hull of the union of the possible images: a single image whose hull dominates the q-pilot region is a sufficient route, not a necessary one (two singleton images of measure 1/4 each jointly have log-volume log(1/2), while each has log(1/4)).

    Ambiguities.

    • Averaging index: the statement (page 173) and Step (x) (page 181) say explicitly that the average is over j ∈ F*_l, so the factor is 1/l* (not displayed); Prop 3.4 (ii) (page 102) and Rem 3.9.3 (page 120) corroborate the labels j ∈ {1, ..., l*}. Pages 153 and 174 index the packets and the sets U, Ū by j ∈ |F_l|; they state no average. Page 183 speaks of a log-volume 'normalized, with respect to j ∈ |F_l|', with no factor; an average over |F_l| would carry 1/(l*+1). How the j = 0 component of a region indexed over |F_l| enters the average over F*_l (dropped, or identified with the diagonal label ⟨F*_l⟩ through △, pages 174 and 181) is not stated.
    • The extracted text of page 174 reads 'V^bad (= ∅)'; the rendered page reads '(≠ ∅)'. This is an extraction artifact, not a discrepancy in the paper.
    • 'possible images' and 'subject to the indeterminacies' are not defined as a set by an explicit formula; whether Ind3 enlarges each image to a containing region or acts as a separate indeterminacy is not stated.

    Pages read: text; rendered and checked: pages 173, 174

    Parts, steps and fragments.

    Step (xii): the global realified Frobenioids appearing in the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link play an important role in the argument of (xi). Since only log-volumes are computed, it might seem possible to dispense with the global Frobenioids and work only with the local Frobenioids at v ∈ V. Key sentences (pages 185 to 186): 'observe that since the isomorphism of [local or global!] Frobenioids arising from the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link only preserves isomorphism classes of objects of these Frobenioids [cf. the discussion of Remark 3.6.2, (i)], to work only with local Frobenioids means that one must contend with the indeterminacy of not knowing whether, for instance, such a local Frobenioid object at some v ∈ V^non corresponds to a given open submodule of the log-shell at v or to, say, the p_v^N-multiple of this submodule, for N ∈ Z. Put another way, one must contend with the indeterminacy arising from the fact that, unlike the case with the global Frobenioids "F^⊛_MOD", "F^{⊛R}_MOD", objects of the various local Frobenioids that arise admit endomorphisms which are not automorphisms.     Explicit hypotheses.

    • v ∈ V^non, N ∈ Z

    Conclusion.

    The global realified Frobenioids cannot be replaced by local Frobenioids: the link preserves only isomorphism classes of objects (Remark 3.6.2 (i)), and local Frobenioid objects admit non-invertible endomorphisms, so an object at v ∈ V^non would not determine whether it corresponds to a given open submodule of the log-shell or to its p_v^N-multiple; this would render the log-volume computation of (xi) meaningless.

    • Prove that objects of the local Frobenioids admit endomorphisms that are not automorphisms, whereas those of F^⊛_MOD, F^{⊛R}_MOD do not (page 185; asserted without argument).

(v) For a canonical smooth proper hyperbolic curve X over the Witt vectors A of a perfect field of characteristic p, with ordinary locus Û and canonical Frobenius lifting Φ, dividing the derivative of Φ by p gives only an inclusion ω_{X_k} ↪ Φ^*ω_{X_k} (square Hasse invariant), hence at the level of global degrees the inequality (1 − p)(2g_X − 2) ≤ 0.

IUT4.ThmATheorem ADiophantine Inequalities
Record

Diophantine inequality for hyperbolic curves: the height of omega_X(D) is bounded, up to a bounded discrepancy, by (1 + epsilon) times the sum of the log-different and the log-conductor on points of bounded degree.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • X a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field
  • D a reduced divisor, U_X = X minus D hyperbolic (deg omega_X(D) > 0)
  • d a positive integer, epsilon a positive real

Implicit hypotheses.

  • heights, log-differents, log-conductors in the sense of [GenEll], Definitions 1.2 and 1.5
  • the relation <~ in the corrected sense of Remark 2.3.1 (ii)

Conclusion.

ht_{omega_X(D)} <~ (1 + epsilon)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on U_X(Qbar)^{<= d}.

Obligations.

  • Theorem A is Corollary 2.3; see that record.
  • The specialization to the abc inequality (X = P^1, D = {0, 1, infinity}, d = 1) is described in docs/PAPER_IV_DERIVATION.md. At the level of statements it is formalized in IUT4.ThmA.frag.equiv_abc: the special case for rational points is equivalent to Challenge.ABC. Not formalized: Theorem A itself, the identification of the height attached to omega_X(D) with Mathlib's logarithmic height, and the direction (ii) implies (i) of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 that the passage from the proof in IUT IV to this special case uses. The bounded degree statement for P^1 minus {0, 1, infinity} implies Challenge.ABC through its degree one piece (IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_abc).
  • Page 3 asserts that the Vojta conjecture for hyperbolic curves, the ABC conjecture and the Szpiro conjecture for elliptic curves all follow as special cases of Theorem A, referring to [Vjt]; these derivations are not given in the paper.
  • In degree one, the compactly bounded form for Sigma empty is equivalent to the abc inequality for triples whose ratios are bounded away from 0 (IUT4.ThmA.frag.cb_degree_one_iff_ratio_bounded, a model test), an auxiliary statement whose relation to Challenge.ABC is not addressed.

Ambiguities.

  • Page 3 and page 54: the statements of Theorem A and Corollary 2.3 agree word for word (checked against both renders), except that Theorem A points to the notation of [GenEll] as recalled before Corollary 2.2.

IUT4.Prop1_1Proposition 1.1Multiple Tensor Products and Differents
Record

Multiple tensor products and differents. For a fixed index * in I and I* = I minus {*}, the normalization (R_I)^~ of the tensor product R_I = tensor over Z_p of the R_i satisfies p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ inside R_I inside (R_I)^~, where d_{I*} is the sum of the orders d_i of the differents over i in I*.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • p a prime number; I a finite set of cardinality >= 2
  • for i in I, k_i a finite extension of Q_p inside an algebraic closure of Q_p, R_i its ring of integers, d_i in Q_{>=0} the order of a generator of the different ideal of R_i over Z_p
  • for nonempty E in I: R_E = tensor product over Z_p of the R_i (i in E), d_E = sum of d_i (i in E)
  • a fixed element * of I, and I* = I minus {*}

Implicit hypotheses.

  • ord is the p-adic valuation normalized by ord(p) = 1; p^lambda denotes an unspecified element of order lambda
  • (-)^~ is the normalization of the reduced ring in its ring of fractions

Conclusion.

p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ is contained in R_I, which is contained in (R_I)^~; the left-hand side is well defined for suitable p^{d_{I*}}, for example products of elements p^{d_i} of R_i (i in I*).

Obligations.

  • For two factors (I = {1, 2}, I* = {2}) the inclusion p^(d_{I*}) (R_I)~ <= R_I is proved, with p^(d_2) any element of order d_2, a generator of the different ideal or any element of it (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.td_order, IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.td_generator, IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.td_different_ideal); the route of page 10 through base change and faithful flatness is not followed. For two factors, K_1 (x) K_2 is proved reduced and a finite product of finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decomposition), the closed unit ball and integral closure models of R_i agree (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models), and R_E <= (R_E)~ is proved with (R_E)~ the integral closure of Z_p in K_1 (x) K_2 (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers). For any finite number of factors the tensor product over Q_p is a finite product of finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.pk_packet_decomposition), under which (R_E)~ is the product of their rings of integers (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.pk_normalization_coordinates). For two factors, this integral closure is the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.ti_normalization). For any finite number of factors, with R_I the image in the tensor product over Q_p of the tensor product over Z_p of the R_i and (R_I)~ the integral closure of Z_p there, the assertions of page 9 are proved: p^(d_{I*}) (R_I)~ <= R_I with p^(d_{I*}) a product of elements of order d_i (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_order) or of elements of the differents (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_different_ideal), R_I <= (R_I)~ (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_trivial_inclusion), the independence of the choice of p^(d_{I*}) (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_choice_independent), and the three together (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_whole), through trace duals over the field k_* rather than the base change and induction of page 10. For any finite number of factors, the tensor product over Z_p of the R_i injects into the tensor product over Q_p with image R_I (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_injective, IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_range), R_I is reduced (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_reduced), its ring of fractions is the tensor product over Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_fraction_ring), and the integral closure of Z_p there is the normalization of R_I in it (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_normalization). On the printed tensor product over Z_p, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.packetId_proposition1_1 states the display of page 9 with p^(d_{I*}) a pure tensor of elements of order d_i (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_whole), and IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.psuit_proposition1_1 states it, with the independence of the choice, for every element of the tensor product over Q_p of order d_{I*} in each field component (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_whole); the page's products are instances (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_examples), such elements exist (IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.psuit_exists_hasOrder), and the setting of subfields of one algebraic closure is an instance (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_closure). psuit_proposition1_1 is the declaration of the whole proposition, compared clause by clause with the render of page 9; its readings are listed in the ambiguities. The route is not that of page 10 (base change and induction on |I|): it goes through trace duals over k_* and the decomposition of the tensor product over Q_p into fields.

Ambiguities.

  • 'Suitable p^(d_{I*})' is read in psuit_proposition1_1 as an element of the tensor product over Q_p of order d_{I*} in every field component, equivalently under every Q_p-algebra map to an algebraic closure of Q_p (IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.psuitHasOrder, IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_components); the page's products of elements p^(d_i) are instances (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_examples). The page writes p^(d_{I*}) as an element of the algebraic closure and gives no action of such an element on (R_I)~; that reading is not formalized. In IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.many_whole and IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_whole the reading is a pure tensor of elements of order d_i, with 1 at *; elements of order d_i exist (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_generator_order).
  • In packetId_proposition1_1 and psuit_proposition1_1 the fields k_i are abstract finite extensions of Q_p, not subfields of a fixed algebraic closure; every subfield of the algebraic closure is such a field (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.suit_closure states the two main clauses in that setting), and R_i, the integral closure of Z_p in k_i, is then the intersection printed on page 9 (that identification is not stated in Lean).
  • d_i is differentOrder at a prime P_i of R_i over p, universally quantified (R_i is local, so P_i is its maximal ideal), and order is read through the spectral norm, p^(-d_i). One generator of the different of that order is shown to exist (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.id_generator_order); generators differ by units of norm one.

    For a commutative Q_p-algebra W and any Q_p-algebra isomorphism e from W onto a finite product of commutative Q_p-algebras A_j, the set (R_E)^~ of elements of W integral over Z_p is the preimage under e of the product of the sets of elements of the A_j integral over Z_p (for fields, their rings of integers); its image under e is that product. It contains 0 and is stable under multiplication by p^k.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • p a prime
    • W a commutative ring with a Q_p-algebra structure
    • J a finite type, A j commutative rings with Q_p-algebra structures
    • e : W = prod_j A_j an isomorphism of Q_p-algebras

    Conclusion.

    packetNormalizationSet p W = e^(-1)(prod_j packetNormalizationSet p (A j)); e(packetNormalizationSet p W) = prod_j packetNormalizationSet p (A j).

    Covers.

    Pages 9 and 13: (R_E)^~ corresponds, under the decomposition of the packet into a direct sum of finite extensions of Q_p, to the product of the rings of integers of the summands.

    Not covered.

    Proposition 1.1's inclusion p^(d_{I*}) (R_I)^~ subset R_I.

    Pages read: rendered and checked: IUT IV pages 9, 10, 13, 14

IUT4.Prop1_3Proposition 1.3Estimates of Differents
Record

Estimates of differents: d_i >= d_0 + (e_{i/0} − 1)/e_i, with equality if tame; and d_i <= d_0 + n_i + 1/e_0 when k_i is Galois over a tame extension of k_0.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Proposition 1.2; k_0 a subfield of k_i containing Q_p, R_0 its ring of integers, d_0 the order of a generator of its different, e_0 its ramification index, e_{i/0} = e_i/e_0, n_i the p-adic valuation of [k_i : k_0]
  • (ii): k_i finite Galois over a subfield k_1 with k_0 in k_1 and k_1 tamely ramified over k_0

Conclusion.

(i) d_i >= d_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/(e_{i/0} e_0) = d_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i, with equality if k_i is tamely ramified over k_0; (ii) d_i <= d_0 + n_i + 1/e_0.

Obligations.

  • prop1_3Full states the notation e_{i/0} = e_i/e_0, the definition of n_i, assertion (i) with the printed rewriting and the tame equality, and assertion (ii) with the printed hypotheses (k_1 between k_0 and k_i, k_i Galois over k_1, k_1 tame over k_0), for finite extensions of Q_p; proved from towerRamificationIdx_eq_mul, towerProp1_3i_ge, towerProp1_3i_eq_of_tame and diffBound_prop1_3ii, with the three standard axioms; checked against the renders of pages 9 to 12.
  • The proofs are not those of page 12: (i) comes from the transitivity of the different and the tame equality, (ii) from the trace of 1 (valid for every finite k_i/k_0); the Galois and tameness hypotheses of (ii) are carried by the statement but not used.
  • Over a general base Q_p <= k_0 <= k_i, the transitivity of the different and of the ramification indices is proved (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_transitivity), the inequality of (i) and its equality in the tame case are proved as two declarations (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_i_ge, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_i_tame_equality), and (ii) is proved when k_i is tame over k_0 and when n_i = 0 (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_ii_tame, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_ii_n_zero). The two clauses of (i) are also proved in one declaration (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_combined). Assertion (ii) is proved for every finite extension k_i/k_0, without the Galois and tameness hypotheses (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.ii_all_finite), and in the form of the page with its hypotheses (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.tower_ii_statement, proved in IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.ii_statement_proved), by a route different from page 12: the bound on the relative different from the trace of 1, not the induction on n_i through Kummer extensions of degree p, which is not formalized. The converse of the tame equality over a general k_0 is not formalized. These fragments are separate declarations; prop1_3Full states (i) and (ii) together. For k_0 = Q_p: the lower bound of (i) is proved for rings of integers of finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_differentOrder_ge, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_differentOrder_ge_tower, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_padic_differentOrder_ge), the prime over p is unique (IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.padicBridge_prime_eq_maximalIdeal), the equality in the tame case, the strict inequality in the wild case and their equivalence are proved (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_tame_equality_padic, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_wild_inequality_padic, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_equality_iff_tame_padic), and (ii) is proved in its base case k_1 = k_i tame over Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.ii_base_padic). These are separate declarations; none states (i) for k_0 = Q_p by itself.
  • Arithmetic steps of the proof are checked in the fragments listed in fragments.

Ambiguities.

  • Readings used by the fragments over a general base: the fields are abstract finite extensions of Q_p with algebra maps, not subfields of a fixed algebraic closure; d is differentOrder (the exponent of the different divided by the ramification index, so ord(p) = 1); tame is read as p not dividing e_{i/0} (finite residue fields); n_i is multiplicity p [k_i : k_0].
  • The fields k_0, k_1, k_i are abstract finite extensions of Q_p with compatible algebra maps and scalar towers (and separate compatible Z_p-algebra structures), not subfields of a fixed algebraic closure.
  • d is differentOrder: the exponent of the prime in the different ideal divided by the ramification index over Z_p, that is, ord of a generator with ord(p) = 1; it is real-valued in Lean (the page has Q>=0).
  • 'Tamely ramified' is read as: p does not divide the relative ramification index (residue fields are finite).
  • The primes over p of each ring of integers are universally quantified; each ring has exactly one, so no choice is made.
  • e_{i/0} is the ramification index of P over P_0; the first conjunct proves it equals e_i/e_0.
  • n_i is multiplicity p [k_i : k_0]; the second conjunct proves it is the unique n with [k_i : k_0]/p^n an integer prime to p.
  • The index set I of Propositions 1.1 and 1.2 plays no role; there is one k_i.
  • k_1 is a parameter of the whole theorem although (i) does not involve it; harmless, since k_1 = k_0 is always available and (i) does not depend on it. In (ii), k_1 is universally quantified, which also gives the reading 'for some such k_1', since the bound does not depend on k_1.
  • 'Finite' in 'finite Galois extension' comes from FiniteDimensional Q_p k_i.

Pages read: renders of pages 9, 10, 11 and 12; the statement compared clause by clause with the renders of pages 11 and 12

    For a finite extension L of Q_p and a prime P of its ring of integers over p with ramification index e: if p does not divide e, the exponent of P in the different (differentExponent Z_p R P) equals e - 1; equivalently differentOrder Z_p R P = (e - 1)/e. Proof: pR = P^e; the trace of R/P^n over F_p is n times the trace of R/P (additivity of the trace along 0 -> R/P -> R/P^(n+1) -> R/P^n -> 0); R/P is separable over the finite field F_p, so some trace is nonzero, and since p does not divide e some element of R has a unit trace in Z_p, which forbids P^e from dividing the different.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • p a prime
    • L a field with a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structure and a compatible Z_p-algebra structure (IsScalarTower Z_p Q_p L)
    • P a prime ideal of R = integralClosure Z_p L lying over the maximal ideal pZ_p
    • p does not divide P.ramificationIdx Z_p

    Conclusion.

    differentExponent Z_p R P = P.ramificationIdx Z_p - 1 (natural numbers); differentOrder Z_p R P = ((e : R) - 1)/e.

    Covers.

    Pages 11 and 12, Proposition 1.3 (i): the equality d_i = d_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i when k_i is tamely ramified over k_0, for k_0 = Q_p.

    Not covered.

    Proposition 1.3 (i) over a general base k_0 (needs the transitivity of the different over R_0 and ramification in towers); Proposition 1.3 (ii).

    Pages read: rendered and checked: pages 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13

    P.ramificationIdx Z_p <= differentExponent Z_p R P; 1 <= differentOrder Z_p R P.

    Record

    For a prime p, a nonzero natural number d and any natural number m: p^m divides d and p does not divide d/p^m if and only if m equals the multiplicity of p in d. So the multiplicity is the unique nonnegative integer n with d/p^n an integer prime to p.

    Explicit hypotheses.

    • p a prime
    • d a nonzero natural number
    • m a natural number

    Conclusion.

    (p^m | d and not p | d/p^m) iff m = multiplicity p d.

    Covers.

    Page 11, the notation of Proposition 1.3: n_i is the unique nonnegative integer such that [k_i : k_0]/p^{n_i} is an integer prime to p; with d = [k_i : k_0] the lemma shows that this integer exists, is unique, and is the multiplicity used for n_i in the library.

    Not covered.

    Assertions (i) and (ii) themselves; they are in IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.prop1_3Full, which uses this lemma with d = Module.finrank K L.

IUT4.Prop1_4Proposition 1.4Nonarchimedean Normalized Log-volume Estimates
Record

Normalized log-volume estimates for p-adic tensor packets: normalization of mu^log, the value of mu^log(log_p(R_i^x)), and upper bounds for the log-volumes of the regions containing phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~).

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of Proposition 1.2; R_i^mu the torsion of R_i^x, p^{f_i} the residue field cardinality, p^{m_i} the order of the p-primary part of R_i^mu
  • (iii): I* a subset of I with p - 2 >= e_i for all i in I minus I*; lambda in (1/e_{i_dagger}) Z, i_dagger in I
  • (iv): p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i in I

Conclusion.

(i) a normalized log-volume mu^log on compact open subsets of finite extensions of Q_p and of their tensor products, with mu^log(R_i) = 0, mu^log(p R_i) = -log p, mu^log((R_E)^~) = 0, mu^log(p (R_E)^~) = -log p; (ii) mu^log(log_p(R_i^x)) = -(1/e_i + m_i/(e_i f_i)) log p; (iii) the inclusions phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I)} log_p(R_I^x) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I) - b_I} (R_I)^~, the bounds mu^log(p^{floor(lambda-d_I-a_I)} log_p(R_I^x)) <= (-lambda + d_I + 1 + 4|I*|/p) log p and mu^log(p^{floor(lambda-d_I-a_I)-b_I} (R_I)^~) <= (-lambda + d_I + 1) log p + sum_{i in I*} {3 + log e_i}, and d_I + a_I >= |I| (p > 2), >= 2|I| (p = 2); (iv) phi((R_I)^~) in (R_I)^~ and mu^log((R_I)^~) = 0.

Obligations.

  • The log-volume of [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7, is not read; mu^log is modeled as log(mu(A)/mu(R))/d for a Haar measure mu (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_def), an interpretation. With it the normalization (i) is proved for one finite extension of Q_p on its ring of integers (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_field_normalization) for tensor packets of two factors on (R_E)~ (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_packet_normalization), and for tensor packets over Q_p of any finite number of factors (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.pk_packet_normalization). The value (ii) is proved for every finite extension of Q_p, with the order of R_i^mu of page 13 (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.uv_ii, IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.uv_card_torsion); the compatibility of the log-volume with log_p of [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7 is replaced by a counting argument inside k_i (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.uv_kernel_count). For two factors, the second inequality of (iii) is proved for every I* (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_iii_second), its first inequality when p > 2 and e_1, e_2 <= p - 2 (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_iii_first) and, through the additivity of page 14 over the two tensor factors (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tadd_additivity), for every I* with e_i <= p - 2 for i not in I*, as printed (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tadd_iii_first), its last sentence (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_dI_aI), and (iv) (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_iv). For any finite number of factors, (i) (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tlsm_i), (iv) (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tlsm_iv), the additivity of page 14 (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tam_A_logLattice) and the first inequality of (iii) for every I* as printed (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tam_iii_first) are proved. Not formalized: the second inequality of (iii) and the inclusions of (iii) for more than two factors, and the injectivity of the tensor product over Z_p of the log_p(R_i^x) into the tensor product over Q_p (the lattices are taken as their images).
  • The arithmetic fragments check the proof starting from supplied volume bounds; the per-index inequality d_i + a_i >= 1 (2 for p = 2) is proved for actual finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.bridge_d_add_a). For two factors the containments of (iii) and (iv) are established (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_iii_second, IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tls_iv); for any finite number of factors the containment of (iv) is established (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.tlsm_iv), and those of (iii) are not.

Ambiguities.

IUT4.Prop1_5Proposition 1.5Archimedean Metric Estimates
Record

Archimedean metric estimates: C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with metrics up to a factor 2; primitive automorphisms preserve decompositions; M_I splits into 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C with metric factor 2^{|I|-1}; tensor products of vectors of length lambda lie in lambda^{|I|} B_I.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • C with its standard Hermitian metric; primitive automorphisms generated by complex conjugation and multiplication by +-1, +-sqrt(-1)
  • (iii), (iv): I, V nonempty finite sets; M = direct sum of copies C_v (v in V); M_I = tensor product over R of copies M_i of M; B_I the product of unit balls
  • (iv): lambda > 0 and m_i in M_i whose components have length lambda

Implicit hypotheses.

  • (i): the isomorphism C tensor_R C -> C + C is any isomorphism of topological rings (one arising from the Chinese remainder theorem); the primitive automorphisms form a group of order 8

Conclusion.

(i) C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with the metrics up to a factor 2; (ii) the decomposition is preserved by primitive automorphisms; (iii) M_I is a direct sum of 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C, with direct sum metric 2^{|I|-1} times the tensor metric, and B_I is preserved; (iv) the tensor product of the m_i lies in lambda^{|I|} B_I.

Obligations.

  • (i) is checked on C (x)_R C with the tensor product inner product (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.i_metric, IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.i_length), and (ii) with the primitive automorphisms (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.primitive_group, IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.primitive_card, IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.ii_preserved). (iii) and (iv) are checked on M_I, the tensor product over R of copies of the functions V -> C, with a tensor product metric defined here (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.tensor_metric): the decomposition into 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C with the factor 2^{|I|-1} (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.iii_decomposition), its uniqueness (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.iii_unique), the integral structure B_I (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.integral_structure) and its preservation (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.iii_preserved), and (iv) (IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.iv). No declaration states (i) to (iv) together, and two points are weaker than the page: the topology of M_I is carried over from the direct sum through one decomposition, so that 'the topological ring structure on each C_v determines a topological ring structure on M_I' is not proved for a topology defined on the tensor product independently of the decomposition; and the metric of (iii) and (iv) is not identified, for two factors, with the tensor product inner product used for (i) and (ii).

Ambiguities.

  • Page 15, (i): 'compatible up to a factor of 2' refers to the metric (the square of the length); the bracket says lengths differ by a factor sqrt(2). The fragment crt_normSq checks the squared-norm form.
  • 'Metric' (page 15) is read as the real inner product Re(z conj w) on C, multiplied on pure tensors of C (x)_R C and summed on C x C; preservation of a complex Hermitian pairing is not claimed.
  • 'Isomorphism of topological rings' (page 15) is read as a continuous ring isomorphism for the topology of the tensor product norm; continuity gives R-linearity.
  • 'Preserves the decomposition' in (ii) is read as preserving the unordered pair of direct summands (each summand onto a summand), with the metric; conjugation on one factor exchanges the two summands, so preservation summand by summand is false.
  • 'Topological ring structure on M_I' (page 15) is read in IUT.PaperIV.Proposition1_5.tmetProp1_5_iii_topological as the topology carried over from the product of copies of C by the decomposition at a chosen index; ring isomorphisms continuous for it are R-linear.

IUT4.Prop1_6Proposition 1.6The Prime Number Theorem
Record

Consequence of the prime number theorem: n <= 4 p_n / (3 log p_n) for n large, and pi(eta) <= 4 eta/(3 log eta) for eta >= eta_prm.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • p_n the n-th smallest prime (p_1 = 2), n a positive integer

Conclusion.

There is n_0 with n <= 4 p_n/(3 log p_n) for all n >= n_0; there is a positive real eta_prm with sum_{p <= eta} 1 <= 4 eta/(3 log eta) for all real eta >= eta_prm.

Obligations.

  • proposition1_6 states both displays with one witness each, proved from Mathlib's Nat.isEquivalent_primeCounting; exists_n0, exists_eta_prm and counting_of_nth (the second display follows formally from the first) are the components.

IUT4.Rem1_7_1Remark 1.7.1
Record

When Proposition 1.7 is used in Theorem 1.10 for packet-normalized log-volumes, the computation uses the normalized log-volumes of Proposition 1.4 (i) instead of the non-normalized log-volumes for which the weights of IUT III Remark 3.1.1 (ii) were computed. Hence the weights [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} must be replaced by [K_v : Q_{v_Q}] [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}], and the normalized weights by prod_{alpha in A} [(F_mod)_{v_alpha} : Q_{v_Q}] divided by the sum over all collections {w_alpha}_{alpha in A} (not necessarily distinct) of elements of V_mod over v_Q of prod_{alpha in A} [(F_mod)_{w_alpha} : Q_{v_Q}]. These are the weights lambda_{Pi e dagger} / sum_{e in E^n} lambda_{Pi e} of Proposition 1.7 with E the places of V (equivalently V_mod) over a fixed v_Q, n = |A| with A = {alpha_1, ..., alpha_n}, lambda_e = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}] > 0 for e corresponding to v, and beta_e a normalized log-volume of a compact open subset of K_v.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • the notation of IUT III Remark 3.1.1 (ii) and Proposition 3.9 (i): V, V_mod, F_mod, K, v_Q in V_Q, a finite index set A
  • normalized log-volumes as in Proposition 1.4 (i)

Implicit hypotheses.

  • the bijection V -> V_mod (underline v to v) restricted to places over a fixed v_Q

Conclusion.

The dictionary for applying Proposition 1.7: E = places over v_Q, n = |A|, lambda_e = [(F_mod)v : Q{v_Q}], beta_e = a normalized log-volume on K_v; the appropriate normalized weights are lambda_{Pi e dagger} / sum_{e in E^n} lambda_{Pi e}.

Obligations.

  • A change of normalization stated without proof; the identity [K_v : Q_{v_Q}] [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} = [(F_mod)v : Q{v_Q}] is the tower law for degrees.

IUT4.Prop1_8Proposition 1.8Torsion Points of Elliptic Curves
Record

Torsion points of elliptic curves over a perfect field k: Serre's criterion; the exact sequence of automorphism groups, the minimal field of definition and models; the 2-torsion representation; uniqueness of models with rational l-torsion; semistable reduction from rational l-torsion; the Legendre form; ramification of torsion fields.

Explicit hypotheses.

  • k a perfect field, kbar an algebraic closure, G_k = Gal(kbar/k)
  • (i): l >= 3 a prime invertible in k, k = kbar, A an abelian variety over k with a polarization lambda
  • (ii): E_kbar an elliptic curve over kbar with origin; n a positive integer
  • (iii): as (ii), with Aut_kbar(E_kbar) = {+-1}
  • (iv): as (ii), l >= 3 a prime invertible in k, E'_k and E''_k models over k with all l-torsion rational over k
  • (v): as (ii), k a complete discrete valuation field with ring of integers O_k, l >= 3 a prime invertible in O_k, E_k a model over k with all l-torsion rational
  • (vi): as (iii), 2 invertible in k, G_E = G_k, and G_E -> Aut(E_kbar[2]) trivial; for the second part k a complete discrete valuation field with 2 invertible in O_k
  • (vii): as (ii), k a complete discrete valuation field, E_k a model over k, n invertible in O_k

Conclusion.

(i) Aut_k(A, lambda) -> Aut(A[l]) is injective; (ii) an exact sequence 1 -> Aut_kbar(E_kbar) -> Aut_k(E_kbar) -> G_k with open image G_E, a representation rho_n on E_kbar[n], k_E = field of definition = k(j), and models over k_H correspond to sections over H; (iii) rho_2 factors through G_E -> Aut(E_kbar[2]); (iv) E'_k is isomorphic to E''_k; (v) E_k has semistable reduction over O_k; (vi) E_kbar descends to E_k over k in Legendre form, which has semistable reduction over O_k' for some k'/k with [k' : k] <= 2, and k' = k is possible if E_k has good reduction over O_k'; (vii) good reduction gives G_k acting unramified on E_kbar[n], and bad multiplicative reduction gives a tamely ramified extension with ramification index dividing n.

Obligations.

  • Needs elliptic curves over local fields, torsion fields and Neron models. Only the Legendre curve y^2 = x(x - 1)(x - t) as a Mathlib WeierstrassCurve, its discriminant and the condition for it to be elliptic are formalized (IUT4.Prop1_8.frag.legendre_curve); the descent of (vi) is not.
